launches.title: Baud - AI Chips for Accelerated Training and Inference
launches.tagline: Novel AI hardware and developer platform, co-designed from first principles to let businesses create frontier models with orders of magnitude better performance than incumbents
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Baud is building a new chip for training and inference of large AI models

We have developed a new arithmetic representation of neural networks that does not contain multiplications. Our silicon is architected specifically for this representation and doing this lets us train and serve AI faster and more efficiently than incumbents.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104577&key=user_uploads/1348413/43bfbd38-2274-4963-b225-3714d18f7c65)

\
\
**Our Team** 

* **Sarang Zambare**, multi-time founder with 4 patents and 7+ years in deep learning and AI hardware. ML lead for Peloton Guide from concept to 100,000+ devices shipped and founding engineer at Caper (acquired by Instacart) building edge deep learning models.
* **Eric Taylor**, ex-NVIDIA chip design veteran with a decade of experience including 4 tape-outs on leading process nodes, two major IP releases, multiple patents and publications, prior roles at NVIDIA, Freescale/NXP, Arteris IP, and Enfabrica.

\
\
**The Problem**

We are living in exciting times where humanity has figured out a way to turn sand and sunlight into machines of scientific discovery.

But creating and serving these machines aka frontier AI models, is extremely capital intensive.

NVIDIA’s publicly documented training recipe of the Nemotron model took **6144 H100 GPUs**, going on for around 3 months, drawing around **4.3 megawatts** of electricity.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104577&key=user_uploads/1348413/eddfed11-11fd-41b3-bbc2-8bb950078002)

That's **$44M in rentals or $245M in capex** plus an ungodly number of developer hours standing up distributed training. Models like Claude Opus 4.6 surprised the world, and that's just the beginning. But at these numbers, **only a handful of teams on Earth control the frontier in AI** and have a shot at a new opus-level moment in other domains like robotics, world models, drug discovery, material science, physics, simulation, the list goes on.\
\
Current attempts at solving this such as Cerebras, Groq, Etched, D-Matrix and 50 other chip startups are only attacking the silicon side and leaving the fundamental math side of the problem untouched, because they are focused on inference and hence have to run existing model weights.

When we looked deeper, we found that if you let go of the constraint of running existing model weights, a radically different silicon architecture becomes possible, with an order of magnitude better performance.

We think we're just scratching the surface of what's possible when you co-design the hardware with the model architecture.

And that’s what we are betting the farm on.

**Solution**

We have developed a new way to represent neural network architectures that eliminates multiplications from both the forward and backward passes, and also compresses the weights by more than 10x without any loss in intelligence. The catch is that you need to train the model in this representation, or start with a base model that is also in this representation.

Both during training and inference, our chip does not need multiplier circuits.

This makes our individual cores drastically smaller and simpler than say GPU’s tensor cores or the PEs in TPU’s systolic arrays.

Which means we can pack way more compute and SRAM on the die and move way more weights for the same memory bandwidth.

This makes our chip faster, less power hungry and simpler to build.\
\
We provide a developer platform based on our hardware that makes creation of frontier AI frictionless and economical to serve, so businesses of all sizes can start owning their intelligence.\
\
**We are live already**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104577&key=user_uploads/1348413/fb27985c-5941-4f2b-aac1-a81378047b7c)

Our first chip is validated on the Global Foundries 12nm process and on schedule for tape-out by the end of this year.\
\
Our training and inference service is already live on a cluster of FPGAs running the chip architecture in emulation.\
\
Using FPGA emulation, we've developed a compiler and a distributed training stack that converts any PyTorch exportable model to our format with bit exact results in most cases, including popular opensource architectures such as GLM, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek, Flux, Wan and others.\
\
You can checkout a small demo of our chip running in emulation on a single FPGA here: <https://baudlabs.ai/demo>

**Our partner program**\
\
Baud is now working with design partners who can test our systems and help smooth out the developer experience, in exchange for reserved capacity on our first cluster for training and inference.\
\
Capacity is limited. Contact us if you are training something new or are tired of paying through the nose for intelligence that you do not own.\
\
<https://baudlabs.ai/partner>

launches.title: Async - Specialized AI agents, that automate costly work for small businesses.
launches.tagline: AI agents that change how small businesses can run
launches.body:
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1pDRqFr9HS9Tlou6LoJb8I9sFyKTJpDbv](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1pDRqFr9HS9Tlou6LoJb8I9sFyKTJpDbv/view?usp=sharing)
\
TLDR: Async builds AI agents that change how real economy small businesses can run. Law firms, healthcare clinics, real estate companies, and childcare facilities hire our AI agents to automate complex work that's never been economical to staff with humans. Every day, our agents complete work from scheduling clinical therapy appointments, to drafting long legal documents, to entering data into legacy practice management systems. We've automated thousands of hours worth of work for small businesses around the country.\
\
**The Problem:**\
Small businesses lack the ability to effectively adopt AI.

* Effective adoption requires rebuilding operating procedures to be agent first, instead of human first. SMB owners generally lack the time and knowledge to do this.
* Out-of-the-box solutions fail to make an outsized impact within complex operations.
* These businesses cannot grow without scaling headcount.

\
**The Solution:**\
We rebuild workflows and deploy AI agents to automate them end-to-end.

* We build a configurable platform that lets us quickly deploy specialized AI agents inside of their business.
* These agents work within our platform and on top of legacy systems.
* The work our agents handle for customers spans everything from drafting real-estate closing documents, to coordinating scheduling for ABA therapy appointments, to handling data entry into legacy legal software systems.

\
**Asks:**

* Introductions to small businesses (especially within law, healthcare, real estate, and childcare) would be greatly appreciated.

name: Induction Labs
long_description:
We are scaling foundation models that are curious about the world.

We’ve seen general intelligence appear exactly once, and its hallmark has been curiosity: a dissatisfaction with what we already know about the world, an ability to learn from world experience, and a disposition to share knowledge with other individuals. Across generations, these human traits have built modern science, technology, and culture.

We think superintelligence will come from models that work the same way: learning from their own observation, updating as they go, growing what they know. These models will start from what humanity knows and discover past us.

We believe that scaling curious intelligence is a defining problem of our time. If solved, we will live to see a new era of technological advances, scientific understanding, and human flourishing.
one_liner: Building intellectually curious AI

launches.title: Induction Labs - foundation models that learn from observation
launches.tagline: Unlocking scalable video pretraining with imagination models
launches.body:
**TL;DR: We're Induction Labs, and today we're announcing research we've been working on: imagination models, a foundation model architecture that unlocks scalable learning from internet video. Our first model, Photon-1, beats a production LLM on internal computer use benchmarks with 30x less training compute, at 3x lower serving cost. \[[Main Article](https://inductionlabs.com/news/scaling-video-pretraining)\]**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107033&key=user_uploads/2757445/94f0365c-7de2-4792-ad4e-a8362f27c233)

Internet video contains millions of hours of people using computers, doing skilled work, and interacting with the world.

Imagination models can scalably learn from this video to get better at completing tasks and understanding the world.

We tested the architecture with Photon-1, a 106B-A5B MoE transformer pretrained on 18 years of computer screen recordings.

**Some Results:**

* **Outperforms a production LLM (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite) on our internal computer use benchmarks**, with 30x less pretraining compute and 3x cheaper inference.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107033&key=user_uploads/2757445/7e217b7a-bbf0-40b0-a160-94855bbf7e90)

* **Simulates full desktop sessions from a single screenshot**: it can imagine VS Code, Gmail, and ChatGPT frame by frame
* **Generalizes beyond computers**: finetuned, it learns checkers and simulates billiard physics better than LLM baselines.
* **Picks up human behavior from video**, like reprompting ChatGPT until it gets what it wants.
* [**Demos here**](https://inductionlabs.com/news/scaling-video-pretraining)

We see imagination models as a path to intelligence that learns by observing the world directly, without a human first translating it into text. 

**Our Ask**

We’re working to scale this method to more kinds of video and looking for exceptional people to work with us! If you’re an exceptional thinker, engineer, or researcher (or know anyone who would be a great fit) - shoot us a message at [team@inductionlabs.com](mailto:team@inductionlabs.com)

name: OS3
long_description:
OS3 is building the platform that makes intelligent robots accessible to every business.

Today, robotics is constrained by two fundamental bottlenecks: hardware is too expensive to deploy at scale, and robots are difficult to train because high-quality robotics data is scarce and costly to collect. 

We built OS3 to solve both.

Our two-person team designed and a US-made mobile humanoid robot for a fraction of the cost of commercial alternatives. On the intelligence side, instead of relying on expensive robot-generated training data, we trained our own video-action model on 150,000 hours of real-world video spanning more than 2,000 tasks. Every deployed robot feeds new experience into our reinforcement learning pipeline, self improving robot fleet over time.

This creates a robot that can be deployed across industries to automate repetitive, physical work without requiring a new robot or training pipeline for every task. Our robots are already deployed in hotels, with customers now expanding the platform into biotech, hospitals, and data centers, including a wet lab at Stanford.

Our mission is to do for robotics what Apple did for personal computing: take technology that was once expensive, specialized, and inaccessible and make it powerful and usable at massive scale. We’re building toward a world with billions of intelligent robots, and OS3 is the platform that makes that possible.
one_liner: Affordable, intelligent humanoid robots built to deploy at scale

launches.title: OS3: Intelligence and Machines for Physical Labor
launches.tagline: Semi-humanoid hardware & Model based on 150k hours of Videos. Preorders Live Now
launches.body:
**TL;DR: OS3 is building semi-humanoid robots for physical labor. Our first robot, H.A.L.E 1.0, is built for everyday human tasks, and our first model is based on 2,000+ distinct real-world tasks and 150,000 hours of video data. We are opening up pre-orders to all with shipments starting this Fall.**

**Physical AI Problem:**

A lot of teams and businesses want to build and deploy in the robotics space. But they have to source parts or buy hardware from different vendors. Furthermore, the recent import ban makes it even harder for beginners and startups to use the latest hardware, unless they are willing to spend tens of thousands of dollars. Post hardware, constant data collection is needed to adapt open or closed-source models to the ever changing hardware choices. In other words, everyone keeps reinventing the same wheel of modern robotics development over and over again. 

**Our solution:**

[**Video Link**](https://youtu.be/dDwaQbZYPLQ)

We built OS3: Both the hardware from ground up and the model to control the hardware. Our first robot, H.A.L.E. 1.0 (Human Aligned Life Enhancing), is designed to handle a wide range of everyday physical tasks, and we are presenting the prototype unit today.

Our goal is towards pushing American robotics forward while ensuring the state of the art is available to all. 

**Hardware and Model:** 

It features a bimanual embodiment with an omni-directional base, full height control to pick up objects directly from the ground while being able to reach top shelves, and a battery that can last a whole work day. Additionally, our design is primarily focused on safety and user-friendliness; a person can start and stop a task at just the touch of a screen on the back of the robot or a mobile app. 

The intelligence layer is a two system architecture, with a high level planner layer and a lower level execution layer. The model has been trained on 150,000 hours of video data spanning over 2,000 real world tasks. Technical report coming soon, once evaluation runs finish. Hardware specs and engineering deep dive posted on our website.  

**Preorders Live now** 

Shipments begin Fall 2026.

Our strong supply chain enables us to make our first low-cost robot starting at just under $10k for businesses to deploy (available in private beta now) and under $15k for developers to experiment with. We are already working with hospitality providers and biotech companies to deploy our robots. 

[**Order Link**](https://os3robotics.com/deploy/)**: 99 dollars deposit fully refundable**

We are also working on our own custom actuators right now, enabling even higher payload for our robots. Happy to discuss more if your business involves such use cases.

**Talk to us:** [hi@os3robotics.com](mailto:hi@os3robotics.com) or book some time [here](https://cal.com/os3robotics/bf?overlayCalendar=true).

name: Evergrove

On average, our customers see a 40% increase in workflow completion, 10x decrease in cycle times, and >60% reduction in cost.

We think voice agents are the starting point for solving slow and fragmented care coordination in this market. Companies that manage an injured worker's care rely on short-staffed contact centres and archaic methods of info exchange: phone, fax, and email. Every delay along the path of care leads to slower rehab of the injured worker, lower throughput for providers, and higher expense for the insurer/employer.

launches.title: Tensr - Robotic Factories that Build Robots from Humanoids to Robots for the International Space Station
launches.tagline: Robotic Factories that Build Robots
launches.body:
Robotic factories building robots. Today we have a 12,000 sqft factory in the Bay Area manufacturing everything from full humanoids to robots for the International Space Station.

Our thesis: Revitalizing domestic manufacturing means driving costs down through automation. We are building an autonomous factory that is able to autonomously process a new order end to end from prototyping to large batch production. That means supply chain management, design for manufacturing, industrial machine retooling, robotic adaptation, quality inspection, packaging, and logistics all automated. Goal: Create a factory that can autonomously go from placed customer order to completed unit scale manufacturing run in 24 hours.

We are currently manufacturing production runs from top labs, full humanoids, and even have a partnership to manufacture robotics for the International Space Station. We've also built supply chain relationships in electronics, actuators, SMT, computing, pneumatics, and raw material suppliers.

A snippet of some of our machines in the factory:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/777065e0-e83d-4501-8799-8c490e883851)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/30775e59-e171-4949-b959-3dc06ffa5322)

## **Manufacturing at the Core**

This isn't just a robotic manipulation company. Its a manufacturing company.

Internally we have pipelines autonomous building large databases of actuators, and raw tracking and trying to predict what items will need to order now to meet our next day targets.

## **The Harness**

The entire factory is a data harness we can "backprop" learnings through from errors in the customer designs, failed supply chain prediction, slow retoolings, to inaccurate robotic manipulation. Our core belief is that robotic machine learning should not rely on human data to scale but instead learn to improve from its own mistakes in the real world in real time. This closes the manufacturing data gap that currently limits large-scale factory automation.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/2baf7c74-80e3-49bb-a6bf-712ce0fb30fc)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/4ed0acb3-e1bc-4210-b4d0-b3f3614bc8da)

## **Any Robot Anywhere**

Our thesis is simple. We should be able to make an robot for any environment whether that be a humanoid for the factory floor or a robot for Low Earth Orbit. We currently have a partnership with the ISS to manufacture a robots for the space station.

NASA Houston, Johnson Space Center

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/e4558cfa-cf98-447a-acaf-7e83650e73a7)

## **Team**

At heart we're a team of Roboticists. Before Tensr we were the leads for a Berkeley lab's autonomous racing team where we raced autonomous full-scale IndyCars at over 160mph as the ML, Sim, and Robotic Controls leads.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112228&key=user_uploads/2763027/c3772faa-f515-4ee0-b32e-2e586b3ae8e3)

We previously worked in industrial automation, aerospace manufacturing, medical device manufacturing, Berkeley AI Research (BAIR), physics simulation, and secured $17M+ in DARPA / industry sponsorship for UC Berkeley / Stanford research.

Our founding engineers range from Berkeley Robotics PhD, ex-NASA, to 10+ years of manufacturing experience.

## A Better World

On a personal note, not only do I believe we have the opportunity to build a great business but also to make a positive impact on the world. Automate away environmentally harmful materials, eliminate waste 0.1% at a time, and drive steady-state COGS toward only the fundamental inputs (materials and electricity), unlocking strong margins while collapsing the price of everyday goods / cost of living.

Lets build a better world :)

A full view of our vision here:[ tensr.com/whitepaper](https://www.tensr.com/whitepaper)

launches.title: Tensr: Building Autonomous Robotic Factories
launches.tagline: Building fully autonomous robotic factories that make scaling hardware as effortless as scaling on AWS
launches.body:
We're building fully autonomous robotics factories at Tensr to create the AWS of manufacturing. Our factories will receive on-demand orders from customers and spin up robots to operate industrial machinery, package, and ship the finished product all in 24 hours.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95506&key=user_uploads/2763027/704a7eb3-1ffc-4fc3-b806-32f3fd256418)

[**https://youtu.be/HLijIfoDfpA**](https://youtu.be/HLijIfoDfpA)

**Problem**

Moving fast in manufacturing today doesn't exist. Iterating designs for manufacturing takes months of back and forth getting samples from China and pre-ordering manufacturing capacity several months before the holiday rush, only then to wait several weeks for shipping praying there isn't a strike at the docks. At the same time we see the complete collapse of America industrial capacity as American workers and experience leave the field and contracts are sent overseas.

**Solution**

With the robotics revolution, for the first time it is possible to fully reimagine the factory floor - moving from rigid lines to modular stations, even in high mix settings. However, we believe that automating manufacturing is more than just deploying a foundation model or a humanoid into an existing factory.

Factories need to be designed from the ground up _around_ robots, not the other way around.

Over the past few weeks we turned our living room into an autonomous factory floor, with stations for CNC, moving stock, and a focus on assembly. After demo day, we'll expand to a full manufacturing facility, and start supporting batch orders of all sizes from other companies throughout the country. Currently we also are in talks to provide our own assembly models to other distributors.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95506&key=user_uploads/2763027/706f70f4-47a7-4466-8281-5cf6d081da43)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95506&key=user_uploads/2763027/e6420b31-3e74-49d3-b751-c901c5379665)

**Team**

We're a battle-hardened team of UC Berkeley graduate robotics researchers (from Berkeley AI Research (BAIR)) who met in a lab, previously worked on and managed multiple DARPA contracts and led an autonomous IndyCar team where we raced full scale autonomous Indycars at 160mph (250kmh) as the Machine Learning, Simulation/Team Manager, and Robotics Control leads respectively.

\- [Eric Berndt](https://x.com/ekberndt) - MS/BS EE/CS, UC Berkeley, CoFounder + CEO

\- [Adith Sundram](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adithsundram/) - MS/BS ME, UC Berkeley, CoFounder + CTO

\- [C.K. Wolfe](https://x.com/ckwolfeofficial) - Current PhD AI/Robotics, UC Berkeley, CoFounder

In addition, our team brings direct operational experience from Rockwell Automation (industrial automation), aerospace manufacturing, and FDA-regulated medical-device production

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95506&key=user_uploads/2763027/f907544d-cb70-45d2-b043-708a6739e40c)

**Our Ask**

We're offering early manufacturing / prototyping pilots for hardware companies of all sizes as the new year starts and we open our first facility. If you or anyone you know fits in this bucket, reach out to [**founders@tensr.com**](mailto:founders@tensr.com)!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112046&key=user_uploads/132378/fc76c836-d166-4caf-b46c-fc2f85ddb653)

Hello friends!!

Did you know that it is harder to build a **50 state SUD outpatient program that takes medicaid**, than it is to put rockets into space?

The licensing requirements once you start treating substances as a primary diagnosis are quite frankly insane, state-level medicaid approval, county level MCO contracts, physical facilities in every state.

But we started Sunflower to solve **hard problems**.

Most people look at us and think “hehe, a mobile app, a sobriety counter”. When we raised our pre-seed with no product and no revenue I told our early investors that this is my version of going to mars. Sunflower isn’t here to just build a sobriety counter. **We are trying to literally and objectively end addiction.**

We’re on a mission to create one TRILLION days of sobriety, one day at a time.

So far we have powered over 21,500,000 days.

We built the first AI Sponsor, named Sam, who has now had over **7,000,000 messages** with our users. More messages than any “entity” has ever had within a single lifetime about sobriety.

Sam is a critical piece to the sobriety journey. Almost 80% of surveyed users at d60 report Sunflower preventing at least one relapse, and **93.6% report a reduction in substance usage**.

But we’ve always known that an AI Sponsor is only a PART of what people need to get sober. They still need **therapy**. They still need **medication**.

The problem?

When you are struggling with substance abuse (alcohol or otherwise), you often don’t have $10 in your bank account to pay for gas.

We have too many users that downloaded Sunflower because **they can’t afford paying $125/hr for therapy**. That can’t afford dropping $350 a quarter for Naltrexone.

Outpatient programs for SUDs are one of the most regulated spaces within behavioral health, and because of this, access to care that _will actually take our users insurance_ (medicaid) is extremely limited.

This is why we are working to build the **Sunflower Clinic of Addiction Medicine**.

A 50 state telemedicine program for SUDs that _actually_ takes medicaid. Now live in MI & PA with SUD facility licensing, state medicaid approval, and in the final steps of county level MCO contracting.

We are combining our best in class AI Sponsor with Mayo Clinic MDs and therapy leadership that built group programs at Charlie Health from 8 - 300+ therapists … our goal is to build the **best outpatient program on the face of this planet** & get it covered by medicaid nationwide.

So far we have over **37,500+ patients on a waitlist** who have requested Therapy or Medication from Sunflower, representing a TAM of $153M waiting to be served.

We are going to solve one of the most important problems in human existence. A problem that globally we spend over $100B treating every year, and is the greatest shackle to the acceleration of humanity.

**Thanks for following along with our story.** Here’s some data. 🌻

launches.title: Frontier Computing – Growing biological brains at scale
launches.tagline: We colocate memory with compute in biological tissue, so you can train larger models at lower cost
launches.body:
TL;DR – We're deploying exascale biocomputing clusters, growing biological systems with memory baked into compute at the substrate level, enabling training of models at parameter counts that would otherwise be inaccessible under traditional GPU architecture-constrained approaches.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112791&key=user_uploads/2627752/445c283b-feb2-4b6b-9d2c-ab2cf60edc7d)

Hey all, we're Frontier Computing, and we’re excited to announce that we are growing the first large-scale neuronal tissues for ML training and inference!

Frontier is launching its 500M biological neurone cluster by January 2027, which will be 2500x larger than the next-largest publicly available system in the biocomputing space that companies are currently restricted to building on. \
\
We'll continue to launch increasingly larger iterations of our substrate to circumvent the challenges of GPU parallelisation seen in roofline analysis across computation/computation/memory, colocating memory with compute in biological neurones to circumvent the infra problem of GPU networking for model training and inference, enabling inference time training at scale on biocompute, at much lower cost than traditional GPU approaches.

# **❌** The Problem

Biological brain tissue is already being bought and sold, including being trained for a range of tasks from gaming environments to next-token prediction, but the scaling limits of the underlying wetware have acted a fundamental barrier to useful economic output.

Academia has previously been unable to exceed a \~1M neurone scale due to "the vascularisation problem", where neurones cannot grow past a geometric limit imposed by insufficient oxygen access in cells that are increasingly far away from active supply.

# **✨** Our solution

Frontier has developed a novel neuronal tissue culture approach to engineer large-scale brain systems that exceed traditional scaling limits of neuronal tissue culture.

This enables us to scale past traditional wetware substrate sizes, supporting much larger biological neural nets with correspondingly greater parameter counts, increasing the complexity of task environments these systems can represent, and using their larger geometric size to provide physically larger surfaces for I/O and informationally rich encode and decode.

We provide the substrate, interfacing and cloud infrastructure to enable third parties to train on our systems, taking advantage of the inference-time training capacities of biological neurones, the sample efficiency, the capacity to exist in an abstraction layer above backprop, and the opportunity to perform RL on models in excess of sizes that would be traditionally accessible on GPU hardware due to memory bandwidth issues that we circumvent through colocating memory and compute within neuronal tissues.

## **🏆** What we've achieved so far

\- We have proven out the first scalable culture system for biocompute, and demonstrated its computational capacities by training our system to play the arcade game Frogger

\- Demonstrated tail-end capabilities in sample efficiency, with 1 hour of real-time learning producing 92% peak cross rate (over a 25-game sample) in our Frogger environment

\- Raised a 10M pre-seed round to produce early scale up our team and wetlab work, led by General Catalyst with participation from LocalGlobe, Amino Collective, Kaya, Long Journey Ventures, Off Piste Capital, SVA and more angels and firms that we are very excited to have on board

\- Begun build out of a 100M and a 500M biological neurone system, live EOY 2026

## **🔜** What's next

\- Demonstrating SOTA task performance of biohybrid models using our larger-scale substrates

\- Launching our API library to enable our customers to implement their own models and RL environments via our platform

\- Iterating towards post-neocortex-scale build outs to further enhance computational capacities of biocompute

## **👥** Our Team

[Michael](https://www.linkedin.com/in/michael-domarkas/), CEO, is a Cambridge Natural Scientist who first learnt programming at 8 through C# Unity game development, competed in maths/chess/bio competitions nationally throughout high school, and has been culturing neuronal tissues for the past two years, starting from $20K USD in grant funding at 17 from Emergent Ventures. He has built the first scalable neuronal culture platform for biocomputation and validated performance via reinforcement learning on this substrate.

## **🙏** Asks

Join the team! We're hiring across the stack for neurobiologists, RL researchers, electrical engineers, and biochemists, accepting both direct applications and referrals. Feel free to get in touch at the link below:

<https://frontier.site/careers>

If you're interested in working at the _frontier_ of biocomputing and scaling the fundamental wetware primitives humanity has access to, Frontier Computing is building out the leading platform in the space. We’re looking forward to collaborating with you.

launches.title: Waddle Labs - Agents that control robots
launches.tagline: Claude Code for robotics - prompt your robot to do physical tasks
launches.body:
Waddle is the Claude Code for robotics. Connect our API to your robot and type a prompt, then our agents write code to achieve the task in \~20 minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107821&key=user_uploads/2132817/afc74f28-33c6-450c-80c3-7f2d263f213d)

### **Our Hypothesis**

Robot intelligence today depends either on large end-to-end VLAs or classical approaches.

\- VLAs are difficult to customise and steer, require huge amounts of data to train, and don’t yet generalise across embodiments and environment. They face limited deployment.

\- Meanwhile, classical approaches are widely deployed for their reliability and explicit control, but are often brittle and costly to redevelop in new setups.

_Does this tradeoff have to be inevitable?_

**Our hypothesis:** By using agents to control robots, we combine the generalisation of VLAs with the speed and reliability of classical approaches. 

### **Our Solution**

Our agents decomposes a goal into subtasks, and completes each subtask by viewing camera feeds, writing control code, and calling models like VLAs. The agent outputs a program that you can run and iterate on by talking to our agents. 

**Where we've been using Waddle internally:**

\- **Create a working policy in 20 minutes** ("Write a program to package the box")

\- **Generate data for model training** ("Pick and place lego bricks at random positions 1000 times")

\- **Facilitate robotics auto-research** ("I am tuning a policy overnight. Reset the scene after each trial”)\
\
Because our agents are LLMs, they inherit properties of the underlying models. Agents and the code they write are inherently generalist, so they work with any robot and any environment without additional data. Moreover, agents excel at long-horizon planning and can decompose a physical goal into subtasks, verify each stage, and re-plan on failure.

**Interested in trying our agents via our preview API?** Sign up at \[our website\](<https://www.waddlelabs.ai/>) or email [founders@waddlelabs.ai](mailto:founders@waddlelabs.ai)

### **Our Research**

Waddle's agents enable new forms of scaling that we are very excited about:

\- **Scaling compositional generalization:** Our agent first wrote the “fold_grasp” skill while flipping a package; another agent later used it to fold a t-shirt. Over time, agents accumulate a library of skills, enabling future agents to compose them and achieve harder tasks.

\- **Scaling multi-robot cooperation:** Imagine an entire fleet of robots collaborating to achieve a task. For VLAs, this is a nightmare. For Waddle, simply hook up more agents. A master agent spawns subagents, coordinating multiple robots working concurrently.

\- **Scaling from scale:** We evaluated Opus 4.8, Fable 5, and GPT 5.6 Sol on a suite of manipulation tasks: larger models with larger thinking budgets consistently produce better policies. As foundation models improve, so do our robots.

### **The Team**

We are @Yiding Song (Vincent) and @Hanming Ye. We met at MIT’s Research Science Institute, where Vincent was working on multimodal astrophysics models and Hanming was researching topology in the math department. Since then, we’ve become roommates at Harvard where we are either doing ML research or breaking robots - usually both.

There will be millions of robots in the future. Our mission is to enable everyone to take part in building them.

launches.title: OneTriangle - The fastest, cheapest inference, powered by KV cache transfer
launches.tagline: Lightweight novel inference
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** OneTriangle is building the cheapest, fastest inference. We cut inference prefill costs by 20% and time-to-first-token by 40%, letting you get large-model quality at small-model cost.

Video: <https://youtu.be/HKe2EZUdNHo>

**Team**

We’re Hannah (CEO) and Medha (CTO), MIT CSAIL grads building with a team of 4 MIT engineers spanning ex-DeepMind and Jane Street, Physics and Astronomy Olympiad medalists, and NeurIPS/ICML authors. 

**The Problem**

Inference is expensive. 

• You’re forced into a bad tradeoff. You need the decoding power of large models, but you have the budget for small ones.

• Prefill is the hidden tax. For long-context and agentic workloads, prefill dominates cost and latency, and everyone just eats it.

**Our Solution**

OneTriangle transfers the KV cache between models, something that has never been done in production. We prefill on a small model, strip the positional encoding, map the cache into the large model’s space, and restore relative importances. The result:

• 20% lower prefill costs

• 40% faster TTFT

• Large-model quality at small-model cost

We beat out NVIDIA’s KV cache transfer paper by getting a lower KL divergence score in 2 weeks.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111487&key=user_uploads/2573695/e64727d6-a7b1-404a-bfbb-22ad2b941142)

\
No API changes, no quality cliff, and we’re upstreaming it into vLLM so the fastest path to cheap inference is the infrastructure you already run.

**Why Now**

Inference has surpassed training as AI’s largest compute cost, and it’s accelerating with demand for agents that generate 10x the tokens a chat session does. Inference already eats up to 90% of total compute cost, over $600 billion is going into AI data centers this year alone. Every team pushing the frontier is bottlenecked by the same thing: serving costs.

\
**The Future**

Our bet is that model-mixing becomes the default serving pattern: small models handle prefill and routine tokens, large models handle the hard ones, and the cache moves freely between them. Whoever owns the transfer layer owns the economics of inference. We are the future of lightweight, fast inference.

launches.body:
Hey YC, we're [Rishab Jain](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rishab-jain-k/) and [Aditya Jain, MD](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adityajain2000/). 

Today, we’re announcing Prescience 🔮: health insurance for the age of abundant intelligence. Prescience is taking on United, Blue Cross, and every other incumbent to build the first health insurance company that doesn’t suck.

**TL;DR -** Prescience is a health insurance solution built for a world with AGI. We help cut premiums by 20%, offer $0 deductibles, include GLP-1s and other modern medicines, and have no hidden fees: we’re only paid when we save you money. We’re already helping some of America’s most ambitious companies save money, provide better benefits, and keep employees healthy so they can focus on their business. [www.getprescience.com](http://www.getprescience.com)

[youtube.com/watch?v=PBqyj9zP4BY&feature=youtu.be](http://youtube.com/watch?v=PBqyj9zP4BY&feature=youtu.be)

**The Problem**

Healthcare is a $6 trillion industry in America. For most companies it's the second-highest line item on their P&L, with costs rising about 15% every single year.

Employers keep paying more and getting less. Deductibles climb and the best benefits get cut. Even employees with "good" insurance still end up with denied claims, surprise bills, and debt.

Nothing changes because the entire industry is built to take a cut of your premium. When care gets more expensive, all of the middlemen make more money. They couldn’t care less if your people get more healthy.

**Our Solution**

Prescience is an AI-native health insurance that flips the incentive. Get a quote without speaking to middlemen, and get better health benefits at lower cost. That adds up to roughly **20% lower premiums**, and **better-than-platinum health benefits** like $0 deductibles, no middlemen, no fees. For YC companies, we have a Deal running with Free Wearables and GLP-1s covered.

Here's how we deliver. **Time Machine** is our reinforcement learning system trained on medical histories. The same way AlphaGo found "Move 37," a move no human would have played that turned out to be brilliant, Time Machine searches millions of possible health trajectories for each member and finds the non-obvious path that keeps them healthiest. Then it steers care toward that path: the right screening at the right moment, the right behavior, before a small issue ever becomes a hospital bill. We’re running a separate waitlist for YC companies who want to try Time Machine for personal use: <http://getprescience.com/time-machine-waitlist>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106632&key=user_uploads/3202469/9ec81a8e-0484-4a24-873c-9aafa87d8124)

Time Machine is paired with **Crystal**: our care navigation assistant in your pocket. As an MD, I’ve seen how patients struggle to manage the labyrinth of healthcare. Hours of phone calls and wait times. Pouring through confusion insurance documents. No more - Crystal can book visits for you, answer questions about your health, and pay your bills.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106632&key=user_uploads/3202469/6d96fb46-38d8-4b14-934d-c070c77b13b4)

Instead of today’s health insurance experience that forces employers to talk to brokers for weeks just to get covered, employers on Prescience get a quote in days and a plan that automatically tracks savings and does filings. We don’t just sit around and collect money from premiums, but actually try to make your employees healthy.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106632&key=user_uploads/3202469/869b2f99-6114-43c4-b8a3-4630545de430)

We are a real, full-stack solution. We’ve built out and partnered to deliver quotes, banking, HSA, MSO-PC, legal, compliance, network, risk, and any other solutions, We have a national team of top doctors who we negotiate with directly - no middlemen - and who we are able to offer fast payment, clear patient histories, and no admin paperwork. They in turn offer us heavy discounts we pass on to employers.

**The Team**

Rishab and Aditya are brothers and serial entrepreneurs. Rishab (CEO) studied CS & Neuro at Harvard, is an RSI alumni, won the International Science and Engineering Fair, and previously founded and exited an edtech company. Aditya (President/COO) earned his MD from Harvard Medical School, has been doing ML research since 2014, and is an Op-Med Fellow at Doximity.

Prescience aims to rebuild the entire $6T American healthcare industry into one that is proactive and prescient, not reactive. Our vision is to be both payer and provider, as our proprietary AI and data becomes ready to take on all of medicine.

Reach us anytime at [founders@getprescience.com](mailto:founders@getprescience.com).

**Our Ask**

1. **If you’re a founder, get your quote:** at [getprescience.com](http://getprescience.com) and **use our YC deal on Bookface**! Free GLP-1 weight loss program, genetic testing, and white-glove support.
2. **Intro us to enterprise:** Founders, Chief People Officers, Benefits Managers, Chief Medical Officers, CFOs, HRIS Platforms, or Brokers, especially at companies reviewing 2027 benefits!

Hi everyone 👋\
We're [Naveen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/naveen-qureshi) & [Frederik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/frederik-vanhevel/), fintech founders and operators building [Rapidfolio](https://rapidfolio.com/).\

\
**Video:**\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0UBIfRhNh08>

\

**If you are a founder or operator at a fintech** **or bank** **who**\
i) has a pressing need to automate manual tasks due to high volume and/or,\
ii) needs to decrease the amount you spend annually on back-office staff or\

**The Problem** 

Fintechs and banks spend up to **30% of their revenue** on operations, compliance, risk and fraud back-office staff. The back-office performs manual processes like KYC and KYB reviews, OFAC/sanctions/watchlist reviews, fraud investigations, disputes and chargebacks, mortgage and loan underwriting, and sometimes even manual data input workflows, among others. The back-office scales as a function of the number of accounts held at the fintech/bank and quickly becomes extremely costly, time consuming, and error prone. 

Frederik and I lived this problem firsthand. **We started Rapidfolio because we wished it existed when we were running Sable (S19)!**

**Our Solution** 

Rapidfolio turns manual compliance, operations, risk and fraud processes into accurate, auditable, and automated flows. We’re running at **100% accuracy** in production. We provide the **end to end platform and services** to:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106986&key=user_uploads/334623/8df4940f-c6ec-41e1-a6a5-4ccd6476667b)

**2.** We generate dozens of **test cases**, including edge cases, and fully test the workflow.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106986&key=user_uploads/334623/940aa8f9-9728-47ef-9a5c-81648c0b28b8)

> **TLDR:** Create an API sandbox with the environments your CI, tests, and evals need. Your coding agent can start the API sandboxes (e.g Linear, Slack, Datadog), run tests, and inspect state changes. Ask your agent about archal.ai!

Hi everyone, I'm Aidan, the founder of Archal. I previously built agent environments at Scale AI and I've been an avid developer for most of my life, which led me to the problem Archal poses to solve.

[https:/youtu.be/pUfu1RFDYVk](https://youtu.be/pUfu1RFDYVk)

**What we found**

Coding agents are getting much better at writing integrations, but testing those integrations is still painful. Many providers do not offer a usable sandbox, so developers fall back to throwaway accounts, shared test workspaces, or thin mocks. Those options are difficult to reset and make it hard to know whether an agent actually completed a task or only returned a plausible response.

As Adam Bender at Google put it, “But with 10x more code and 10x more services, integration tests are going to become the most important part of your quality strategy.” (Google, Software engineering is at the tipping point)

**How Archal works**

With all of this in mind, I built Archal for a starting point of how the next generation of devs will do QA. It's a tool focused on giving agent developers and integration engineers API sandboxes of the SaaS platforms they use in prod pipelines. With Archal, a developer or their coding agent can start a sandbox, run the task, inspect what changed, and reset everything for the next test. We eliminate the need of separate test accounts, thin mocks and stubs, as well as overburdening rate limits on provider-owned sandboxes.

**Our ask**

We're giving out $20 in Archal credits to each new developer that signs up and starts a sandbox. We’d love for you to give it a try and give us feedback, cheers to making testing easier in the era of coding agents!

name: Datoric
long_description:
Datoric develops custom datasets for voice models, robotics, and world models, treating research, collection, verification, and production as one continuous process. We work closely with frontier model teams to turn emerging limitations and model failures into testable data hypotheses, while running our own experiments ahead of customer demand. This allows us to operationalize validated methods into repeatable collection systems at scale.

Data is collected through private invite-only applications separated by modality, customer, and trust level. Every submission remains linked to the contributor, device, task, session, consent, rights, and processing history that produced it, giving our internal QA and fraud models the context to detect problems that may appear legitimate in the finished file. Each collection reveals new failure cases and quality signals that improve the systems behind the next dataset.

Once a collection method is validated, we scale it up as a solution to the model failure and it also becomes a reusable data recipe for future custom projects or independently collected, rights-cleared data products.
one_liner: The secure training data R&D engine for physical AI

launches.tagline: Collecting the human experience AI needs, securely.
launches.body:
Datoric provides custom, security-first training data for voice models, robotics, and world models. Our private, project-specific contributor systems have led to a dramatic improvement in quality for customers and helped us generate nearly seven figures in revenue over the last 30 days.

## **Our background**

In 2023, we built large-scale automations that completed paid LLM training tasks across major crowd-work platforms by bypassing QA testers. We earned six figures in three months, and even helped fix some of the vulnerabilities that we found. From this experience, we learned just how easily training data can be compromised, and how it can lead to unsafe model behavior.

<https://youtu.be/GXuyd2PfsAY>

## **The problem**

Labs are searching for the high-quality, authentic human data their models need, but quality and provenance become harder to control at scale, especially when relying on outside data providers. Poor-quality or compromised data can distort model behavior, while unqualified contributors, automated submissions, unclear instructions, and weak consent records can still slip through QA. At the same time, data providers hold concentrated stores of customer data, contributor identities, and payments that attract fraud and security threats.

## **What we built**

Datoric manages the full collection process for multilingual speech, egocentric video, and action-conditioned data. We collect this data through more than 300,000 active contributors who record conversations, everyday tasks, and other project-specific activities through our private apps. Because Datoric has no public marketplace or open upload system, every collection can run inside its own isolated environment, keeping customer projects separate and limiting unauthorized access. Each recording also remains linked to the verified contributor who created it and the consent they provided. This blocks automated or manipulated submissions and protects quality throughout the collection process rather than leaving it to final QA.

## **Traction**

We’ve seen a major uptick in quality compared to other providers, and in the last 30 days, Datoric has generated nearly seven figures in revenue.

## **Our ask**

We would love introductions to teams building voice models, robots, or world models that need difficult, custom human-generated data.

Send us your hardest collection specification at [**founders@datoric.com**](mailto:founders@datoric.com), or visit [**datoric.com**](http://datoric.com).

launches.title: Libra Robotics: Robots That Build Solar Farms Together

launches.body:
**002C:** “002A, 5.3 mm left.”

**002B:** “002A, you’re running low. Next pallet is on the way.”

**002C:** “Am I clear to come in?”

**002A:** “Aligned. Panel released. You’re clear.”

**002C:** “Fastening.”

**002B:** “Next load arriving now.”

This isn’t a human crew talking.

**It’s three robots building a solar farm together.**

**TL;DR: Libra Robotics is building robotic crews for utility-scale solar. Most robots automate a task; Libra automates the installation workflow. Our specialized robots work together to transport modules, pick and place them, align them with millimeter-level precision, fasten them, and inspect the result.**

We believe the right unit of automation for solar isn’t a single robot - it’s the crew. Utility-scale solar module installation is highly repetitive but deeply interconnected: every module has to be staged, transported, picked, positioned, aligned, fastened, and inspected, repeated across millions of modules on a single project. Automating only one of those steps still leaves people and equipment coordinating everything around it.

So we built a robotic crew. LIBRA-002A picks, aligns, and places modules; LIBRA-002B autonomously stages and transports them; and LIBRA-002C follows behind to fasten them. The robots communicate continuously, share task state, coordinate handoffs, and assist one another to keep the installation workflow moving as one system.

In just 10 weeks, Libra has secured **20+ MW of planned deployments**, **7+ GW of customer LOIs (\~$56M in potential deployment value)**, and is **fully booked for pilots through March 2027**. Demand already exceeds the capacity of our current robot fleet, so we’re building more robots for upcoming deployments.

**▶ Watch how it works:** <https://youtu.be/GGWhvq3RGRU>

# 

### **Why Solar**

Utility-scale solar is one of the clearest places to start.

Contractors already face persistent labor shortages, just as electricity demand is accelerating from data centers, AI infrastructure, and new industrial loads. Global **data center electricity demand** alone is expected to nearly double by 2030, adding roughly **465 TWh of annual demand**. Nearly half of that growth is expected to be met by renewable energy, with solar playing a major role.

A single project can stretch across hundreds of acres and require crews to install millions of modules, often in remote environments and 100°F+ heat.

But installing a solar module isn’t one task. It’s a sequence: **stage → transport → pick → place → align → fasten → inspect.** Each step depends on the one before it.

That makes solar particularly well suited for a coordinated robotic crew.

### **Why a Crew**

Most construction robots automate a single task. But solar farms are built by crews because the work itself is interconnected: if transportation falls behind, installation stops; if placement is inaccurate, fastening stops; and if one machine operates faster than the rest of the workflow, it simply creates another bottleneck.

**Our approach is to optimize the crew, not just the individual robot.** Specialized robots can coordinate around the workflow, rebalance work when one part falls behind, and scale throughput by adding additional robots where they are needed.

This also avoids trying to build one giant machine that does everything. Each robot can remain relatively specialized while the capabilities of the crew expand over time.

### **What We Built**

**We built a coordinated robotic system for utility-scale solar installation.** LIBRA-002A picks modules from the staging area, positions them on the structure, and performs millimeter-level alignment. LIBRA-002B autonomously transports and stages modules to keep installation moving. LIBRA-002C follows behind to fasten each module in place.

The robots operate as one system. They continuously share task state, coordinate handoffs, and communicate when each step is complete. The system knows when a module is arriving, when placement and alignment are finished, and when the fastening robot is clear to move in.

The architecture is designed to scale with the jobsite. More transportation, installation, or fastening robots can be added as throughput requirements increase, while new capabilities can be introduced without redesigning the entire system. Over time, this also enables 24/7 continuous operation, with robotic crews keeping material and installation work moving through the night.

We deliver the system through **Robot-as-a-Service**. Libra provides the robotic crew, deployment, supervision, and maintenance. Contractors don’t purchase robots or take on upfront robotics CapEx - they simply pay for the work performed.

## 

### **Where We Are**

In just 10 weeks:

* Evolved from **LIBRA-001A**, our first installation robot, into the **002-series - a coordinated three-robot crew** for transportation, installation, and fastening
* Deployed our robots on **real commercial utility-scale solar jobsites** in California.
* **Demonstrated the system live** to **50+ leading EPCs and solar developers.**
* Secured **20+ MW of planned deployments**
* Secured **7+ GW of customer LOIs (\~$56M in potential deployment value)**
* Built a pilot calendar **fully booked through March 2027 (5+ projects)**
* Customer demand now exceeds the capacity of our current robot fleet

### **Where This Goes**

Our near-term north star is simple:

**You go to bed, and by the time you wake up, the solar farm is built.**

We’re starting with solar, and that’s where we’re focused today: building robotic crews that can eventually transport, install, fasten, and inspect modules continuously, day and night.

Over time, the same capabilities - mobility, material handling, manipulation, fastening, inspection, and coordination - can extend to other construction and infrastructure workflows.

Our long-term vision is to deploy robotic crews anywhere in the world, making critical infrastructure possible in places that are too remote, dangerous, labor-constrained, or uneconomical to develop today.

**We want a future where robotic crews can turn deserts into oases.**

### **About Us**

**We’ve spent years building robots for the real world and studying how to make them actually work in construction.**

**Jermaine Zhao** built **three generations of autonomous agricultural robots from scratch** and deployed them on commercial farms, working end-to-end across mechanical design, electronics, perception, communication, controls, and autonomy. He trained across mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, and computer science at Stanford.

**Yaojing Huang** defended her Stanford PhD in **Construction Robotics**, with a background in **Civil Engineering and Computer Science**. Her dissertation focused on enabling a **shared robotic platform** and **reusable construction skills** to **generalize across multiple construction tasks** and jobsite scenarios. She conducted research at Stanford’s **Center for Integrated Facility Engineering** and the **Stanford Robotics Center**, helped teach Stanford’s **Construction Robotics** course, and has worked with **40+ contractors and construction robotics companies worldwide**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111169&key=user_uploads/3178817/a9f7150d-3b49-4a0f-8659-cbf1a26eab42)

### **How Can You Help**

If you’re a **utility-scale solar EPC or developer**, send us your next project. We’ll do a robotic-crew feasibility assessment and show you where Libra can automate the workflow.

If you’re a roboticist, construction innovator, or builder who wants to bring robots into the real world of construction, come build with us.

**Jermaine Zhao: [jermaine@librabots.com](mailto:jermaine@librabots.com). Cell: 650-546-9548**

**Yaojing Huang: [yjh@librabots.com](mailto:yjh@librabots.com)**

launches.title: Meteoric — Drones that clear clouds over solar farms and ultimately weaken hurricanes
launches.tagline: Meteoric is building drones that reduce the reflectivity of clouds above solar farms and ultimately reduce the intensity of severe storms and hurricanes.
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111583&key=user_uploads/2005935/6f49c082-1391-4bb6-939f-8f92d0dee7a0)

**TL;DR:** Meteoric is building drones that fly into clouds and reduce their reflectivity without spraying any chemicals. We're starting with clearing overcast clouds above utility-scale solar farms to increase their annual generation by 10–30% with no new infrastructure. Our long-term goal is to scale this system to weaken severe storms and hurricanes. First large-scale cloud clearing flight in 2027 and first storm flight in 2028.

Hey everyone! We’re [Mete](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mete-karslioglu) and [Eric](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eric-nilsson-2b3775254), and we’re building drones to engineer clouds.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111583&key=user_uploads/2005935/5c79de40-e828-4e83-aff5-e1ae0feb3dc4)

⚡ **Starting with solar**

AI has created an enormous demand for power, and solar is scaling exponentially. [US utility-scale solar capacity is set to double by 2030](https://cleanpower.org/resources/market-pulse-utility-scale-solar-summer-2026), and [the world will add 2+ TW](https://www.iea.org/reports/renewables-2025/renewable-electricity) over the same period.

But building new capacity is getting harder and less profitable. Only [\~14% of US utility-scale solar projects](https://emp.lbl.gov/queues) actually get built and [773 GW is already waiting in interconnection queues](https://emp.lbl.gov/queues). 

At the same time, generation costs are rising as tax credits are overhauled and tariffs increase material prices. This makes each additional MWh generated from an existing plant more valuable.

[Low and mid-level overcast clouds cut incoming sunlight by 73–82%](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0038092X80903916) while they’re overhead. We recover that without building new infrastructure. 

🌤 **What we're building**

Fleets of 10s-100s of autonomous drones that fly into low and mid-altitude clouds (1–5 km) over a solar farm and alter the water droplets that form them without using any chemicals. This reduces their reflectivity and brings back measurable amounts of sunlight to the panels below.

Our cloud-loss model shows that this process can increase annual generation from existing assets by 10–30% across major US grid regions, worth \~$5,000–28,000/MW, without building any new infrastructure.

⚙️ **Traction**

* Built a working prototype that dissipated an artificial cloud by 13% in cloud-chamber tests
* Built a cloud-loss model that quantifies how much generation a given US solar plant is losing to the clouds we can treat

👉 **Why now**

* Cloud access got \~97% cheaper: conventional seeding aircrafts cost $2,000+/hr; electric drones are at $30–60/hr. 
* AI is transforming weather forecasting: DeepMind's weather models produce [15-day forecasts in less than a minute](https://deepmind.google/blog/weathernext-ai-model-achieves-breakthrough-in-forecasting-cyclones/) and [outperform traditional physics-based models on more than 90% of benchmarks](https://developers.google.com/weathernext/guides/evals).

🎯 **Weakening storms and hurricanes**

Our ultimate goal is to reduce the intensity of severe storms and hurricanes.

Severe weather has already cost the US [$31.9B in the first half of 2026](https://www.climatecentral.org/climate-services/billion-dollar-disasters), and from 2020 to 2024 severe storms, floods, and tropical cyclones caused [an average of \~$121B/yr in losses](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/billions/summary-stats). Severe storms alone generated [$50B+/yr in insured losses for the past three years](https://www.iii.org/press-release/triple-i-severe-convective-storms-generate-more-than-50b-in-insured-losses-for-third-consecutive-year-041326). There's now [a billion-dollar weather disaster every 16 days vs. every 82 days in the 1980s](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/billions/climatology).

Globally, these disasters caused [over $2T in damage in the past decade](https://iccwbo.org/news-publications/policies-reports/new-report-extreme-weather-events-cost-economy-2-trillion-over-the-last-decade) and claimed [more than 2 million lives in the past 50 years](https://news.un.org/en/story/2023/05/1136897). 

Clearing stable overcast clouds is our first major technical milestone. It will prove we can reliably alter clouds at scale. From there, we’ll expand our fleets and control systems to reduce the intensity of severe storms and hurricanes. First storm operation targeted for late 2028.

👥 **Team**

We're two Cambridge engineers with backgrounds in weather engineering and droplet-control systems:

Mete (CEO): Master's research on making clouds more reflective using seawater spray nozzles at the Cambridge Centre for Climate Repair (funded by ARIA, UK's DARPA). MEng from Cambridge in aerospace/aerothermal, energy, and mechanical engineering.

Eric (CTO): Master's research on microfluidic chips that control water, and built droplet-removal technology for LiDAR lenses. MEng from Cambridge in electrical, control, and computer engineering. Placed 4th nationally in the British Physics Challenge.

🙏 **We'd love to hear from you if you:**

* work in disaster response or severe weather at the state or federal level (FEMA, state EMs, NOAA, NWS)
* run hail suppression programs (North Dakota, Texas, Alberta)
* own, manage, build, or operate utility-scale solar plants (especially in Texas, northern US, UK, or northern Europe)
* work in weather modelling / meteorology / atmospheric science (especially in hurricane or storm research)
* are engineers with experience in drones or high-voltage systems / power electronics

Reach us at [team@meteoric.earth](mailto:team@meteoric.earth)

**You give us your Airbnbs to manage, and you’ll take home 10-20% more while both you and your guests have a better experience.**

Launch Video:\
<https://youtu.be/gvvV5zLIPV4>

## The Problem

Short-term rentals were sold as passive income. But in reality, every Airbnb is a tiny hotel and a nightmare of operations. Every reservation restarts the operational clock: prices must be adjusted, guests screened, messages answered, cleaners scheduled, access coordinated, supplies restocked, and maintenance handled, often overnight or between back-to-back stays.

And in traditional short-term property management companies, operational failures are common, and they can quickly become very costly:

* A missed cleaning becomes a bad review
* A poorly screened guest becomes property damage
* A neglected maintenance issue becomes an issued refund or lost booking

On top of these operational failures, the average management company takes 15–30% of rental revenue, often alongside cleaning, maintenance, and other fees.

We’ve been property managers for the past year and ran into the same lose-lose choice every owner faces: manage a 24/7 hospitality business yourself, or hand over a quarter of your revenue to a management company whose costs increase with every property it adds.

## The Solution

We are building a new type of property management company, with infrastructure built for agents and human-computer-interaction from the ground up. By replacing the layers of coordination and operational overhead built into traditional management companies, we provide a much better service at a much lower fee.

We center around a simple premise: owners shouldn’t have to choose between good service and reasonable fees. With our model, **owners take home 10–20% more and guests have a more premium experience.**

## Team

We’re Shaan and Edmond, longtime friends, Duke roommates, and property managers.

Edmond previously built AI voice agents at Rilla, LLM agents at S&P Global, and data pipelines at Vanguard. He has been managing rentals for a year, experiencing the owner’s dilemma firsthand.

Shaan previously designed GPU hardware at Apple, brain-computer interface research at Yale, computer architecture research at Duke. He also has been managing Airbnbs and longer-term rentals for a year and a half.

## The Ask

We are live in 80 properties today, and would love to have you join us.

**If you own a short-term rental** (such as an Airbnb), we can help you generate more revenue while providing better experiences to guests and giving you that peace of mind that your property is in good hands.

**If you are considering investing in a short-term rental,** we can help turn your investment into a much more lucrative investment vehicle.

You can reach out to us at [founders@atlia.com](mailto:founders@atlia.com). And schedule a free property review at [www.atlia.com](http://www.atlia.com).

launches.tagline: Dream makes pocket-sized, battery-powered AI cameras that catch damage teams miss.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋, we are Ryland and Alexander, co-founders of Dream.

**TL;DR: Dream automatically photographs every vehicle or machine that passes through your gate, builds a 3D condition record, and uses AI to catch new damage the moment an asset passes through.**

**Launch Video: [https://youtu.be/uMP12lCb12E](https://youtu.be/uMP12lCb12E)**

**The problem**

Damage is an expensive leak for anyone who moves large, expensive assets in and out all day. It shows up two different ways:

**Car dealership service departments**

* As a car pulls into the service entrance, damage that could be identified and fixed goes unnoticed, which is lost revenue.
* Without a record of the car's condition on arrival, disputes come down to the customer's word against the dealership's, and the dealership gets blamed for pre-existing damage.

**High-value asset rentals (heavy equipment, trucks, boats, planes, trailers)**

* Teams are inconsistent about photographing assets as they go out and come back, so new damage gets missed before the customer is billed.
* When damage is missed, there's no evidence to charge the customer, so the company eats the repair cost out of pocket.

**What Dream does**

Dream cameras sit at your gate, lane, or service drive and turn every pass into evidence, automatically:

* **Continuous capture:** every vehicle or machine that moves through is photographed from every angle. No one has to remember to do it.
* **Asset identification:** Dream knows exactly what you need to look at.
* **3D reconstruction:** every pass becomes a complete 3D condition record for that asset.
* **AI damage detection:** on return or intake, Dream compares against the last record and flags new dents, scrapes, and visible changes right away.

The result is one clear source of truth for every asset's condition over time: rental companies catch damage before they bill so they stop eating repair costs, and dealership service departments find more fixable damage and resolve customer disputes with evidence.

Works across cars, vans, trucks, heavy equipment, and more.

**Why us**

We have spent years training models for aerial imaging and edge computer vision devices. Ryland has worked on the exact problem of detecting damage to assets from aerial imaging, such as degraded paint. Alexander has trained models that run on edge cameras deployed in the wild in Africa and India to detect poachers.

**Our ask**

We're onboarding partners now. **We'd love intros to:**

* **Car dealerships**
* **High-value asset rental companies** (heavy equipment, trucks, boats, planes, trailers)

If you run one of these, or know someone who does, please message us on LinkedIn!

launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/DfSQ8L7d0BM?si=9Zp7BVPvCD_vB4ke>\
\
**THE PROBLEM**

Industrial control software still looks and feels like it was built in the Windows 95 era. Manufacturers spend weeks stitching together Programable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), HMIs, databases, and custom integrations just to get systems running. Additionally, legacy systems collect enormous amounts of high-quality data, but don’t do _anything_ with it, even though it could easily be used for things such as anomaly detection or optimization recommendations.\
\
**OUR SOLUTION**

We're building an AI-native platform to unify the industrial control stack, starting with SCADA and eventually extending down to PLC hardware and the devices on the factory floor. We offer both a product and a service:

**1) Software**

We already built a full SCADA system to replace legacy platforms like Ignition, WinCC, and FactoryTalk. It’s AI native: users can use AI to generate controls screens in seconds (this used to take hours), write custom scrips/logical flows, and automatically detect issues before they become catastrophic. \
\
Not only is this a full SCADA system, but it can operate on top of an existing one so that users can take advantage of our “intelligence layer” without having to rip out their current infrastructure (people understandably don’t like doing this).\
\
**2) System Integration** 

We’ve recently expanded to become an AI-native industrial integrator. Instead of just selling our software, we integrate it into our clients existing stack for them, and help them set up any other tools they need to run it. 

Over the past few months, we've spent hundreds of hours talking with controls engineers, manufacturers, operators, and system integrators. We already knew that industrial software was broken, but we also learned that even when better technology exists, people are understandably cautious about adopting it. These systems run critical infrastructure and reliability matters more than novelty. Change is slow, but we want to reindustrialize America now.

**Instead of waiting for the industry to adopt an entirely new software stack, we're bringing our technology directly into customer projects today.**

While larger firms can spend millions on integration services, smaller firms don’t have that kind of money. Traditional integrators use highly manual methods to set up their clients software stacks (which are also outdated). By leveraging AI, we’ll be able to set up the same systems at 10x the speed and charge way less. 

**Our ask: if you’re exploring controls/automation systems, PLC programming, SCADA systems, or system integration**, **we’d love to talk. Or, if you know any deep tech companies that want to set up a controls system, let us know!**

See more at <https://controlseat.com>.

**TL;DR: [Cova](https://cova.care/) is a licensed home care agency in Michigan. AI agents run the entire back office, which lets us pay caregivers the highest base rate in the state, charge families less, and help unpaid family caregivers get paid through programs they didn't know they qualified for.**

<https://youtu.be/28Xmk3izvks>

**The problem**

This is one of the largest, fastest-growing markets in the country. 11,000 Americans turn 65 every day, and 70% want to age at home. 53 million people are already unpaid family caregivers, over $1 trillion in economic value every year that the system doesn’t capture.

But getting someone into home care is brutal. The application and paperwork alone take weeks of back-and-forth across a caregiver, a patient and their family, a doctor, and a state caseworker, with paper forms bouncing between all of them. Most of that time isn't care; it's coordination. Most families give up before care ever starts, and caregivers wait unpaid.

When care finally begins, caregivers suffer from missed payments and poor coordination, affecting patients downstream. All of this because existing agencies aren’t built to handle care at scale.

**What Cova does**

We own the full stack: Cova is its own home care agency serving Medicaid, LTCI, and private-pay patients, and AI agents run it end to end.

* **Weeks → days.** AI agents handle the applications and paperwork that normally drags on for weeks in just a few days.
* **Zero FTE overhead = highest caregiver pay in the state.** AI agents do the coordination work, so we carry no non-caregiver headcount and pass that straight to caregivers as the highest base rate in Michigan.
* **We get family caregivers paid.** Millions are already caring for a loved one for free and qualify for programs they've never heard of. AI agents find those programs and get them enrolled and paid.
* **We bill the payers directly.** Because we own the agency, we make money the way agencies do, billing Medicaid, MCOs, LTCI, and private pay, just with a fraction of the cost structure.

**About the team**

**Jordan Ibe (Co-Founder)** – Studied Computer Science & Statistics at Cornell University. Previously a Forward Deployed Software Engineer on Palantir’s Healthcare team and Software Engineer at Uber.

**Ansh Tandon (Co-Founder)** – Completed a BSE & MSE in Bioengineering at the University of Pennsylvania. Previously a Deployment Strategist on Palantir’s Healthcare team and Researcher at Daffodil Health.

* Intros to Michigan MCOs (Medicaid managed care orgs) and long-term care insurance contacts

* Intros to Michigan discharge planners, hospital case managers, and social workers who place patients into home care

launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: Your customer data is fragmented across Pylon, Granola, Posthog, Hubspot, Slack, and Notion. Poth connects that information into a living model of your customers, mapping analytics from Posthog and transcripts from Granola to the same customer, so you can finally answer the questions that live across multiple tools: churn, adoption or what to build next, with cited evidence. pothlabs.com**

<https://youtu.be/k9gsdaxXdtM>

**The problem:**

Companies have customer information scattered across support tickets, sales calls, CRM notes, surveys, interviews, product analytics and more. 

But answering a new question about customers still usually means manually searching across those systems or beginning another research project.

**The (soft) pivot:**

We originally built Poth to generate hypotheses and launch adaptive interviews and surveys to test them. To determine what questions to ask and which customers to ask, Poth first had to understand all of the customer information a company already had.

Under the hood, we built a customer knowledge graph: Poth identifies the important objects in a company’s data: customers, accounts, users, products, features, conversations, behaviors, and feedback, and connects them through their relationships.

As we integrated with more teams, we noticed that several were using this underlying model as much as, or more than, the survey functionality itself. They wanted to ask questions across everything their customers had already said and done so we made that a core part of the product!

**Customer knowledge graph example:**

For a company like Slack, Poth might model five objects:

* **Account**  (a company paying for Slack)
* **User**
* **Workspace**
* **Feature** (Slack Connect, Huddles, Canvas, or workflows)
* **Customer signal** (A support ticket, call transcript, survey response, or product event)

It then connects them through relationships such as:

User —BELONGS_TO→ Account Account —OWNS→ Workspace User —USED→ Feature Customer Signal —CREATED_BY→ User Customer Signal —REFERENCES→ Feature

Slack could then ask:

“Why are enterprise accounts trying Slack Connect but not adopting it broadly?”

And Poth could connect low Slack Connect usage in PostHog, permission-related support tickets in Pylon, security concerns mentioned in Granola transcripts, and renewal context from HubSpot, all through the same accounts, users, workspaces, and features.

Instead of returning a generic summary, Poth can show the supporting and contradicting evidence, cite the underlying sources, and explain what information is still missing.

In practice, the model contains many more objects and relationships based on each company’s business and data.

**Ask Poth:**

Connect your customer data sources and internal documentation. Poth automatically builds the living model, and your team can ask questions naturally across everything customers have said and done.

When the existing evidence is not enough, you can also use Poth to launch adaptive interviews and surveys to collect what is missing.

Some use cases we’ve seen:

* **Discovery:** “Across our discovery calls, what do users want most that we haven’t built?”
* **Adoption and growth:** What is preventing activated customers from adopting more of the product and expanding?”
* **Churn and risk:** “Identify the top three reasons customers have churned, then flag the five active accounts showing similar warning signs.”
* **Win-loss analysis:** “What are the most common reasons we lose enterprise deals, and which product gaps are actually affecting revenue?”
* **Account intelligence:** “Give me everything relevant to this account before my next customer call.”

**Our ask:**

We’re already working with several teams in the YC batch, and we’re looking for more companies whose customer context is spread across several systems.

I’d especially appreciate introductions to:

* Founders and product leaders at growing startups with significant customer data across three or more tools
* Heads of Customer Insights, Voice of the Customer, Customer Experience, User Research, or Customer Success at larger companies

And if your team has important customer questions it still cannot answer confidently, email me at [matthew@pothlabs.com](mailto:matthew@pothlabs.com)! We’ll work closely with early teams to connect their core systems and get them live.

pothlabs.com
