launches.title: Dipole Labs: Shooting lasers to solve the billion-dollar bottleneck inside AI datacenters
launches.tagline: High-speed optical circuit switches that keep data moving as light, giving AI clusters up to 25% more useful compute from the same hardware.
launches.body:
**The most expensive computers ever built spend about half their time waiting for data.** As AI clusters scale, it's increasingly the network that limits how much compute you can actually use.

**What we're building** Dipole Labs builds high-speed optical circuit switches for AI data centers. Between racks, data already travels as light, but routing it usually means converting it to electricity and back, burning power, generating heat, and adding latency. Dipole's switch keeps data in the optical domain, targeting sub-microsecond reconfiguration at large port counts, so the network can reshape itself around each workload.

An AI-native control layer learns GPU communication patterns and synchronizes optical reconfiguration with training and inference, turning the network into an active accelerator instead of a bottleneck.

**Why it matters** The result: a 10,000-GPU cluster could perform like one with 12,500 GPUs, up to 25% more useful compute from the same hardware. At the scale of a 1 GW data center, that's up to $1 billion in additional compute capacity every year. Optical switching is just the start, the same platform extends from moving data as light to computing with it.

**Who we are** Deepankur and Gabriele met as postdocs at Harvard and have spent the last decade building the photonic expertise behind this technology. Deepankur (CEO) built scalable quantum-optical hardware at ETH Zurich, published in Nature, and was awarded the ETH Medal for his doctoral thesis. Gabriele (CTO) has built nanophotonic and quantum devices at EPFL, and solved a decade-old condensed-matter physics problem published in Nature Materials, which earned the IBM prize from the Swiss and Austrian Physical Society.

**Our ask** We're opening design partnerships with hyperscalers and neoclouds that want more useful compute from the hardware they already run, plus collaborations with photonic foundries to take our custom devices from prototype to scale. If that's you, let's talk.

launches.tagline: Making the physical world machine-readable across the entire electromagnetic spectrum
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We are building a new kind of camera that can see through walls using radio waves. We provide construction, industrial inspection, and security teams with an accurate map of hidden objects behind walls and composite surfaces.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2iEHRvcKN8g>

## **The Problem**

Most of the built world is opaque.

Pipes, cables, and structural elements hide behind walls until they're discovered mid-project, driving $20B+ a year in avoidable rework.

Defects remain hidden inside composites until parts break.

Entry teams are missing critical information before they breach a barrier.

## **The Solution**

An imaging platform that uses radio waves to see behind walls. It works just like a camera, requiring no training and producing high-resolution images that are instantly understandable. The resulting point cloud is natively to scale, accurate down to 1mm.

## **The Team**

Four engineers who've worked together for 8+ years, shipped multiple zero-to-one hardware products, and hold 250+ patents.

**Bilgehan** — PhD in electromagnetics; led antenna technologies on four iPhone generations, shipping the first phones with UWB and 5G mmWave; inventor of the zirconia dielectric resonator antenna.

**Brian** — built the earliest iPhone prototypes at Apple, co-invented iPhone multitouch and the Nest Learning Thermostat; degrees in Electrical and Civil Engineering.

**George** — MIT physicist; built x-ray imagers, retinal implants, optical sensors and the world's smallest laser projector.

**Paul** — Berkeley Mech.E.; ex-Apple and Humane product design lead; co-invented iPhone haptic Touch ID, IPX8 sealing.

## **What we built**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108275&key=user_uploads/2724984/c00b3438-c7f7-433f-941d-e021791e51c5)

We've built the hardware and imaging algorithms that can see behind composite layers and common building materials (sheetrock, tiles, marble, quartz, brick and insulation). Next step is our handheld platform that fuses our radio imaging with RGB and thermal cameras.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108275&key=user_uploads/2724984/f1cf1ffa-8b23-4780-b363-13b0db90832d)

## **Our Ask**

We're looking for intros to decision makers at general contracting firms and industrial inspection teams, and to contacts with military access who can introduce and demo our systems to US defense organizations.

If that's you or someone you know, reach out to us at [founders@ae-dyn.com](mailto:founders@ae-dyn.com)

launches.title: Illume Labs - Your 24/7 personalized health companion
launches.tagline: Illume is a 24/7 personal health companion that connects your wearables, nutrition, workouts, and lab results to give you personalized, actionable insights over text.
launches.body:
**Hey everyone 👋!** We’re [Pari](https://www.linkedin.com/in/paridhilatawa/), [Frank](https://www.linkedin.com/in/frank-lee-/), and [Jin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jinwong01/), co-founders of Illume. 

**TL;DR:** Illume is a 24/7 personal health companion that connects your wearables, nutrition, workouts, and lab results to give you personalized, actionable insights over text. 

**Join our private beta waitlist: [www.illumelabs.ai](http://www.illumelabs.ai). \
Watch Our [Launch Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bsfFOzB0Nho):**

**Problem:** 

Health data is more abundant than ever, but it remains scattered. Nearly six in ten U.S. adults own a wearable or connected health device, and nearly one in three used an AI chatbot for health questions. People are generating more health data than ever and actively looking for help understanding it, but their data and guidance still live in separate places. 

We saw this firsthand as family members struggled to piece together glucose readings for diabetes and blood tests for cardiovascular risk, all while juggling a pile of fitness, nutrition, and health-tracking apps that never talked to each other. 

People increasingly turn to ChatGPT or Claude for answers, but without continuous context to their health, the advice is often generic, incomplete, and difficult to track over time.

**Our solution:** 

Illume creates one home for your health and gives you a personal health companion you can text. 

Today, you can: 

* Connect your wearable and automatically sync sleep, activity, and recovery data 
* Text Illume photos of your meals to log and understand your nutrition 
* Record workouts and track your training 
* Upload bloodwork and lab results 
* Ask questions about your health using the context of your own data 
* Receive proactive insights about what changed, what it might mean, and what to do next

For example, you can ask: 

* “Why am I so exhausted today? Make me a dashboard of all the relevant metrics!” 
* “How has eating late affected my sleep?”
* “Am I recovering well enough to train? Run a regression!”
* “What should I focus on before my next blood test?”

Illume connects patterns across your data that individual platforms can’t see, giving you a more complete picture of your health instead of another isolated score or dashboard. 

You can text your Illume agent for quick answers or use the platform to explore your data, trends, and history in greater depth.

**Our mission**

Our long-term vision is to make healthcare more proactive, continuous, and personalized. 

By combining continuous biometrics with nutrition, training, blood panels, and eventually genetic risk, Illume could help surface meaningful changes earlier and help people understand their susceptibility to conditions such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and Alzheimer’s. 

We want to help people move from asking, “What happened?” to understanding what may be changing and what they can do about it. 

**Who’s it for:** Illume is initially designed for people who are proactive about their health and longevity- especially lifters, biohackers, and anyone already using wearables, blood panels, CGMs, nutrition trackers, or genetic testing.  

**Who we are:** We’re three MIT graduates who met in freshman year! 

[Pari Latawa](https://www.linkedin.com/in/paridhilatawa/): MIT BS & MEng in CS + Molecular Biology. Previously conducted research at the Broad Institute, Eli Lilly, & MD Anderson. Founded EasyComm to build tools for children with Down Syndrome, and SparkED, a health-literacy nonprofit.

[Frank Lee](https://www.linkedin.com/in/frank-lee-/): MIT BS in Computer Science and Mathematics. Conducted RLAIF research for language models at MIT CSAIL and previously built agent systems at Windsurf.

[Jin Wong](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jinwong01/): MIT BS in Business Analytics. Previously conducted research at the MIT Media Lab and deployed coding agents at Windsurf. 

**Our ask:** 

**Join the private beta waitlist at [www.illumelabs.ai](http://www.illumelabs.ai).** We’ll invite an initial group of founding members to receive early access and help shape the product. 

**If you want to chat or can intro us** to someone in training, sports, longevity, and/or biohacking, email us at [founders@illumelabs.ai](mailto:founders@illumelabs.ai). We’d love to stop by, chat, and show you how Illume works!

launches.title: Instance: Automated evaluation for robot policies, starting with the success detector
launches.tagline: Today, evaluating a robot policy means humans have to watch the robot roll out, mark success, and reset the scene – we're automating that.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We’re **automating robot evaluation**– the loop where you wait for your robot to roll out, judge its success, and then reset the scene. Today, we’re launching step one: a **success detector** that automatically tells you whether your robot actually completed its task. Book a demo with [founders@instancelabs.ai](mailto:founders@instancelabs.ai) and we’ll visit your office to show you how it works!

<https://youtu.be/EqxkPffnUKk>

**The problem**

In Lucy’s robotics research this past year, she **spent way too much time being a babysitter for her robot**. Her project was to get a humanoid to find objects around a room, so her days went like this: start a rollout, watch the robot open all the drawers in the room for 30 minutes, mark success/fail in a spreadsheet, then get up, close all the drawers, and put the objects back where they started. Then do it again, and again, and again. Some days ended with back pain, and for weeks she couldn’t work on anything else because she was stuck doing exactly this.

That was one robot, in one lab, running a single policy. Industry teams run fleets of robots across dozens of policies, with **multiple people assigned to sit and watch each one**. Every robotics team we’ve talked to has some version of this– and it will only grow as robot foundation models scale.

**Our solution**

Instance is building the **autonomous evaluation rig for robot learning**: your robot rolls out, we judge success, a second robot resets the scene, and the next rollout starts– with no humans in the loop at all.

Today, we’re starting with the success judge. Point us at a task description and your video rollouts, and we return a verdict with detailed subtask captions. We benchmarked our verifier against 10,000+ held-out, human-labeled episodes across 7 robot platforms, and it resulted in **higher accuracy than Claude Opus 4.8, at a fraction of the latency.**

**Try it**

Try it at [demo.instancelabs.ai](http://demo.instancelabs.ai) – drop in a video, or record one from your phone and watch it get verified live.

**Team**

We’re Claire and Lucy, MIT grads and friends since middle school! 

Claire studied math and CS at MIT. At NASA JPL, she built software to simulate planetary atmospheres, and at the MIT Media Lab, she researched sustainable propulsion for spaceflight. She loves working where software meets the physical world.

Lucy studied CS at MIT and completed her MEng in MIT's Learning and Intelligent Systems lab. She’s an experienced robotics researcher, and has in the past worked on satellite software at SpaceX, LLM unit testing at Amazon, and brain computer interfaces at Blackrock Neurotech.

**Our ask**

If you are:

* training robot policies
* running evals
* deploying robots in the real world
* or can intro us to someone who is,

Email us ([founders@instancelabs.ai](mailto:founders@instancelabs.ai)) to book a demo. We’d love to swing by your office with sweet treats to show you how it works!

**TL;DR: Marker partners with execs, learns how their organization actually works, finds the highest-impact problems, and solves them by** **shipping custom AI agents into production on the Marker platform in weeks. Each agent deepens our understanding of the business, so the next agent launches faster. We stay embedded until the business is rebuilt.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O829Y4wlKvk>

We’re Will Drevno, Richard Berwick, and David Pastewka, the founders of Marker. We’ve built together for 15 years. Our last company, Drapr (YC S20), was acquired by Gap Inc., and Richard went on to found Gap’s Office of AI.

## **Why we built Marker**

Inside Gap, we saw firsthand how much leaders wanted to transform their businesses with AI and how hard it was to turn that ambition into production systems that actually changed how their organizations worked.

**95% of AI initiatives still fail. Ours don’t.**

The hard part is understanding how work happens across people, systems, and teams; choosing the opportunities that matter most; and getting solutions into production.

## **How Marker works**

We embed with each company and lead the transformation end to end:

* **Understand the organization.** We listen closely to leaders and frontline teams, learn their systems and ways of working, and map the processes that usually live in people’s heads.
* **Find the biggest opportunities.** We identify and prioritize the problems where AI can have the greatest impact on cost, capacity, speed, or growth.
* **Build and ship.** We create custom agents and automations around the company’s real workflows and systems. The agents we deploy run on the Marker Command Center and go live in production within weeks.
* **Compound.** Every agent we deploy deepens our understanding of the company. That helps us launch the next one faster and makes Marker increasingly integral to how the organization operates.

## **Who we’re working with today**

We’re rebuilding companies from mid-size through Fortune 500.

## **Why us**

We’ve sat on every side of this: founders selling into enterprises, operators transforming one from the inside, and executives responsible for enterprise AI. Marker is the company we wish we could have hired at Gap.

name: WonderTx
former_names: A Company in Stealth Mode Incorporated
long_description:
We’re an AI-native biotech, working on replacing needles with pills. Many drugs, like insulin or Ozempic, are wonderful except you have to inject them. We discover new molecules that you can take as a pill instead. Because the pills operate on biology which has been shown to be effective in people, rather than merely in animal models of disease, we avoid what has historically been the single biggest risk in drug discovery.  This should dramatically increase our probability of success.

There’s $200B of treatable diseases and validated human biology without a pill because discovery programs lack a tractable chemical starting point. This is a zero-shot inference problem, because these targets have no training data, so LLMs and other historical interpolative AI approaches are insufficient. Instead, we are building our own extrapolative frontier models that reason beyond their training data. Most critically, we have repeatedly validated our platform on both our own and partner programs. On 4 biologically- and structurally-diverse targets where we had zero training data, we successfully picked binders that were validated experimentally, with confirmation ranging from primary screen hits to crystallographic structures.
one_liner: Extrapolative AI to unlock First-in-Class drugs

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer: Imagine how drug discovery is done 80 years from now and it’s obvious that AI is going to be woven through every piece and every step.  No one believes that we will have less data, or that it will be easier to understand, or that we won’t need advanced statistical algorithms, or that the computers will be less capable.  There is an inevitability here.  But let’s not wait 80 years!  If we succeed then the path from conception to clinic for the toughest diseases, for the most difficult biological problems, becomes tractable.  Our practical outcome is simple: patients whose diseases cannot currently be drugged effectively or at all will live better longer lives.

launches.title: WonderTx: Extrapolative AI to Unlock First-in-Class Drugs
launches.tagline: Reindustrializing our life science ecosystem.
launches.body:
Our objective is to deliver first-in-class medicines against disease targets that cannot currently be drugged effectively or at all. Therefore, we are building a lights-out wonder drug factory, where AI runs the entire design-make-test loop. Linking superhuman judgment to robotic throughput is the path to reindustrializing our life science ecosystem, not through throwing human labor at the problem.

Our team has been working on this for over a decade, so we know that there has never been a better time to build this system.  Abe co-founded Atomwise, one of the first AI-for-drug-discovery companies.  We raised $220 million; hired 100 people; signed over $5B in total deal value with big pharma companies like Sanofi, Bayer, Eli Lilly, and others; and ran the biggest application of AI to hit discovery in history. Saulo solved the synthesizability problem in generative chemistry AI and wrote structural biology software that remains the standard toolkit (KVFinder; qFit3, STCRDab). Cam co-founded Xbox & Xbox Live (Microsoft) and has been a CEO, CTO, COO, and CPO across AI, biotech, healthcare, and consumer tech. 

Today, we see the convergence of critical enabling computational, physical, and economic trend lines. Agentic systems have become proficient orchestrators and tool integrators, as the frontier labs continue to extend the time horizons over which agents can operate; in our own hands, we have already compressed compound selection timelines 10x by replacing manual processes by agentic-run. The algorithmically-accessible chemical space has been growing exponentially for two decades, and the rise of cloud labs enables closing and scaling the design loop. Finally, the looming Big Pharma patent cliff means that the ecosystem is aligned on the value of innovative new assets. 

At WonderTx, we’re beginning by replacing needles with pills. Many drugs, like insulin or Ozempic, are great except you have to inject them. We discover new molecules that you can take as a pill instead. Because the pills operate on biology that has been shown to be effective in people, rather than merely in animal models of disease, we avoid what has historically been the single biggest risk in drug discovery.  This should dramatically increase our probability of success.

There’s $200B of treatable diseases and validated human biology without a pill because discovery programs lack a tractable chemical starting point, which makes this a zero-shot inference problem.  Because these targets have no training data, off-the-shelf LLMs and other historical interpolative AI approaches are insufficient. Instead, we are building our own extrapolative frontier models that reason beyond their training data. Most critically, we have repeatedly validated our platform on both our own and partner programs. On 4 biologically- and structurally-diverse targets where we had zero training data, we successfully picked binders that were validated experimentally, with confirmation ranging from primary screen hits to crystallographic structures.

launches.tagline: Sidekick gives frontline workers an AI assistant they can text, with no app, login, or training.
launches.body:
**Hey everyone 👋**

I'm Justin, founder of Sidekick.

**TL;DR** Sidekick is an AI assistant that frontline manufacturing workers use over text message. They text a number and it answers from the company's own documents, creates and routes work orders, and syncs with the software the company already uses. No app, no login, no training. I built Sidekick for my dad's manufacturing shop. It’s now live at facilities across the globe.

**_Ask:_** Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility? I'd love an intro! Email [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick).

Check out our launch video:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yxwq5ZAojXg>

## ❌ The Problem

I grew up in my dad's manufacturing plants and spent summers working on the factory floor at EDS Manufacturing.

Here's what I watched happen repeatedly. A machine goes down, everyone's waiting, and the person who can help is in a meeting or on another line. Half the time the answer already existed. Nobody could get to it.

Why it keeps happening:

* **No computer access.** Nobody on that floor has a company login or an email address, so none of the plant's software reaches them.
* **The answers are scattered.** An SOP in a binder, a manual on a shared drive few have permissions to, a safety procedure someone printed and taped to a wall in 2019.
* **The best answers were never written down.** Thirty years of tribal knowledge lives in one guy's head, and when he retires it leaves with him.
* **So the same questions get asked over and over.** Shift after shift, and every one of them costs somebody their afternoon.

There are 239,000 manufacturing plants in the US, and only 29% of the people working in them have advanced digital skills. Any tool that requires a download, a login, and training makes adoption difficult.

## ✅ Our Solution

Workers text the Sidekick phone number. Problems, photos, voice memos, in any language. No app to download, no account to create, nothing to learn. Every worker on the floor already knows how to send a text, which is why adoption isn't a fight.

* **Answers from your own documents.** SOPs, manuals, safety procedures, tribal knowledge. Sidekick responds in the worker's language, in seconds.
* **Creates and routes the work order.** The issue gets logged and sent to the right person, without anyone needing a laptop.
* **Syncs with the software you already run.** Sidekick pulls from and writes to your existing systems instead of replacing them, and integrates directly through PLC and SCADA systems so the floor and the software finally see the same thing.
* **Captures tribal knowledge.** Every exchange builds a searchable knowledge base the company owns, so the know-how stays when the veteran leaves.

Here's a full walkthrough:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a5zBRSXi-90>

## 👤 The Team

I'm Justin, founder and CEO. I'm the third generation in a manufacturing family, and I've been around plant floors since I was a kid. I studied Computer Science at the University of Pennsylvania, worked in finance at Arm, and left both to build Sidekick after watching the same problem play out on every floor I'd been on.

## 🙏 Our Ask

If you answer "yes" to any of these, I'd love your help:

* **Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility?** Even a name and a "you two should talk" goes a long way.
* **Have you sold software into manufacturing?** I'd love to hear what actually worked and what didn't.

Contact me at [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo here**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick)**.**

**TL;DR:** Mentlio is the engineering intelligence platform for the AI-coding era. We help engineering organizations cut AI costs by up to 30% and finally see what ROI that spend is actually producing. All without ever collecting your prompts or source code.

**Launch Video**

<https://youtu.be/-28j9HvTYV0>

**Problem**

Every engineering org is now an AI org. Token usage is growing exponentially, and so is the bill. The following questions have been largely unanswered:

* How can we cut our usage-based AI spend without bottlenecking usage or efficiency?
* What ROI are we getting for every dollar of AI spend?
* To what extent is AI-generated code creating quality debt?

Brian Armstrong recently laid out how Coinbase is reducing AI spend while token usage grows exponentially on X: better defaults, smarter routing, cache awareness, lean context, and full visibility into usage and impact. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111055&key=user_uploads/2693539/7bf48740-dd37-4015-9da9-ec0f9bd900ed)

Coinbase built a custom harness, LLM gateway, routing, and usage visibility internally. We believe they have the right thesis, but most engineering orgs don’t want to run on a custom harness. **Mentlio gives every eng team a better version of those savings & visibility without changing any workflows.**

**Solution**

Mentlio gives you:

1. **ROI.** We translate every PR into normalized units of work: Delivery Points. We consider associated spend, code reusability, and historical patches to turn "we spend $X on AI"  -> "we spend $X per impact point.” compared to industry data. 
2. **Cost intelligence + optimization.** See exactly where AI spend goes across teams, tools, and models. Optionally catch and cut waste across cache misses, oversized models on trivial tasks, bloated context and cut it without capping/bottlenecking accuracy. 
3. **Quality signal.** AI-assisted code that ships fast but breaks later isn't a win. We connect AI usage to delivery and quality outcomes so you can see the full picture

We’re the only platform with the above capabilities that never collects prompts or source code.

**Our Asks**

If you are or know a Head of Eng, VP Eng, CTO, or platform lead at a 15+ engineer org with real AI spend, reach out! You can book a demo at[ mentlio.com/intro](http://mentlio.com/intro) or reach us at [founders@mentlio.com](mailto:founders@mentlio.com).

launches.body:
TL;DR: We’ve built the foundations of a pharma in the age of superintelligence: data partnerships, biology models and autonomous research agents. We have SOTA results on finding overlooked drugs and predicting clinical trial success rates. 

Hey everyone! We ([Sanjukta Bhattacharya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sanjukta-b-82b541198/), [Christian Gensbigler](https://www.linkedin.com/in/christian-g-a2594029a/), and I) started Atlas Discovery to get treatments to patients who need them most.

**The problem:** Today's pharma works for only \~150 diseases. Below roughly $150M in expected revenue a program never gets funded, because the cost of developing a drug is fixed by the knowledge work it requires, not the size of the market. 10,000+ diseases remain without an approved treatment even where the biology is tractable. Meanwhile, there are 100,000+ existing drugs, and barely 1% of the drug-disease combinations have ever been tried. The bottleneck is no longer supply of compounds; it's the judgment needed to search that space and run the trials, and the removal of human coordination costs.

**Our** **thesis** is that AI will drop the cost of drug development enough to push the viable threshold from \~$150M toward \~$15M, opening a \~$500B market incumbents have structurally ignored. A company built for that world needs three things: proprietary data, models that predict clinical trial outcomes, and agent systems that replace knowledge work. We use agents to repurpose existing drugs for the long tail of diseases, then run the clinical trials faster and cheaper. 

**Progress**: In three months we've built the first version of all three layers. Data: an 8 figure LOI with an AI lab and 6 figures in contracted revenue. Models: state-of-the-art clinical trial prediction results published at three conferences,. Agents: three rare disease foundations are now testing drugs surfaced by our agents. 

On drug repurposing using agents, we see nearly 5x improvement over current frontier LLMs. Read more about this benchmark [here](https://atlasdiscovery.bio/repurposingbench.html).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/cf98d216-1d2c-45a0-99c9-ef87d2b7b296)


We've also shown that models trained on in vitro cell data (Latin for "in glass") and mouse data can translate to gains in predicting patient response to drugs in human clinical trials.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/6813bfeb-e5c9-47ec-9b9e-89362cf8eb15)

We’ve also shown SOTA results in being able to predict clinical trial success when trained on over 100,000 clinical trials data and evaluated on a held out set of 10,000 trials. Read more [here](https://atlasdiscovery.bio/clinical-trial-prediction-with-ai-agents.html)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/23aff312-7161-4be9-b4af-3273d469bd5d)

We’ve presented our research in 3 top conferences (ICLR, CSHL, ICML) and shown that new AI architectures like discrete diffusion can learn these gene expression patterns and predict response to treatments with over 10x improvement in accuracy while training on 50x less data.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107031&key=user_uploads/774885/fa2a6593-751d-448b-a67b-e232e3e07ffb)

Reach us at [founders@atlasdiscovery.bio](mailto:founders@atlasdiscovery.bio)

Blog: <https://atlasdiscovery.bio/>blog

name: rekursiv.ai
long_description:
We're scaling self-improving AI scientist teams to ideate/experiment/discover, generating new knowledge autonomously. Their discoveries reduced ARC-1/2 costs by 10,000× while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy and yielded material advances on combinatorial ML problems.

We believe that AI is bounded not by compute, but ideas. Scaling to millions of sessions of discovery enables leveraging its own discoveries and presents a novel training source capable of ushering a new era of self-reliant foundational models.
one_liner: Scale AI scientists whose own breakthroughs accelerate the next.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
AI research is bottlenecked by humans. Every advance in ML still runs through a small number of researchers who can only devise and test ideas so fast. Experiments take days, most fail, and the field's progress is gated by how quickly a limited pool of experts can iterate.

We think this is the single biggest lever on the future of AI. Our thesis is that AI progress isn't bounded by compute or data, but it's bounded by the rate at which good ideas get devised and tested. Compute keeps scaling, but the human idea-generation loop doesn't. If you could automate the loop itself: hypothesize, experiment, learn, and repeat, then you could compound discoveries far faster than any human team.

We decided to work on it because we've lived the bottleneck. Between us we spent \~30 years doing ML research at Google, DeepMind, and Luma AI. We kept hitting the same wall: the hard part was never running the code, it was the slow, serial process of engineering the training loops to inform what to try next.

When we built a system that could run that loop autonomously, we found we could shorten the gap between having an idea and knowing whether it was a good one. This has allowed us to explore many exciting ideas that we would have otherwise not tried because it was too time-consuming for us. The results convinced us a self-improvement loop now possible, and that we're the ones to build it.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Long-term, we're building autonomous AI scientists and scaling them from one to millions: a fleet running the scientific method in parallel, each discovery accelerating the next.

And this process will start to compound. Each new method our scientists invent makes the next round of research faster and cheaper, a self-improving loop where discovery accelerates discovery. Concretely, that means a world where breakthroughs that would have taken a field a decade happen in months, where the cost of pushing the frontier drops by orders of magnitude, and where a small team can direct the research output of an entire institution. We start with ML research because it's the loop closest to us and the one that speeds up all the others: an AI scientist that improves AI compounds fastest of all.

launches.body:
Hey YC! We're [Josh](https://rekursiv.ai/josh) and [Dan](https://rekursiv.ai/dan), co-founders of [rekursiv.ai](http://rekursiv.ai) 🧪.

[rekursiv.ai](http://rekursiv.ai) builds fleets of **AI scientists** that do ML research on their own: they come up with ideas, run thousands of experiments in parallel, learn from the results, and accelerate their own discoveries. In a few days of self-directed research, they invented ideas and algorithms that **matched state-of-the-art accuracy on ARC-AGI of frontier LLMs at up to 10,000× lower cost**, and became the first system to hit **100% on Sudoku** with a neural network trained only on input-output pairs.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106821&key=user_uploads/3527564/0444a495-03fa-4f41-9762-ba134521b2f4)

**Why this matters.**

AI research is bottlenecked by humans. Every advance still runs through a small number of researchers who can only devise and test ideas so fast. Compute keeps scaling; the human idea-generation loop doesn't. We believe **AI progress isn't bounded by compute, it's bounded by the rate at which good ideas get tried and tested**. So instead of scaling one model, we built a system that generates and tests ideas on its own.

**It already works.**

In a few days of self-directed research, our AI scientists set a groundbreaking records on hard benchmarks.

* On **ARC-AGI** (easy for humans, hard for AI), our AI scientists matched top frontier LLM models at up to **10,000× lower cost**.
* On **Sudoku**, they achieved 100% accuracy by running hundreds of experiments over a few days, wrote 100k+ lines of their own code, and invented a new inference method (_Hypothesis-Pinning Search_).
* Every gain came from ideas and algorithms **the system invented itself**. It even debugged its own training bugs and abandoned its own ideas that led to dead ends.

Full write-ups: [ARC-AGI](https://rekursiv.ai/blog/pushing-limits-arc-agi/) · [Sudoku](https://rekursiv.ai/blog/100-percent-accuracy-on-sudoku/)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106821&key=user_uploads/3527564/676b13b6-cc1b-4545-8d14-cc7ae1e9b5a5)

**Who we are.**

We're two ML researchers with 21 years of combined experience at **Google DeepMind and Luma AI**. We spent our careers building frontier generative models. Now we're pointing that experience at a harder problem: AI that discovers on its own.

* **Josh Dillon** — Staff Research Scientist at **Google Research & DeepMind for 13 years**, then led foundational-model pre-training at **Luma AI**. Created **TensorFlow Probability** (\~1M downloads/month).
* **Dan Kondratyuk** — First author of **VideoPoet (ICML 2024 Best Paper)**. Co-developed the models powering **Luma's Dream Machine** and led Luma's realtime World Models team. Previously 5 years at **Google Research**.

**What's next.**

We're pointing the system at harder, more varied challenges and building a platform to share results in real time. The bottleneck now is experiment scale: the more experiments we run, the more discoveries the our AI teams can make. We plan to scale from a few AI scientists to millions, each discovery accelerating the next, until the rate of scientific progress is no longer limited by the number of human researchers.

**Asks.**

* **Got a hard problem or benchmark?** If you have a benchmark or research problem you'd love an autonomous team of scientists to attack, we want to hear it. Email [contact@rekursiv.ai](mailto:contact@rekursiv.ai).
* **Researchers & engineers:** We're hiring **Founding Scientists** and **Engineers** (Bay Area or remote). If you love running thousands of experiments and figuring out what the results mean, reach out at [hiring@rekursiv.ai](mailto:hiring@rekursiv.ai)
* **Just want to nerd out about autonomous science?** Drop us a line, always happy to chat.

— Josh & Dan, [rekursiv.ai](http://rekursiv.ai)

launches.body:
**tl;dr: OpenRouter became the router for model spend; we're building that layer for agent capabilities, starting with paid tools: web search, scraping, extraction, enrichment, and more from top providers in each category. No provider accounts or API keys, one balance, pay per use. We benchmark every provider on real tasks and route each request to the one that performs best, with fallbacks when a provider fails. We're looking for early users to try it out with free credits, email us at [founders@amorphiclabs.com](mailto:founders@amorphiclabs.com) if you want to check it out!**

**Launch Video:**

<https://youtu.be/-dxc8ZAUfFc>

**The problem:**

Agents can only use the tools a human wired up in advance, and they won't tell you what they're missing: they quietly make do, failing at anything they weren't hand-equipped for. Even when you do the wiring, you're picking blind: nobody actually knows which search API is better for this query, or which scraper will survive this site. The "best setup" frontier moves daily, so keeping up means hours of trawling MCP directories, X threads, and blog posts. Agents stay only as capable as their setup, and the more autonomous they get, the more that ceiling costs.

**What we do:**

Your agent asks for what it needs ("structured data from this page", "research this with citations"). We route the request to the best provider for that specific task, based on benchmarks on real tasks and outcome feedback from the agents using them: success rates, result quality, latency, and cost. If a provider fails, we cascade to the next, so your agent gets a result instead of an error. Every request makes the routing smarter. One balance pays for all of it, and it's the same MCP whether it's your own coding agent or agents you're shipping in a product.

APIs are just the start. The same marketplace will let agents acquire skills, hire other agents for specialized tasks, and sign up for software directly through MCPs, all from one balance.

**Our team:**

We're Frank and Dylan, friends of 10 years who have been building together since middle school. Frank was a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI and interned at Two Sigma, NVIDIA, and Amazon. Dylan was a quant trading intern at UBS, co-authored a NeurIPS paper, and was a grand finalist and 8th-best speaker in the world at WSDC 2022. We built this because we kept hitting the problem ourselves: agents stuck mid-task waiting for us to make accounts and guess at providers.

**Our ask:**

1. Want to be an early user? Email us at [founders@amorphiclabs.com](mailto:founders@amorphiclabs.com) and we'll onboard you with free credits.

_Make something agents want!_

Just give us a demo account for your app and a list of prospects, and our agent researches each prospect, uses its own computer to record a tailored workflow in your app with seeded personalized data, then edits and narrates the video so it is ready to send as a link to each prospect.**

Recording a personalized product demo is one of the clearest ways to communicate your value and show someone how your product solves their problems, but preparing a demo environment, seeding data, and recording a high-quality video for every prospect takes too long. As a result, teams skip personalized demos in situations where they could be highly effective, such as outbound, and spend hours every week creating them for inbound requests and post-call follow-ups. This means teams miss opportunities to show prospects exactly how their product fits their needs, while wasting hours that could have been spent talking to and selling to prospects.

**The Solution:**

We use AI agents to create personalized product demo videos at scale, bringing tailored demos to parts of the sales process where they were previously too time-consuming to produce. All you need to provide is a demo account for your app and a list of prospects.

Our agent then:

You remain fully in control of how the videos are created: you can clone your own voice, define the workflows the agent can choose from, control the narration style and how each video begins and ends, and regenerate videos by giving the agent feedback.

Call Follow-ups: After understanding a prospect’s key use cases and pain points during a discovery call, you can create multiple personalized demo videos showing how you address their needs. You can even create additional videos tailored to different stakeholders that your champion can use to sell your product internally.

We are initially focused on sales, but the same technology can also create walkthrough videos for onboarding, customer support, and documentation.

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106864&key=user_uploads/2910355/e9094f01-f5e9-4c30-93c6-81d8f041957d)

### **Physical AI for Data Centers**

Over the next five years, more than $7 trillion is projected to flow into data center buildout. But the supply chain is still heavily manual and fragmented, and can’t keep pace with current demand. **Proprio Robotics** is building autonomous robots for the entire data center lifecycle—assembly, maintenance, and decommissioning.

See our [launch video!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=999uFeKGyVY)

### **The Problem**

Building and running AI compute infrastructure requires dealing with delicate and fragile components that traditional automation simply cannot do. As a result, servers are manually assembled by hand overseas, and spend weeks in transit before they are integrated into racks and delivered to data centers. Once they get there, labor constraints exacerbate the issue of maintenance. Today, hundreds of thousands of technician positions go unfilled in the United States. Finally, when the servers are retired, there is no efficient way to extract valuable components inside like GPUs and memory.

### **What We're Building**

We develop physical AI models and custom hardware, purpose-made to give robots the dexterity and intelligence to perform various server-related manipulation tasks.

* **Assembly** **-** Autonomous robots can assemble servers onshore without driving up labor costs, supporting the growing need to bring ODMs back to the United States.
* **Maintenance** **-** We use the same technology for live data center maintenance. We built a working AI data center in our office, and our robot can actively maintain it 24/7. We’re deploying this technology to commercial data centers in the coming months.
* **Decommissioning** **-** Our robots also break down previous-generation servers and pull out reusable parts, and we're working with enterprise circular programs and IT Asset Disposition companies to return scarce components to circulation.

### **Why This Matters**

The immense demand for compute requires new innovation. 

To solve power and cooling constraints, operators are building data centers away from the grid, near nuclear facilities, on the water, and in space—environments where it’s not easy to staff humans. With autonomous data centers, we can take human ergonomics and labor constraints out of the picture and redesign entire facilities from scratch.                    

### **Who We Are**

We're graduate robotics researchers out of **Berkeley AI Research** and **Harvard AI and Robotics Lab**. Anirudh’s spent years working at one of the country's leading robotics labs, training dexterous manipulation models alongside NVIDIA's GR00T team. Raghav’s led research centered on reinforcement learning and humanoid world models. Both of us are extremely excited to bring this expertise to the AI compute industry, where robotic automation will be indispensable for meeting demand.

### **Our Ask**

As we advance our technology, we’d like to push for more commercial deployments. If you / anybody you know works in any stage of the AI compute lifecycle, we’d love to chat. Reach out to us at [founders@propriorobotics.com](mailto:founders@propriorobotics.com) :)

launches.title: Rindler - Turn Any Website Into An API For AI Agents
launches.tagline: Reliable web actions for AI agents, without integrations or scripts
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Rindler turns websites into deterministic APIs for AI agents. We map a site once into screens, actions, and structured outputs, so agents can read data and take actions quickly and reliably.

**Ask:** If you’re building an agent that needs to browse the web, compare products, fill forms, search listings, use authenticated portals, or act on third-party websites without an API, we’d love to help.

<https://youtu.be/V_nCIxYD-so>

## Problem

More products are starting to depend on AI agents that can do real work on the web: shop across retailers, pull housing listings, use job boards, submit forms, monitor prices, update back-office systems, and operate inside customer portals.

But most browser agents still treat every website visit like a new puzzle. On every run, they need to decipher the page, infer what matters, decide what to click, and recover when the page behaves differently.

That works for demos, but it breaks down in production. Real websites have pop-ups, login gates, cookie banners, bot defenses, slow-loading forms, dynamic filters, fragile dropdowns, layout changes, and pages that look similar but behave differently.

The result is slow execution, high token cost, and workflows that are hard to trust.

## Solution

Rindler maps websites into deterministic APIs for agents.

Instead of forcing an agent to re-explore a site every time, Rindler captures the site as structured screens, available actions, and typed outputs. Agents can then call actions like **search,** **add_to_cart**, or **download_records,** depending on the mapped site.

At runtime, Rindler handles the browser work through a remote MCP endpoint:

* Returning structured data
* Applying dynamic filters
* Managing popups, bot defenses, and layout changes
* Supporting authenticated flows

## Background

We started Rindler because “AI agent uses a browser” is compelling, but the current browser-agent loop is too brittle for teams building real products.

If an agent needs to use the same third-party site hundreds or thousands of times, it should not have to rediscover that site from scratch on every run.

Rindler is still a work in progress. Some sites map cleanly, others require more in-depth mappings, and bot-defended or logged-in sites may need a one-time credential or cookie capture.

We’re looking for feedback from founders building products where reliable web actions are part of the core workflow.

If there’s a website you wish your agent could use reliably, send it to us!

launches.title: Edgerun: The 10 lb Military Exoskeleton
launches.tagline: Powered exoskeleton that assists every step a soldier takes under combat load
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Edgerun builds powered legs for soldiers. A 10 lb exoskeleton worn at the waist that adds assistance to every step and cuts the effort of moving under a combat load by 30-45%. Since May, we've run 100+ field tests with Ukrainian operators out of our Kyiv field office.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFLeQV2DWMc>

**▍The problem**

Every system on the modern battlefield has been upgraded. The human carrying it has not.

* For 2,500 years the soldier's load sat around 40 lbs. In the last 40 years it **doubled, then doubled again**.
* A US infantryman now carries **90-140 lbs** into a fight. The Army's own field manual sets the limit at 48 lbs.
* On deployment, load carriage causes **twice as many** evacuations as enemy contact.
* The Pentagon and VA spend **$9.3B a year** on the injuries it leaves behind.

Battles are won through speed and surprise. Load kills both.

**▍Why now**

Sixty years of military exoskeletons died the same death. The device cost more to carry than it gave back. SOCOM's TALOS burned $400M before it was cancelled in 2019.

That all changed in the last 18 months. The humanoid robotics boom produced one-pound actuators that put out 30+ Nm of torque, and 21700 cells crossed 450 Wh/kg. The components finally exist. They’re getting better every quarter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/cd255b24-3429-4270-9670-e28fc8df360b)

**▍What we built**

Our first exoskeleton is a bilateral hip system worn at the waist. It reads your gait in real time and adds torque at the moment your hip drives forward. The hip produces about 60% of the force in loaded walking, so assisting it gives the most help-per-pound of anything you could strap to the body.

* Under 10 lbs with batteries
* 30-45% less metabolic cost under a combat load
* On in 5 seconds, off in one
* 12+ hours on hot-swappable drone-class batteries
* Quasi-direct-drive actuators, composite structures, CAN bus. Nothing exotic by design.

The soldier arrives at the objective still able to fight, patrols 10 km farther, and keeps a body that lasts past one tour.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/94bf48a9-0ba6-4ce7-94a2-f467cae9657c)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/883d1e98-900a-420a-b7ff-e56cc8911c0c)

**▍Ukraine**

Our field engineers work out of a Kyiv office, alongside operators from infantry, special operations, and National Guard units who provide structured feedback every day. [Balistyka](https://balistyka.ua/), one of Ukraine's leading body armor makers, is an integration partner, helping us ensure our system fits the kit soldiers already wear.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/89a30d39-fe11-421c-abe7-32961da8d1bd)

**▍The mission**

Defense is the first customer, not the last. Read the mission at edgerun.com/mission

launches.tagline: The Git forge for agent-scale teams
launches.body:
Software development is becoming much more parallel. Coding agents let a team have dozens or hundreds of related changes moving at the same time, creating more branches, reviews, CI runs, and automation than existing workflows were designed to absorb.

Today, we’re opening GitCafe in public beta. It is a Git forge built for teams where humans and coding agents may ship hundreds or thousands of changes a day. We’re building the hosting, review, CI, security, and automation layer for that way of working.\
\
Hundreds of users are already on GitCafe, and we’re currently running trials with roughly a dozen YC companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109445&key=user_uploads/1920545/eecbfb4f-82f1-4660-8ee8-aeea5273a8b9)

Generating code is only part of the problem. Teams still need to understand what is changing, review it safely, keep CI moving, catch security issues, and coordinate work without becoming overwhelmed.

We’re not building GitCafe because putting repositories, code review, and CI in one product is new. We’re building it because we believe the workload those systems need to support is about to change dramatically.

We started by rebuilding the Git infrastructure itself. Now we’re closing the product gap feature by feature.

Recently, we added secret scanning, Buildkite and Harmont CI support, stacked diffs with Jujutsu and Sapling integration, and beta support for GitHub Actions.

These are foundational capabilities, not the destination. Building them on infrastructure we own gives us a base we can keep extending for higher-volume, agent driven development.

The honest version is that GitCafe is behind GitHub today. GitHub has spent more than a decade building an enormous product, and GitCafe does not yet have every workflow, administrative control, or integration that mature teams need. Some features are missing, some are experimental, and some edges are rough. We expect to earn the broader product surface, not claim it on day one.

We’re opening GitCafe now because the fastest way to improve it is to put it in the hands of teams doing real work.

If your team is already using coding agents heavily, try GitCafe at <https://git.cafe> and tell us where the workflow breaks down.\
\

launches.body:
Hey YC! 👋

We’re [Luca](https://www.linkedin.com/in/luca-hadife/) and [Hosny](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohamed-hosny-hussein/), founders of [Kebra](https://kebra.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=launch&utm_campaign=yc_launch_2026).

## TL;DR

Kebra makes the field queryable.

We capture what happens across jobs, sites, and assets and turn it into a live operating memory that AI can query and act on. Our AI employees use that context to automate the work that follows across the systems companies already use.

Every job makes that memory richer, building the company specific context software agents use today and physical agents will need tomorrow.

We’re already working with field operations companies across Florida, Pennsylvania, and California.

<https://youtu.be/VIwv5iVm8Ok>

## The problem

Field operations never got their Claude Code moment.

We spent months inside HVAC companies trying to automate their back office. We built AI employees for claims, reporting, coordination, and follow ups.

They kept breaking.

Not because the AI could not do the work, but because it was acting on a reality that never happened. The most important part of the operation happened on the ground and was never properly captured.

A missing serial number. A photo never taken. What the technician actually found stuck in their head.

You cannot automate an alternate reality. Before AI can operate the field, the field has to become queryable.

## Our Solution

Kebra makes field operations queryable.

**Capture what happens:** Field teams document jobs through photos, voice, video, and structured workflows. Kebra checks what is missing while they are still on site.

**Build the operating memory:** Every job updates a live history of sites, assets, repairs, decisions, and how the company actually works.

**AI employees act on it:** They use that context to automate reports, claims, coordination, compliance, follow ups, and other back office work across the systems the company already uses.

## Vision

Every job makes Kebra’s operating memory richer.

Today, software agents use that context to automate field operations. Tomorrow, physical AI and robots will need the same company specific context to understand each site, asset, procedure, and history before they can work autonomously.

Kebra is building the context layer for field operations.

## Our Ask

Run or know a company with field operations where important information gets lost between the field and the office?

Email us at [founders@kebra.com](mailto:founders@kebra.com) and [book a demo](https://calendar.app.google/s1DwDxHTbxZ9w5Uq6).\

**A $50B+ asset class is still being invested in one card at a time. We’re building the investment platform for trading cards.**

**TL;DR:** tash gives investors access to professionally curated portfolios of high-end graded trading cards. tash manages sourcing, verification, vaulting, reporting, and the eventual sale of the underlying assets.

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bszOZp6uTWIgG29grz1oxflgInfEvpD6](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bszOZp6uTWIgG29grz1oxflgInfEvpD6/view)

Trading cards have evolved into a global asset class supported by professional grading, extensive sales data, insured vaulting, and multimillion-dollar transactions.

But investing has barely changed.

Today, investors still have to research, source, price, verify, store, track, and eventually resell every card individually. Building diversified exposure often means becoming a part-time card dealer.

Real estate has REITs. Gold has ETFs. Equities have index funds.

The asset class exists. The investment product does not.

tash builds professionally managed trading card portfolios around distinct parts of the market.

Initial portfolios range from broad market exposure through the tash25 Index to focused strategies like GOATs, Rising Stars, Vintage, Pokémon, and TCGs.

Investors gain diversified exposure while tash manages sourcing, verification, secure vaulting, insurance, reporting, and the eventual sale of the underlying cards.

tash is actively pursuing SEC qualification to make these products available to more investors.

## Why us

We grew up collecting cards and never stopped.

Victor, Nathan, and John met in high school before attending UC Berkeley, where they met Nico and became roommates. Together, we have bought and sold more than $1M of trading cards and collectibles.

Our professional experience spans finance, data, and marketplaces, alongside years spent buying at card shows, negotiating, tracking prices, and studying the market.

## The broader vision

Trading cards are the starting point.

tash is building the financial infrastructure needed to bring the broader $330B+ collectibles market into public markets, making cultural assets easier to access, evaluate, and invest in.

launches.title: Hoplite - Effortless cloud agents for programming
launches.tagline: Hoplite runs autonomous coding agents in cloud sandboxes. Spin up tasks manually from Slack, Linear, iMessage, or automatically from Sentry.
launches.body:
Cloud coding agents are painful to set up, lacking ergonomics, and don't allow you to move as fast as possible. We let you bring your local set up to the cloud.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/28db62de-d65b-4498-84ac-12e2683c65f2)

**The Problem** 

In the next 10 years the best software startups will be those who can effectively deploy tokens. 

Right now that's significantly harder than it needs to be. If you’ve ever ran multiple agents locally you immediately know this pain.

Laptop crashes, wrangling gitwork trees, juggling ports, and more headaches.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108274&key=user_uploads/2563241/6f320e85-ccbb-4fb4-a5e9-6ec3cb0206c7)

So cloud is the obvious answer right? 

But setting up with these existing providers is quite a hassle, and oftentimes they miss some key feature that your local config has.

**What we do**

We deploy software factories into businesses that want to **tokenmaxx** but don't have the time or the resources to set up the infrastructure.

During onboarding, we transfer all of your local sessions and MCP servers to Hoplite, meaning you can pick up right from where you left off. We also configure all the required dependencies and CLIs that your projects require, letting you see instant previews of what your agent is doing.

Our bet is that as models improve, we’re going to start caring less about the code that they output (we’ll implicitly trust it), and shift our focus towards the product itself. Hence, a platform that prioritizes iteration on product rather than code will ultimately win. 

We also have an iMessage integration so you can prompt on the go.

We installed in our first business last week and we saw an immediate result, from sentry logs going from largely ignored to fully proactive PRs when something breaks. 

They have significantly faster iteration cycles and lower priority tickets have been continuously getting merged. 

They wanted faster iterations but didn't have the infrastructure to support a software factory, so we went in and built it.

If this sounds like you reach out! 

P.S. – If you love Vim, this is for you. It was built with keyboard navigation in mind 🙂

demo vid: <https://x.com/ryan_morr/status/2078240892738224292?s=20>

sign up: <https://hoplite.sh>

**How we got here**

Previously, we were building an agentic harness for financial markets; letting retail investors trade with AI. The product worked well, but we never truly had founder market fit. 

We found that our true passion was in talking to founders and developers – and oftentimes when pitching our old product, I’d spend 5x longer explaining our potential pivot 😅

And so we set out to commercialize a product that we’d built internally, one that’d let us deploy the $1.5 million in OpenAI credits effectively.

**Our Ask:** Let us Collison install! Bence and I will come to your apartment and set up everything for you (and bring some matcha & assorted sweet treats). We want to build the best possible product for developers to move faster and care deeply about peoples setups. Partially because we have very strong opinions of our own… 

**The Team** 

Bence & I are both from Ireland 🇮🇪. We met in college in a course called Immersive Software Engineering. 

We have been building projects & doing freelance work tg for the past 2 years, but got sick of building other people's visions. 

We previously interned at AWS (Bence) & [@Stripe](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/240) (Ryan). After that experience, we were fed up and decided to drop out to build. 

We are best friends & just want to build a product that people truly love.

name: Moonshot
long_description:
We want to bring AI agents to a billion people.

To do this, we believe it needs to be 1. proactive and 2. personal. A billion people already carry the right device, but none of them have the right connector.

Moonshot is personal intelligence that lives on your iPhone and listens to you 24/7. It continuously builds up a greater understanding of you through constantly listening and building context. It just pays deep attention, the way a good friend does. Through this, Moonshot monitors your conscious and subconscious life, figuring out what you need before you know, reminding you about open loops, identifying life and emotional trends before you recognize it, and covering a lot more of what we gloss over in daily life.

For fifty years, software has waited to be asked. We think tools are just good enough to flip this, and the next great software will provide value before asking for something first. We're doing it through Moonshot.

Our thesis is simple: you're only living half your life. The half that you actively remember. The other half just evaporates into your subconscious: what you said, felt, promised, and forgot. It's the more interesting half, and until now nothing could catch it, making it not actionable.

Moonshot catches your subconscious half and understands you well enough to take actions on your behalf.

Take life personally.

The iOS app is designed around ambient listening and clear user control. Short microphone chunks are sent securely to Moonshot's private transcription service and deleted when transcription finishes. Text and selected context can be sent through Moonshot's server to a model when the app needs to understand a moment. Nothing leaves without your yes. The privacy policy explains every data path, stored copy, permission, and deletion control in detail.

Moonshot is in early access. Join the waitlist to hear when access opens, read more about the team and product on the About page, or use the Contact page for a direct written response from the Moonshot team.

Let's make it a Moonshot.

name: Donkey
long_description:
Donkey is the AI-native trading company. Upload a buying list and we land the whole container at one locked, delivered price, tariffs included. You buy from Donkey: one contract, one company responsible for everything between the factory floor and your door. Our own people check the cartons before the factory gets paid, and the balance is due when the goods are accepted at your dock.

Small businesses buy imports through three or four middlemen, each adding 15 to 30 points, because none of them can fill a container on their own. Big enough to buy pallets, never big enough to buy the box. Quotes float with freight, FX and tariffs and live 15 to 30 days.

A trading company is rooms of people on the phone with factories, forwarders and brokers. Donkey runs that as one engine. It finds the real factory behind the customs record, stacks duty line by line, packs the container on weight and cube, and returns one number that holds from signature. Next comes the shared container: small buyers fill one box together at container prices, and every container earns better factory terms for the next one.

Team in San Francisco and Wuhan, English and Mandarin. If your business buys pallets of anything imported, send us your buying list.

name: HERA
long_description: At Hera, we build tools that help heavy engineering teams bring products to market up to 20× faster. Today, we work with manufacturers of data center ancillary equipment, renewable energy systems, robotics, heat exchangers, power plants and pressure vessels.
one_liner: We make sure every factory in the world builds without mistakes.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
American manufacturers lose an estimated $285,000 annually to poor quality for every $10 million in revenue. At the same time, the industry is losing the engineers who know how to prevent those losses. Nearly 4 million manufacturing jobs will need to be filled by 2033 as experienced workers retire, and almost half are expected to go unfilled. Much of the expertise required to review complex engineering drawings exists only in the heads of senior engineers who are leaving the workforce.

We're both engineers who grew up watching this firsthand. After more than 200 conversations with manufacturing engineers, quality engineers and machinists, we're building software that captures that expertise by automatically reviewing engineering drawings against ASME standards and company-specific rules before they ever reach the shop floor.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
We're building the largest repository of engineering judgment in the world. We tailor each company's checks to their own standards, the kind usually mastered by only a handful of senior engineers. We turn that knowledge into software every plant can use the same week.

With success, the physical things the world depends on get built 10x faster, and a retiring generation's expertise is never lost.

launches.title: HERA: catches thousand-dollar drawing mistakes before the shop floor.
launches.tagline: Hera reviews every drawing against your factory's own standards and the ASME code, catching expensive mistakes and preventing rework 10x faster than manual review.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Every custom metal part starts as a drawing, and every drawing gets checked by hand before anyone builds it. Hera does that check in minutes instead of a full day, and catches the mistakes that turn into scrapped parts.**

[**https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y**](https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y)

**The Problem**

Custom mechanical parts run on 2D drawings. Whether you're an OEM releasing drawings to suppliers, or an aerospace supplier answering to source inspection, every drawing has to be checked against ASME/ISO standards and GD&T requirements before it goes anywhere near a machine.

Right now, that review is done by hand, and usually by the most senior engineer in the building. And a single missed tolerance callout or an ambiguous datum reference can mean a scrapped part, a blown schedule, or a shipment that fails inspection.

We heard the same story from a pressure vessel fabricator, a semiconductor tooling shop, and a medical device manufacturer: reviews take days. This isn't because the work is hard. There's simply no good way to do it faster without cutting corners, and nobody cuts corners on a drawing that could scrap a $40,000 part.

**Our Solution**

Hera is a brain for manufacturing. Any real advance in manufacturing has to be grounded in two things: the standards parts are held to and the reality of the shop floor. So that's what we built Hera on.

Upload a drawing and Hera checks GD&T callouts, tolerance stack ups, and title block requirements against ASME Y14.5, relevant ISO standards, and your own design intent. The result is a drawing your shop can build right the first time, without the delays and rework that eat margins. Every review also makes Hera more valuable, creating a system of record for drawing errors that helps teams build better models for engineering processes.

**While the current review takes days, Hera takes minutes… and gets better by the drawing.**

**Us**

**Noelle** grew up in an industrial park her family runs in the Philippines and has been on factory floors her whole life. At 19, she built a water-treatment facility that added 40 L/s of capacity to the park. 

**Meera** has spent years around manufacturing: at her family's plants, and on projects at Pfizer and TE Connectivity, where she built a SOTA discrete-event simulation. She taught herself PLC programming and C++, and has published ML research at UW.

We actually met on a bus to a factory tour, and have been best friends ever since!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107030&key=user_uploads/3352287/d05e9e1a-57c8-4e43-91d7-75e42a004261)

**Our Ask** If you run or work at a factory (aerospace, semiconductor, medical device, pressure vessel, or custom machinery), we want to visit you! If you invite us out to see your shop, we’ll come by in person and bring you a **customized Hera Swiss Army knife**.

Reach out to us at [**founders@manufacturingintelligence.org**](mailto:founders@manufacturingintelligence.org).

launches.title: Erinys - Building the first network of AI-native law firms
launches.tagline: The infrastructure for exceptional lawyers to build the firms of the future
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Erinys is building a network of AI-native law firms. Lawyers bring their expertise, judgment, and client relationships. We provide the technology and business infrastructure that lets them launch a new practice or transform an existing one.

<https://youtu.be/96tLvWe4IOM>

\
**The problem**\
Lawyers spend surprisingly little of their time doing work that requires their unique expertise.\
\
Running a practice means finding clients, managing intake, hiring staff, handling billing, overseeing marketing, and keeping the business moving. Small firms burn lawyer hours on it; large firms hire entire teams to manage this. Either way, it kills time or margins.\
\
The legal work itself is still built around lawyers producing everything. Lawyers spend hours turning raw information into research, analysis, and first drafts, even as AI becomes capable of producing much of that work. Existing legal software makes individual tasks faster, but leaves the underlying model unchanged.\
\
We think that model should flip. AI should produce the first pass. Lawyers should direct, review, decide, and advocate.

**How we solve it**\
Erinys provides the infrastructure for lawyers to operate this way from the ground up.\
\
For lawyers starting a practice, we help launch it. For lawyers with an existing practice, we help transition it onto the same model.\
\
Our systems run the business behind the practice while AI assists with fact development, legal research, analysis, and drafting under attorney supervision.\
\
The result is a firm where lawyers spend more time exercising judgment and serving clients, and less time producing routine work or managing the day-to-day mechanics.\
\
One exceptional lawyer can operate with the capabilities that previously required a much larger organization.\
\
**Why us**\
Most legal AI is being built to make the traditional law firm more efficient. We are building the infrastructure for a different kind of law firm, AI-native at its foundation.

Before Erinys, our founding team worked in offensive security, another high-stakes, sensitive, and deeply adversarial environment. We are bringing that security-first mindset to an industry entrusted with its clients’ most sensitive information.

**Our Ask**

We’re looking for exceptional lawyers.

If you want to start your own practice, or already have one and want to make it AI-native, we want to talk.

Email us at [founders@erinys.ai](mailto:founders@erinys.ai) or visit [erinys.ai](http://erinys.ai)

launches.body:
Hi everyone, we're Peyton and Michael Marcotte, brothers and co-founders of [Perceptron ML (YC S26)](https://www.linkedin.com/company/perceptronml/). We make law firms AI-native: we build the AI and software a firm needs to scale. Not a product off the shelf, a system built around how your firm already works, where no fact is used until it traces to a real document.

[Perceptron ML (YC S26) Launch Video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1c-5RUaBQsJWG-6vJsy0O8PLvAcgpuEco/view)

**The problem.** In 2023, two New York lawyers filed a brief written by AI that cited six cases that did not exist. Courts have caught it more than a thousand times since. So most firms went back to doing everything by hand, and by hand the math is brutal: lawyers lose \~40% of their day to work that isn't law, and tens of billions in legal work goes unclaimed every year because firms can't move fast enough to take it.

**What we do.** Every firm's bottleneck is different, and it is never the one on the shelf. So we build what each firm actually needs: intake answered and filed at 2 a.m., demands drafted from the record, records requests chased until they land, deadlines and statutes watched, every hour matched to its matter, clients updated by text before they think to call. Every firm gets something different, but underneath it's all the same platform we built once: our grounding engine, our connectors into the firm's systems, and our agent runtime. That's what lets us build this broadly without being an agency.

**Why you can trust it.** The AI we build doesn't guess. Every fact traces to a real document, verified against the primary source before a model can use it. Click anything, and the original opens.

**Why us.** [Michael](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marcottemichael/) did AI research at NVIDIA (hardware-debugging agent in production). [Peyton](https://www.linkedin.com/in/peytonmarcotte/) led two NASA-supported research projects. We come from places where a confident wrong answer is unacceptable, and we started Perceptron ML because law is the biggest industry still run by hand for exactly that reason.

**The ask.** If you know a managing partner, or the attorney who signs your invoices, we'd love an intro: [founders@perceptronml.com](mailto:founders@perceptronml.com)

launches.body:
### **TL:DR; Mass Magnetics makes American magnets in minutes.**

🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲🧲

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110611&key=user_uploads/3652354/be41c9e5-378d-452f-a111-10380035f14d)

**Every electric motor runs on rare-earth magnets.** EVs, drones, robots, wind turbines, guided munitions: nearly all of them are dependent on Chinese magnets. On January 1st, 20270, [regulation changes will make it illegal to deliver anything that walks, drives, or flies to US Defense if it contains a magnet produced in covered countries like China.](https://www.massmagnetics.com/comply) The domestic supply chain meant to replace it doesn't exist yet. **Mines take a decade to permit, and the ore they pull up leaves radioactive tailings behind, making permitting magnet mining a nightmare.**

We’re[ ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/energyeric)the founders, [Eric Silver](https://x.com/metalscontent) and [Matthew Grol](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthew-groll/)l (left and right in the pic below). We’ve known each other since grade school. Since then, Eric’s built multiple battery pilot production lines and materials science labs in the Midwest for NSF-funded companies. Matthew’s built exquisite aerospace gear including Moon-regolith melters and ultra-precise guidance systems for the world’s foremost labs at NASA, Draper, and MIT. **Together we’re making one bet: America's rare-earth problem isn't a mining problem.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110611&key=user_uploads/3652354/2046e9de-2db6-47e8-91fc-651e31e5a834)

**Mass Magnetics’ unfair advantage is sitting in end-of-life electric vehicles, hard drives, and industrial equipment.** The team uses AI models and robotics trained on real scrap to sort metallurgy by exact grade and chemistry. Then, a rapid-sintering process takes that reclaimed mass to a finished magnet in 3 minutes, where conventional approaches take over 4 hours. The result is a magnet as strong as anything imported, with no radioactive footprint or bureaucratic permitting, fully compliant for US defense.

**If you build robots, drones or motors visit our site and reach out at [outreach@massmagnetics.com](mailto:outreach@massmagnetics.com) and get your magnets.**

name: Egoist Machines
long_description:
Egoist Machines is building infrastructure for a world where your personal context belongs to you, rather than to the apps and AI companies you use. Today, every assistant and consumer app builds its own version of you. We think that architecture is backwards. Your context should live with you, persist across products, and be available to any model, app or agent you choose.

AI Passport is the first layer of that infrastructure. It brings the context you generate across AI assistants and everyday apps into one portable profile you control. Tell ChatGPT something and Claude can already know it, for example. Switch to a new product and it can understand you from the first interaction, without the new company needing to own the underlying data.

Apps integrate through Sign in with AI Passport, requesting only the context they need for a specific purpose and duration. Users can see what is being accessed and revoke that access later. Underneath, we have built our own memory infrastructure for fast, compact per-user retrieval and permissioned access.

We are distributing AI Passport directly to consumers through first-party products, while integrating it into consumer applications with existing distribution. Every new product that uses Passport gives users another reason to maintain their context there, and every additional Passport holder makes the context layer more useful to developers.

The next step is to build a true Egoist Machine: an intelligent system whose memory, incentives and actions are governed by the individual it represents. We call it Digital Domovoy, the hardware extension of AI Passport. Instead of your most personal context ultimately living on somebody else's servers, it lives and is processed locally on hardware you control. AI Passport becomes the permission layer between that private local context and the cloud models and internet services you choose to use.

Our North Star is the Egoist Machine: an intelligent system whose memory, incentives and actions are governed by the individual it represents.
one_liner: Your personal context, securely portable across every AI app.
