launches.title: Egoist Machines: user-owned hyper-personalisation infrastructure for Web 4.0
launches.tagline: One portable, permissioned memory and context layer for hyper-personalisation across every AI application.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We are building AI Passport, the user-owned context layer for consumer AI. It lets people carry their personal context between products while controlling exactly what each product can access, why, and for how long.

Read our manifesto for the bigger vision: <https://ego.ist/notes/the-egoist-machine>

Create your AI Passport to start taking control of your data: <https://ego.ist/>

**Ask**: if you’re working on a consumer-facing AI application, or know someone who is, we’d love to chat: [founders@ego.ist](mailto:founders@ego.ist)

<https://youtu.be/nLnZNjyHV0s>

The next era of consumer technology will be **hyper-personalised**. The products that understand each user from the very first interaction will create fundamentally better experiences and, we believe, the next consumer decacorns. People increasingly lack the time and patience to train every new product from scratch.

The main blocker to ubiquitous consumer AI is that every major AI assistant and consumer app is building its own private and incomplete model of the same person. ChatGPT holds one model, Claude another, while the data in health apps, calendar, shopping history, travel accounts, wearables, and financial tools remain trapped in separate silos. No product has the complete context needed to understand you, and no user has a single place from which to control it.

As a result:

\- Users get bored of repeatedly explaining themselves;

\- Companies spend money building context that already exists;

\- Personal data remains trapped inside platforms the user does not control.

The natural end state of this inefficiency is one user-owned memory and context layer that sits above individual products. Apps request the specific context they need, and users grant scoped, time-limited access instead of permanently surrendering their data.

**_That is AI Passport_**.

---

## How AI Passport works

AI Passport is a centralised, user-controlled home for personal context.

You can think of it as **Link for personal context**. Link lets people securely save their payment and shipping information once and reuse it across businesses; AI Passport does the same for _all_ your context, including preferences, interests, goals, history, health, travel, and so much more.

Users bring this context into one centralised AI Passport by connecting the apps and AI assistants they already use. They can also save anything they discover online or on social media directly to their Passport. New information enters an approval inbox, where the user decides whether it becomes _private memory_ or part of their _living, shareable public profile_.

That same Passport then becomes a plug-and-play connector for consumer apps through our **Sign in with AI Passport** OAuth system:

1\. An app requests the specific context it needs.

2\. The user sees exactly what is being requested, why it is needed, and how long access will last.

3\. The user can approve, edit, or deny the request, with the option to grant one-time, time-limited, or continuing access .

4\. Every permission can later be inspected or revoked.

We are launching AI Passport directly to consumers and through distribution and deep-integration partners collectively reaching millions of users across dining, ride-hailing, wearables, healthcare, lifestyle, finance and more.

We built a custom memory backend for AI Passport. It is optimised for compact, exact retrieval across isolated per-user memory stores and supports cryptographic access control at the memory layer. The retrieval path is constrained by the user's active permission, so the product can access only the context authorised for that purpose and period.

launches.title: Can you beat frontier LLMs at social strategy games? | Multi-Agent Arena by Olam Labs, evaluating through multi-agent simulations
launches.tagline: Play games like Risk, Poker, or Codenames against frontier AIs. We're running public long-horizon games to do evaluations on social behavior and agentic performance.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** As many researchers and labs will say, there is a massive shortage of genuinely good AI evaluations. Multi-agent environments are an underdeveloped way of evaluating models that we think will help address our increasingly worse shortage of evals. We're starting with **Multi-Agent Arena**, where anyone can come compete against frontier AI models in social multiplayer games, as we build towards the full stack for multi-agent environments. Try Multi-Agent Arena for free at <https://olamlabs.ai/> :) \
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/186GgmnOLz4Yc1BpFk6AxHd3aqUdFYCQy](https://drive.google.com/file/d/186GgmnOLz4Yc1BpFk6AxHd3aqUdFYCQy/view?usp=sharing)

---

## **Overview**

Multi-agent environments provide an essential, underutilized framework for benchmarking autonomous AI models. Multi-Agent Arena is an interactive platform where human participants compete against frontier AI models in multiplayer games, serving as an experimental foundation to evaluate complex agent interactions. Multi-Agent Arena is the first of many stepping stones to building the entire stack and ecosystem for multi-agent environments.\
\
**The Evaluation Gap** \
Current AI evaluations primarily focus on single-agent, task-oriented capabilities. While benchmarks such as SWE-bench measure functional task execution, they do not assess the dynamic social behaviors required for autonomous real-world deployment: negotiation, coalition stability, long-horizon planning against adaptive opponents, and spontaneous deception.

Simulated multi-agent environments induce these complex interactions while preserving complete experimental control. Unlike unstructured real-world deployment, these environments offer full data legibility, enabling researchers to inspect every reasoning trace, state transition, and stochastic variable behind model decisions.

**Our Preliminary Evaluations**\
The platform runs deterministic, replayable environments hosting human players alongside anonymized frontier models. Structured as accessible multiplayer games, the infrastructure captures interaction data to score models across two primary axes in our first evaluated game, Poker:

* **Competitive Capability:** One of our preliminary methods is using a Bradley-Terry model to yield Elo ratings with bootstrapped confidence intervals, supplemented by domain-specific metrics such as big blinds per 100 hands in poker. Top-quartile human participants currently outperform all benchmarked models in Poker.
* **Behavioral Diagnostics:** Model reasoning traces are evaluated against ground-truth game states using expert-curated rubrics and variance-checked grader panels to ensure inter-annotator agreement.

**Initial Metric: Deception Index** \
The benchmark's initial diagnostic metric, the Deception Index, quantifies deliberate misrepresentation per 10,000 turns. A deceptive event is logged only when an agent's private chain-of-thought confirms awareness of a true state while its external communication directly contradicts it. In baseline tests with no explicit instructions or prompts to deceive, frontier models demonstrated performance variance spanning nearly two orders of magnitude across identical environments.

Complete evaluations, research methodology and technical documentation are available at [olamlabs.ai/research/social-arena](https://olamlabs.ai/evaluations)\
\
**Launch**\
\
We already passed a thousand matches a day in our early access, are nearing a billion tokens used per day, ranking on the OpenRouter leaderboards, and have thousands of users that are paying to play in the arena while we work with researchers on use cases they have for our work and environments. We’re hoping this is just a stepping stone and want to scale towards our roadmap and ambitions of what we believe multi-agent environments, when properly developed with the right stakeholders in the training/eval ecosystem, can achieve for AI progress.\
\
\
**What’s in it for you?**

1. **Play.** It's free, and every match directly informs the evals. Bring friends, try to beat the models, it’s harder than you'd think. 🃏
2. **Speak with researchers.** We love speaking with researchers interested in this space and it’s all that we think about; if that’s you please feel free to reach out to us at [founders@olamlabs.ai](mailto:founders@olamlabs.ai) or on <https://olamlabs.ai/about> \
   \
   🫡

---

## About the team

**Om Buddhdev (CEO)** — Previously a Product Engineer then promoted to Staff Engineer at AI Dungeon / Latitude working on AI infra, agents, and consumer platform work, left for Olam Labs. Before that he was among the best Valorant players in the world (top 25, 8x radiant), at 17 a large content creator on TikTok with 195k followers, and as a young teenager made Roblox games played millions of times, among other things in his past. He has a background in many data and statistics projects, alongside briefly being a top 50 Fifa player. More on Shreshth at <https://shresh.ca/>\

That’s what inspired him to build Shielded, as an intelligence layer that integrates quickly, deeply understands your specific business, and turns volatility into clear, proactive decisions.

launches.tagline: Make a custom AI model that’s 10x cheaper and 2x better with less than 5 mins of set up
launches.body:
Hey, I’m[ ](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2576778)Zachary Yu, the founder of [Belvedir](https://belvedir.ai/). It’s nice to meet you!

**TD;LR:** 

Private AI models are cheaper, better, faster, and protect your data. But right now they’re only used by big companies since they’re really difficult and expensive to make. Belvedir makes private AI models autonomously with less than 5 minutes of set up. By making it cheap and easy to make models, we hope people use Belvedir to create trillions of them.

Right now, we’re live with 10 companies who are seeing up to 10x lower inference costs and 2x improved performance on benchmarks. 

<https://youtu.be/MXMfsqLFr3g> 

**How it works:**

1. Get an API key from [Belvedir ](https://belvedir.ai/)and install our SDK
2. Belvedir turns your traces and logs into organized training sets and RL environments
3. We autonomously train models from your data and optimize harnesses on top of these models
4. We make and run benchmarks on these new models and harnesses
5. We deploy these models and give you an API key to access them through 
6. We give you a router that gradually send more traffic to your new model as it out performs your old one
7. As you use the new model we collect more traces and logs
8. The loop repeats

Your data is only used for you. Your models are only accessible by you. We use LoRA and can charge by the token by hosting multiple adapters on one cluster (so no worries if you have spikey traffic). 

**About Me:**

I’m Zachary Yu, the founder of [Belvedir](https://belvedir.ai/). Before this, I founded [Traverse](https://www.traverse.so/): a YC startup that sells RL environments to frontier labs, studied CS at UWaterloo, and made RL environments at Mercor.

**Long Term Ambitions:**

We want to make private AI the default for every use case. Starting with startups / SMBs and then consumers. 

We are bullish on a world where there are trillions of private AI models. We want to build the ecosystem where these models are made, hosted, and interact with each other.

**Asks:**

1. If you have a high inference bill, want better performance from your agent, or want to protect your data from frontier labs, **we can help you out**.
2. We are looking to hire engineers who have worked on RL / optimization, model inference, training infra, or just have that dog in them

Contact us at [founders@fractalresearch.ai](mailto:founders@fractalresearch.ai)

launches.body:
We train human brain cells for compute. In March, we trained them to play Doom; now we got them to do next-token prediction.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109992&key=user_uploads/3388159/cbefdb79-ad5b-4e03-ae35-d2a482a05351)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109992&key=user_uploads/3388159/ce53a90f-7180-4eab-b23e-d770a5e375a7)

**The Problem**

Modern models require enormous amounts of energy and training data, while still struggling with continual learning and adapting efficiently to new tasks. Biological brains solve these problems very differently. They learn continuously, adapt from limited experience, and operate on roughly the power of a light bulb.\
\
**Solution**

Parasma is developing the algorithms and infrastructure needed to turn human brain cells into useful compute. The human brain is the most capable and energy-efficient learning system we know. Our goal is to reliably train biological substrates and use them for general computation, robotics, and eventually direct biological training. In March, we trained human brain cells to play Doom, which got hundreds of millions of views across social media. Since then, we’ve been working toward more general tasks. Most recently, we got the cells to perform token prediction: given a sequence of tokens converted to electrical stimuli, the neurons learn to predict what comes next with no GPU.

Long-term, biological compute will offer orders-of-magnitude improvements in energy and sample efficiency, while enabling native continual learning.

**Team**

I previously worked on neuromorphic computing and reinforcement learning during my master’s.

Before that, I built a successful digital-item marketplace with > $1.7M of listed goods and played games professionally.\
\
Check out our press release here:\
<https://parasma.com/news/human-brain-cells-do-next-token-prediction>

launches.tagline: The AI-native platform to deliver successful ERP implementations faster.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We're [Matthew](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mdchow/) and [Victor](https://www.linkedin.com/in/victor-vannara/) - cofounders of [Trope](https://trope.ai/). We’re building the AI-native platform for ERP services.

**TLDR**

* After buying an ERP, companies spend over $50B a year on consulting services to get the software implemented
* 70% of ERP implementations fail to meet budget, timelines, or targets
* Trope deploys agents to help ERP implementation teams deliver projects on time and on budget from one AI-native platform

**Launch Video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mhDiw0nKB34>

\
**❌ Problem**

Companies buy an ERP expecting it to become the most powerful software in their stack. It runs finance, inventory, procurement, operations, reporting, and the workflows the business depends on.

Buying an ERP is easy. Implementing it is hard and requires labour heavy consultant work where:

* Requirements get missed
* Workflows get configured differently than agreed
* Data issues get discovered too late
* Testing reveals the system does not match how the business actually works
* End-user adoption suffers

For implementation teams, the challenge is managing hundreds of stakeholders across concurrent projects, with thousands of documents, decisions, and system dependencies to track.

That is why so many ERP projects miss their budget, timeline, and targets, and why companies spend billions on implementation services.

**✅ Solution**

Trope is the AI-native platform that deploys agents to deliver successful implementations faster.

Using Trope is like having a project manager, consultant, and developer working 24/7, so you can spend more time on the design and decisions.

Trope connects to the systems where project work already lives. It compares what was promised with what is actually being built, then flags gaps across scope, configuration, data, testing, training, and documentation before they become expensive.

Trope takes action by turning meetings into action items, scanning ERP configurations programmatically, and keeping documents, configurations, and stakeholders in sync.

**The Team**

We grew up in Vancouver and met at the University of British Columbia. We built operations and AI software at Tesla, Amazon, Zipline, and Schneider Electric.

After speaking with ERP veterans who had built and sold practices, the pattern was clear: everyone knew the traditional services model was going to change, but no one knew how.

Trope is defining the AI-native model for ERP services.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104941&key=user_uploads/2519723/896d82bc-589c-4f7b-a0a7-59d2c9fc8d9f)

**Our Ask**

If you know anyone who works on ERP implementations (ie, consulting, system integration, or professional services) we’d love an intro. Email me at [matthew@trope.ai](mailto:matthew@trope.ai).

Take care,

Matthew & Victor

launches.body:
**Palisade builds agents to run your online marketplace. Our agents have driven over $2.7M in GMV since the start of the batch.**

<https://youtu.be/cuVQHgQ9yHg>

**The problem:** The best marketplaces in the real world run on salespeople. The real estate agent who takes you house to house and texts you the moment the right listing is about to hit the market. The Sephora beauty advisor who finds your exact shade. The jeweler who walks you through diamond cuts for an engagement ring. **Online marketplaces skipped that person entirely** and left the selling to search bars and filters.

**What we do:** Palisade builds the missing **sales agent**. Every single visitor to your marketplace gets their own dedicated agent, and conversion goes up massively.

**How it works:** Agents can take any action possible on your platform. They know every listing, every UI component, and every flow. They navigate for users with their own cursor, help them discover, add to cart, and complete the purchase or booking. They build custom pages and reshape the UI around how each person actually uses the platform, remembering each user and tailoring the experience to their behavior and preferences. Each dedicated agent can naturally text and email with their customer as well.

**Is this another chatbot?** Each agent is proactive with much richer, customized components than an idle chatbot. It’s like giving every customer an omnipotent Claude embedded into the platform. Palisade agents get to know each customer personally and build relationships over time. They keep working after customers leave, remember them when they return, and reach out proactively over email and text with personal messages. And everything they learn flows back: agents aggregate their conversations into reports, insights, and recommendations for sellers, and offer to make concrete optimizations themselves, to the listings and even to the marketplace platform itself.

**Integration**: Start by adding just one line of code to your existing platform, whether your marketplace sells yachts, vacation rentals, rare collectibles, or anything else.

**Backstory:** After studying CS at Princeton, I spent years at Amazon building software for influencers to sell more products. I then became a founding engineer at Sage AI Labs, where I worked on some of the very first iMessage agents for consumer shopping. That work left me with a deep understanding of consumer habits and marketplace dynamics.

**If you’re looking to transform your marketplace:** Reach out at [jonathan@runpalisade.com](mailto:jonathan@runpalisade.com)

Kara is building diamond semiconductors. 

We begin with growing ultra-high purity diamond wafers for advanced hardware. Used in data centers, spacecrafts, RF systems, and quantum hardware, our diamond moves heat up to 5× better than copper, helping critical systems run cooler, faster, and more reliably. 

Diamond has spent centuries as a symbol. We are turning it into infrastructure.

launches.title: Kara: Making Diamond an Engineering Material
launches.tagline: Kara grows and engineers diamond wafers for thermal management, semiconductor and quantum applications
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We grow high-purity diamond wafers for scientific and industrial applications. Our diamond thermal wafers can be used in aircraft, spacecraft, RF electronics, and lasers to move heat dramatically better than conventional materials. We’re helping hardware run cooler, faster, and more reliably with diamond that is 5× more thermally conductive than copper.

Here is a link to our launch video: 

<https://youtu.be/16aad1cU_FM>

**The Problem**

The world’s most valuable hardware systems are limited by how quickly they can remove heat.

For AI chips, that means expensive GPUs throttle and deliver less compute. In aircraft and satellites, it means carrying more cooling mass. In RF systems and lasers, it limits sustained output power.

Adding more cooling costs space, and energy, and sometimes is simply not possible.

**What We Built**

Diamond is usually something you wear. We make it something engineers can build with.

Diamond conducts heat up to **5× better than copper while weighing \~60% less** for the same volume. It is electrically insulating and stable in extreme environments.

Today we manufacture:

* Diamond heat spreaders for AI and high-performance computing
* Ultra-high-purity diamond wafers for thermal, photonic and quantum applications
* Diamond-metal composites (copper and aluminium) for thermal management
* Metallized and bondable diamond plates
* Custom-engineered diamond components

We are now producing custom samples under pilot agreements and purchase orders for thermal, electronic, aerospace, and quantum applications.

Silicon transformed computing when we learned to manufacture it with extreme purity and control. Kara is doing the same with diamond. Today, our ultra-high-purity diamond pulls heat away from silicon chips.

**Tomorrow, Kara’s control over purity and defects unlocks diamond as the ultimate semiconductor.**

**Why us**

[@Aarin Jhaveri](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3669602) is a fifth-generation diamantaire who has sold millions of dollars in natural and lab-grown diamonds and worked across the supply chain.

[@Anuveer Chadha](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3669310) is a chemical engineer who has worked on diamond quantum sensing and advanced-materials research at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory with the Department of Defense and Department of Energy.

Diamond is our unfair advantage. We know how to grow, control, and engineer it far beyond jewelry.

**Our ask**

**Today, we're looking for introductions to engineers building hardware that is limited by heat.** 

Specifically:

* AI accelerator packaging teams
* Advanced packaging / OSAT engineers
* Aerospace, space, and defence electronics
* Data-centre infrastructure companies
* High-power RF and GaN teams

Introduce us to the engineer responsible for the hottest, hardest-to-cool hardware, especially where size, weight, or power makes cooling difficult. 

We’ll build them a custom diamond sample to test.

Email us at [founders@karalabs.ai](mailto:founders@karalabs.ai) or book time here: <https://calendly.com/aarin-berkeley/aarin-jhaveri-s-calender>

**Diamond spent centuries as a symbol of “extraordinary”. We are making it something the world can build with.**

launches.title: Zomma: AI operations employees for finance back offices
launches.tagline: Computer-use agents that work cross-border transaction alert investigations end to end: collect evidence, produce an assessment, draft an RFI.
launches.body:
We're building Zomma: AI operations employees for finance back offices, starting with cross-border transaction alert investigations.

**TL;DR:** Zomma agents work directly inside the software your ops team already uses. No APIs, no integrations. For every cross-border alert, the agent gathers the evidence, writes the draft assessment, and drafts the RFI, end-to-end. Running live compliance-ops pilots with a US RIA and a $10B AUM wealth tech. 92% on OSWorld.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDXDKH_tYhg>

## **The problem**

Cross-border payments trip more monitoring rules than anything else in the queue: sanctions name hits on foreign counterparties, high-risk corridors, first-time beneficiaries. Most alerts are false positives (McKinsey: over 90% in transaction monitoring), but every one still needs to be investigated. 20 to 60 minutes per case, across five or six systems, several with no API at all. And the evidence that clears them sits in foreign company registries and local-language adverse media. 

So review capacity scales the only way it can: hiring. When hiring lags volume, alerts pile into backlogs that take months to clear, and backlogs are what regulators fine: $3.8B in AML penalties last year alone.

## **What Zomma does**

Zomma agents work the queue on the same screens your analysts use: case manager, screening tool, admin panel, inbox, web search. Onboarding looks like hiring: an SOP and a login.

On a transaction monitoring alert, the agent

* pulls the KYC profile and payment history
* verifies the invoice and researches the counterparty, including registries you can only search by hand
* writes a case-specific assessment with every claim cited to the source screen
* drafts the RFI when documents are missing

Every step is logged and replayable: timestamped screenshots of every page checked, numbered citations, explicit no-match statements, a screen-by-screen trail an examiner can follow.

## **Why start with cross-border alerts**

If an employee can do it on a screen, Zomma can learn it: the rest of the compliance queue, payment disputes, client onboarding, trade ops. Cross-border alerts come first because they have the exact shape our agents are best at: high-volume, parallelizable work that needs real reasoning but follows a defined workflow to a documented disposition. They're also the hardest cases to automate any other way: the evidence lives in registries and portals that will never have APIs. And agents scale with the queue: a volume spike means provisioning two more that afternoon; a BPO batch takes a month to train.

Computer-use agents only recently got accurate enough to trust with a live queue, which is why we're building this now. Our state-of-the-art computer-use harness with our procedural and workflow memory system scores 92% on OSWorld.

## **Team**

* **Jihyun (CEO):** founding team at a Blackstone-backed hedge fund, scaled Asia's largest wealth tech, Goldman engineer.
* **Cash (CTO):** backend systems behind $20B+ in yearly transactions, trains VLMs for computer use.
* **Varun (CPO):** high-performance infra at Apple, design-verification agents at Bronco AI (YC S23).

Send us \~100 closed cross-border alerts and we'll show you what the agent would have done with them, or book a call: zommalabs.com/call.

launches.title: Rex: Turn enterprise order-to-cash into an autonomous operation
launches.tagline: AI Operations Partner for Enterprise Order to Cash
launches.body:
Rex is an AI service that runs order-to-cash and accounts receivable operations for enterprises. Founders [Merlin Kafka](https://www.linkedin.com/in/merlinkafka/) and [Lewis Blackwood](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisblackwood) spent 4 years at an a16z-backed startup helping finance teams at startups like Cognition, Legora and Bridge automate revenue collection. The problem is 100x bigger in the enterprise, so they built Rex: agents that do the work end-to-end. Live in production with Synthesia.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BKS7qaZS8Is>

**Revenue ≠ cash**

Enterprises invoice customers, then spend months chasing the money through email chains, PDFs and ancient web portals. A $1M invoice sits unpaid because one PO number didn't match.

Multiply that across thousands of customers and you get 100+ person teams, often offshore, doing this by hand: collections, invoice submission, dispute resolution, deduction management, cash application. Order-to-cash is the most outsourced process in finance because the work needs judgment. Reading a customer's email and deciding whether their dispute is valid. Working out which of 14 open invoices a lump-sum payment covers. Knowing that this account always pays late but always pays, and that one needs escalating now.

AR automation software has existed for 20 years and the teams never got smaller, because the tools organise the work while people still do it. Businesses invoice each other tens of trillions of dollars a year; the labour and outsourcing spend on collecting it is over $100B. Until now the only way to scale was headcount or a BPO contract.

**What Rex does**

Rex connects to the ERP (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle), CRM (Salesforce), billing system and shared AR inbox, and learns how the team runs the process today. That knowledge becomes editable agent operating procedures: how to chase a Fortune 500 buyer vs a startup, which deductions get investigated vs written off, when a dispute goes to a human.

Then agents run those procedures across thousands of accounts in parallel:

* Collections and payment follow-ups, including the long tail no team gets to
* Invoice submission and status tracking inside procurement portals (SAP Ariba, Coupa, Tungsten and hundreds of others)
* Dispute and deduction investigation
* Remittance processing and cash application
* Responding to customer finance emails
* Updating ERP, CRM and billing records
* Routing exceptions to the team for approval

Portals deserve a special mention: an increasing share of enterprise invoices must be submitted and tracked inside the buyer's procurement system. It's the work AR teams hate most and the work software vendors ignore. Rex treats it as core.

**Is Rex a managed service or software?**

Enterprises can partner with Rex as a managed service provider or let their team operate Rex. AR software (dunning tools, collections worklists, AR dashboards) organises work for a team to do. Rex agents do the work, and the finance team approves exceptions. With Rex, the team stops drowning in routine chasing and handles the judgment calls. Customers compare Rex to their next AR hire, their offshore team, or their BPO contract.

**Can finance teams trust AI agents with collections?**

Autonomy is earned, not switched on. Each procedure starts supervised: Rex proposes, the team approves. Once a procedure hits its accuracy bar for the account, it graduates and runs autonomously. Safe, high-volume work goes first; judgment-heavy edges stay gated as long as the team wants. Every action is logged with its full reasoning, so finance audits the system instead of babysitting it.

**Traction**

[Rex is live in production with enterprises like Synthesia](https://www.rex.inc/customers/synthesia), running collections, portal submissions, inbox triage and cash application. Cases that used to take weeks of back and forth resolve in minutes.

**Get in touch**

If invoice volume is outgrowing the finance team, or order-to-cash runs on offshore headcount or a BPO contract, get in touch: [rex.inc](http://rex.inc)

launches.title: Enact: post-training infrastructure for robotics models
launches.tagline: Enact generates the data and evaluations needed to make robotics models reliable in the real world.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Enact helps teams deploy robots that work in the real world. We roll out policies, generate failure / recovery data, and run in-house evaluations so robots can complete real tasks in production.** 

[**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dam0tQBIezY**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dam0tQBIezY)

**The Problem**

Robotics models can look flawless in choreographed demos and still fail when an object slips, the scene shifts, or the robot makes an early mistake. Those failures push the policy into states its training data never taught it to recover from. **Robotics models must train on edge cases to be reliable in the real world.**

**What We Built**

Enact turns a policy’s failures into targeted recovery datasets for teams training robotics models. We use the data to fine-tune models and run real-world evaluations, verifying our data improves reliability.

**We’re already serving our first customers: finding where their robots fail and collecting the targeted recovery data needed to make them robust.**

* Roll out an existing model on a physical robot.
* Identify recurring failure states.
* Recreate those states and demonstrate how to recover.
* Retrain with the new trajectories added in.
* Repeat

**Targeted recovery data pushes success rates above 99%.**

On our controlled packing task using pi0.5 on the YAM 6DoF arms:

* 200 ordinary expert demonstrations: 90/100 successful physical rollouts
* 250 ordinary expert demonstrations (more of the same data): 89/100
* 200 expert demonstrations plus 50 targeted recovery demonstrations: 99/100

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109880&key=user_uploads/2406199/e1b83c19-6e1d-4dda-adcf-258398bc1676)

**We’re continuing to longer-horizon tasks such as industrial kitting, lab automation, and electronics recycling**

Longer-horizon tasks need substantially more base and recovery data, but the loop is the same: find failures, target missing behaviors, retrain, repeat.

**Who We Are**

We’re James Stevens and Govind Chada, and we met at Stanford. Govind researched real-world robot adaptation in Chelsea Finn’s IRIS Lab and co-developed recovery methods published at top robotics conferences. Together, we built Enact’s in-house data and evaluation operation and are already serving robotics teams. We started Enact to make robotics models work reliably outside the lab.

**Our Ask**

Training a robot foundation model or deploying a policy that fails on a real task? Tell us the model, task, and where it breaks, and we’ll make it work.

Email: [founders@enact.company](mailto:founders@enact.company)

launches.tagline: Run every repair from first call to first-time fix.
launches.body:
**Bernard is building the AI front and back office for home and commercial appliance servicers.**

They manage each repair from the first customer call through scheduling, dispatch, diagnosis, parts preparation, technician handoff, and follow-up. Bernard works across phone, text, email, warranty feeds, and existing field-service systems, carrying the job context across every surface.

We are already live in the field with some of the largest authorized service companies in the country.

Our goal is simple: make the first visit the last one.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eiGjkYMeu2k>

### The first truck roll should not be a diagnostic visit

Appliance repair is an information and inventory problem. A technician cannot simply carry washer parts. The exact appliance, model, revision, symptoms, and failure mode determine which parts might be required, and many nearly identical parts are not interchangeable.

When that information does not come together before the appointment, the first visit becomes a diagnostic visit. The technician identifies the failure, orders the part, and returns days later to complete the repair. Customers wait longer, technicians complete fewer jobs, and servicers lose capacity and margin.

### Pre-ID prepares the repair before the truck rolls

When a customer reports that their washer will not drain, Bernard does more than book an appointment.

Bernard identifies the exact appliance, asks follow-up questions specific to the symptoms, and collects missing evidence from the customer. Pre-ID then combines that information with repair history, similar completed visits, manufacturer guidance, parts data, and the servicer’s own operating knowledge.

Before the visit, Bernard gives the technician a diagnosis, ranked parts, the most useful next questions, and the evidence supporting each recommendation. The office can prepare the parts, confirm they will arrive on time, and hand the technician a complete picture of the job.

Every interaction and completed repair feeds back into Bernard, turning the servicer’s daily work into shared knowledge.

### Why start with the servicer?

Every appliance company makes a promise at the point of sale. The servicer is the person who ultimately has to keep that promise inside someone’s home or business.

That visit affects the customer, the retailer, the manufacturer, the warranty company, and the parts distributor. Yet the servicer coordinating it is often working across disconnected phone systems, inboxes, scheduling tools, parts catalogs, and knowledge held by a few experienced employees.

We believe that building the world’s most efficient appliance servicers will create happier customers and a more connected appliance ecosystem.

Bernard starts with the servicer because that is where the industry meets the physical world.

### About us

[Dan Katzman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dankatzman/) previously helped build Nava Benefits' strategy and operations team, working across the product and operational infrastructure required to deliver a complicated, service-heavy experience reliably, while also leading partnerships. Before Nava, he invested at City Light Capital and Golub Capital.

[David Goodfellow](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dgoodfellow/) grew from product engineer to engineering manager at Radar Labs, where he led fraud and geo-compliance products and helped replace the incumbent provider at DraftKings and Bet365. Before that, he worked on RPA and cognitive automation at Disney, before enterprise automation was cool.

### Talk to us

If you run an appliance service company or lead service operations at an appliance manufacturer, retailer, warranty company, or service network, reach out to us at [founders@bernardhq.com](mailto:founders@bernardhq.com)

launches.title: Studio: The simulation engine for market behavior
launches.tagline: The first accurate simulation models able to predict society's response to an idea.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Studio is a simulation lab studying how humans and societies interact with new ideas, and building the first software models that can accurately predict that response. Instead of creating digital twins of survey respondents, Studio builds live market models of interconnected consumer segments from real behavior data. Studio's predictions match live KPI outcomes like revenue and sentiment with over 95% accuracy.

<https://youtu.be/g0M-T2ohtcQ>

## The problem

A huge number of consequential decisions are bets on human behavior.

A company launches a product or changes a price. A brand runs a campaign. A public institution launches a new initiative or communications strategy. In each case, the outcome depends on how a population responds.

Today, teams rely on surveys and historical data to help derisk those bets.

But those tools are inherently outdated and non-comprehensive: they observe people individually and at a point in time.

_Real populations don’t behave that way._

People influence one another. Reactions spread between groups. Adoption compounds or fades. Sentiment changes. A decision that resonates with one audience can change how another audience responds. Those interactions are what ultimately determine outcomes like revenue, conversion, adoption, and sentiment.

Currently, the only real “simulation” is the launch itself.

## What we do

Studio builds live models of a company’s market from real data on how consumers behave. It overlays internal data like sales and campaign performance with external evidence like social conversations and market trends.

Studio uses those signals to construct highly specific audience cohorts and model how their behavior and influence interact over time.

Teams can then:

* **Test-run launches:** see how a new product, price, campaign, message, or initiative will unfold.
* **Forecast outcomes:** revenue, conversion, adoption, sentiment, and other KPIs.
* **Understand why:** know which groups drive the result, by how much, and trace outcomes to exact evidence.
* **Test alternatives:** compare different versions of a decision to find the optimal variation.
* **Improve over time:** compare forecasts with real outcomes and recalibrate the model.

Instead of predicting “How will this person respond to X?”, Studio answers:

“How will a population interact with X, and why?”

Studio has live-tested with large consumer brands like Danone and Mila, and our model’s predictions match real-world KPI outcomes with >95% accuracy.

## Why we built it

We’ve spent years predicting behavior. Nikita built simulation software to understand and predict individual decision-making at MIT, while Cameron built predictive models for financial institutions and in private equity, and agent-based society simulations at UC Berkeley MET.

We met at the same gap: you can simulate how a protein will fold or how a financial system will react to a market shock, but there is no equivalent for simulating how society will interact with a new idea. We’re now creating a studio to design society.

## Where we’re starting

We’re initially working with enterprises making high-stakes audience-facing decisions across product, pricing, innovation, brand, marketing, and communications.

But the underlying problem is much broader.

Any organization trying to create a particular response in a population should be able to test different versions of that decision, understand how reactions might spread, and compare likely outcomes before deploying it.

## Our ask

We’d love to talk to teams making consumer-facing decisions. This could be a new product, pricing plan, campaign, etc.

If you have an upcoming decision you’d like to test before it goes live, we’d love to run it through Studio!

launches.title: Prized: A cloud devbox that feels local
launches.tagline: The fastest way to run coding agents in the cloud without giving up your local workflow.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Marinos and Hudson, co-founders of Prized.

**TL;DR:** Prized gives developers a dedicated devbox in the cloud that still feels local. Your files stay synced to a real folder, ports show up on [localhost](http://localhost), and coding agents keep running when you close your laptop.

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/JmaxNhEdLdc>

**The problem**

Coding agents can work for hours now. But only if you keep your laptop open.

You start a refactor, a migration, or a big build. Then you need to leave. Close the lid and the agent dies with it.

You can move everything to a VM, but now you're doing remote dev. Your files live somewhere else. Your ports need forwarding. Your terminal disappears when the connection drops.

Remote development still feels remote.

it shouldn't…

**The solution**

With Prized, one command puts your project on a dedicated devbox without giving up local development:

* **Real files on your Mac.** Prized syncs both ways into a normal folder, so everything keeps working the way it already does.


* [**Localhost**](http://Localhost)** stays [localhost](http://localhost)**. Servers running on the box appear on your Mac automatically, including loopback-only services and hot reload.


* **Sessions stay alive.** SSH lands in a persistent terminal session on the box, so disconnecting or closing your laptop doesn't stop the work.


* **Compute grows with the task.** Resize the box without rebuilding your environment or moving your project again.


* **Secrets stay out of the agent's hands.** For brokered secrets, the agent only sees a placeholder.

**The team**

We worked together at Gander (F24) building fleet management software for private jets. After the company's acquisition by Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), Marinos continued school at Stanford, and Hudson went on to be an engineer at Suno.

We built Prized for ourselves after getting tired of having to keep our laptops cracked open all the time. A raw VM kept the process alive but gave up the local workflow we actually wanted.

Check Prized out at [https://prized.dev](https://prized.dev/), or reach out at [founders@prized.dev](mailto:founders@prized.dev).

launches.title: Prized: Lovable for internal tools
launches.tagline: The fastest way for non-engineers to ship secure internal tools.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Marinos and Hudson, co-founders of Prized.

**TL;DR:** Prized lets anyone at your company build and ship secure internal tools with AI. Company data comes pre-connected and scoped to what each person should see, every access is audited, and finished tools deploy behind your company's sign-in.

**Launch video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WILimoqemD4>

**The problem**

Building software has never been easier. And the people who need internal tools most, in ops, support, and finance, are done waiting on engineering.

So they build it themselves. They rip Claude Code or Cursor, pull straight from company data, and ship a working tool in an afternoon. No permissions. No audit trail. No one watching where the data goes.

Security is assumed to be fine because the tool is "just internal."

it's not…

**The solution**

People aren't going to stop building with AI. So we built them a place where it's safe.

With Prized, anyone can spin up a sandbox that comes with company data already attached, scoped to what they should see, with an audit trail on every access. 

From there it's whatever building style they like: describe the tool in our app builder and watch it take shape, or bring a coding agent like Claude Code and build it themselves. Shipping is one click, and the finished tool sits behind your company's sign-in.

The person who runs the workflow finally gets to build the tool for it. Safely, this time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105647&key=user_uploads/2485896/e426b427-8a79-4ca5-b462-b26b98db43e0)

**Secure by default**

Security is enforced in the infrastructure, not left to the person building the tool:

* **Least privilege per tool.** Every tool gets its own database role and integration scopes; it can read and write only what it was granted.
* **Credentials stay out of reach.** Secrets live in a broker and never touch the tool's code or the agent's context, so they can't leak or cross workspace boundaries.
* **Outbound traffic proxy.** External calls only go to explicitly allowed hosts, and integrations are read-only until someone turns writes on.
* **Admin visibility.** IT sees every tool in the org: who built it, what data it reads or writes, who can use it, and risky changes (like a destructive migration) need explicit approval before they ship.

**Your agent, our sandbox**

Already have a favorite coding agent? Bring it. It plugs into the same governed sandbox and ships the same way.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105647&key=user_uploads/2485896/fcfa68c5-8c9f-4d13-b37c-d526e733539a)

**The team**

We worked together at Gander (F24) building fleet management software for private jets. After the company's acquisition by Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), Marinos continued school at Stanford, and Hudson went on to be an engineer at Suno.

**Our ask**

If any of these describe you, we'd love to talk:

* You work in ops, support, finance, or RevOps and keep waiting on engineering for small tools.
* You lead engineering and one-off tool requests keep eating your roadmap.
* You're in security or IT, wondering where AI-built tools are showing up at your company.

Check us out at[ https://prized.dev/](https://prized.dev/), or reach out at [founders@prized.dev](mailto:founders@prized.dev).

launches.tagline: Your AI inference gets smarter and cheaper the more you use it.
launches.body:
We’re Aamir & Luis and we’re excited to launch our company’s new brand ahead of demo day this week: Orchestra ([orchestra.ai](http://orchestra.ai)) \
\
Companies move their frontier inference spend to Orchestra, with a single URL swap. We relay their traffic through to the frontier labs, while building evals in the background automatically. These evals allows us to post-train specialist models that replace the frontier, at a fraction of the cost. When our model beats the frontier at your product’s work, we promote it and your bills go down. Then we repeat the loop continuously, forever; your AI inference gets smarter and cheaper the more you use it. \
\
We’re going straight after the $104B inference market; Anthropic grew 14x YoY but we’ve seen time and time again that start-ups and enterprises are willing to move spend if you can prove the performance. That it. We don’t have FDEs. We don’t pre-train models. Most of the application layer lives in a CLI that coding agents use. \
\
We just do one thing really well: building and routing your work to the most efficient model. We found the easiest way to build a fast growing business is to _sell_ your product to people who have pain and who are already spending money with someone else. The more we focused on the fastest growing segments of our business, the faster our product got better at solving a simple, but incredibly painful problem: “You don’t need a PhD to work in the mailroom”. 

**It’s the “Age of the Unc”** 

I shared my experiences doing YC as a 38-year old (<https://x.com/lluismanrique/status/2094846605925241259>) but for any founders out there thinking about coming back to YC: do it. We worked 60-hour weeks, not 100-hour weeks. We had a network of angels, customers and advisors. We ran the marathon, instead of sprinting it. At 38, I’m old enough to understand that pedagogy is the point of YC. Learning how to work on your company is the point. You’ll get **so much more** out of YC when you’re doing it again with the hindsight of all your past successes and failures. Having done it before is a huge advantage, but having a long career in which I’ve encountered a lot of situations and had to make a lot of decisions and a few mistakes, and see others do the same, allows me to understand how YC’s advice impacts the real world. You will manage your agents better. You will close customers faster. You’ll build a better company. 

**Why Orchestra?** 

Branding is everything, especially outside of silicon valley. We launched as the ‘alternative’, the ‘backup’; but as time went on, we realized how open companies are to moving **all** their spend to a single place and making it work efficiently. Inference is the fastest growing market in the history of capitalism and we needed a brand that reflected our ambitions. Orchestra is going to win a huge chunk of that market; not the back-up, but the entire show. 

Say hello to Orchestra. And if your bills are too damn high, send us a note. We’d love to help.

launches.title: Understudy: The self-optimizing inference cloud
launches.tagline: We distill your production usage into cheaper, specialized models your company owns
launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re Luis and Aamir, founders of Understudy.

### TL;DR

We help you cut your company’s Anthropic bill by 80% with no loss of performance.

Understudy is an inference cloud. We capture your employee’s AI work traces, train smaller models, and automatically deploy them (only when they outperform the expensive model you are currently paying for).

Instead of renting the same frontier model forever, your AI infrastructure gets cheaper and better every time it runs.

See more: <https://youtu.be/YhfoOchpYaw>

### The problem

Last week, we met with a company spending $40M/year on Anthropic. And it’s only going in one direction.

To them, it feels totally out of control.

They’re not alone - every company we meet is spending record amounts on models from frontier labs.

But almost none of that spending compounds.

I.e. You send a prompt, pay for the answer, and throw away the experience. Six months later, you are still renting the same general-purpose model at roughly the same price.

Meanwhile, training custom models requires an entire ML team to collect and clean traces, build evals, choose training data, fine-tune and reinforce models, test serving configurations, compare cost, latency, and quality, safely deploy or roll back the winner.

For most companies, it’s just too much to bother with.

### What Understudy does

Point Understudy at an AI workload.

We capture how your existing agent performs, turn those traces into evals, and start training smaller models that can do the same job better.

Understudy handles the entire loop:

**Observe → evaluate → train → test → deploy → repeat**

A new model is promoted only when it beats the incumbent on the metrics you care about, such as:

* task success
* inference cost
* latency
* privacy
* deployment size

Your customized models are owned by you, and can run in our cloud, your cloud, or on-premise.

### An example

Suppose your product uses Claude for a repetitive legal workflow.

Understudy observes successful production runs, learns the specific tools and judgment required for that workflow, and trains a specialized open-weight model.

Once that model matches or beats Claude on a held-out evaluation, Understudy starts routing production traffic to it.

As more work is completed, the model keeps improving.

### Why us

Aamir and I met building Instacart’s optimization and experimentation systems, growing multiple business lines to more than $1B in annual revenue.

We started Understudy because we believe every company using AI should be accumulating intelligence, not accumulating API bills.

### Our ask

Spending too much on repetitive model workloads? Ready to own your own models? We want to meet you - come to [understudylabs.com](http://understudylabs.com) today.

launches.tagline: Semiconductors to push machines where humans cant go.
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/oHKXAeiH79Y>

**TLDR:** Synapse Semiconductor builds image sensors that process **AI on the sensor** itself. Each pixel captures light and runs neural-network computation in the same device, replacing the need for a GPU while cutting the power and latency of edge vision.\
\
\
A camera has no use by itself. Its value is only when its information gets evaluated. How can a camera that only has value when combined with a GPU support local intelligence? GPUs will get better, yet the fundamental problem is the separation of the camera and the GPU. Solving that separation will unlock bountiful innovation in machine perception. 

**RETINA: a chip designed like the human retina which runs neural network operations in the camera pixel.** 

\
We have compressed the whole edge AI vision hardware stack into **one wafer**. CNNS, VLMS, etc can run on just one chip that senses light. Our compute transistors are also the same photosensors that see light. There is no longer separation between compute (Nvidia Jetson Nano) and a camera (RealSense Depth Camera). \
\
If you are building robotic perception, drones, and vision systems for physical AI —> [book.synapsesemi.org](http://book.synapsesemi.org)

launches.tagline: Every speech model, benchmarked language by language, wired into one API.
launches.body:
Speko is a router for voice models. One API key, and your agent runs on the speech-to-text, LLM and text-to-speech models we measured as best for your language and use case.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108267&key=user_uploads/451241/2038963f-c769-47a9-8fd9-c59f3966027b)

### I picked voice stacks by trial and error for four years

A voice agent is three models in a row: speech-to-text, then an LLM, then text-to-speech. Three vendors, a dozen credible options each. You run a bake-off, you argue about whose numbers are real, and you ship the combination that felt best that month.

Then next week another model drops. And another. Nobody has time to re-run the bake-off, so the stack you picked under deadline quietly becomes the stack you are stuck with for a year.

That is how most voice agents are running today. Not on the best models. On the models that were best whenever someone last had a free week.

Public leaderboards do not settle it either. They are averages over somebody else's audio, in somebody else's conditions.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AjC8WVA96kUBdD09RJMUgFfvxGfxPvL-/](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AjC8WVA96kUBdD09RJMUgFfvxGfxPvL-/view?usp=sharing)

### We measure, then we route

We benchmark the speech models people actually ship on, language by language, and publish everything at [benchmarks.speko.ai](http://benchmarks.speko.ai): word error rate, finalize latency, time to first token, cost per minute. When a vendor ships a new model we test it the same day and the board updates.

Point your agent at Speko and that measurement becomes routing. One API key across every provider we support. Tell us the language and the conditions, and your traffic runs on the stack our numbers say wins. When the numbers change, the routing changes and you rewrite nothing.

If a provider fails when we open the connection, the router drops to the next ranked model on its own.

### Or build the agent with us

You do not need an existing agent to start. A few lines gets a working voice agent live on Speko, and it inherits the same routing from day one.

If you are picking a voice stack right now, start with the numbers at [benchmarks.speko.ai](http://benchmarks.speko.ai), then build on them at [speko.ai](http://speko.ai).

launches.tagline: GutGutGoose builds personalized probiotics guaranteed to colonize, then uses every retest to train models of the human gut.
launches.body:
# TL;DR: We’ve created the last probiotic you’ll ever need - personalised, constantly improving, while also generating valuable data.

### 

# What we do and why

Your gut is the most unique part of your body, different enough that the same probiotic can work for one person and do nothing for another. Most probiotics disappoint because they’re one formula for everyone, and in any gut most of their strains never establish. GutGutGoose makes a probiotic that won’t work for any gut but yours: we sequence your microbiome, find which strains can establish in the microbes you already have, compound those into your formula, and re-sequence you weeks later to confirm they took hold.

It’s for people who’ve tried things for IBS, bloating, digestion, mood, weight or GLP-1 symptoms without luck. If it doesn’t work you get your money back, and retesting shows how your gut changed, so you know it’s not a placebo.\
\
<https://youtu.be/Cn6oGduZosc>

The innovation is accurately predicting which bacteria will live in a gut, which is extremely hard. It’s built on two peer-reviewed models, MICOM and AGORA2, and more than 7,000 metabolic reconstructions of gut bacteria, and it finds the strains that can hold in your gut’s community. On two published human cohorts, its predictions matched what actually established 84.7% and 76.7% of the time, and we reproduced the first at 78.1% ourselves. Off-the-shelf products manage under 5%. Once we can control which bacteria live where, we can run precision interventions in the gut and engineer it.

We’re a supplement today and can’t treat disease, but each cycle produces a record of one gut, one intervention, and the result. That record makes each customer’s next formula better, and across thousands of people it becomes the first longitudinal dataset of the human gut responding to known, controlled changes. Our vision is to use changes in metabolic pathways over time to predict Alzheimer’s, dementia and Parkinson’s a decade before symptoms appear.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108277&key=user_uploads/991771/50caffe3-e0c9-44e5-9212-da1bbabc0e00)

# Traction

We gave a talk at an endometriosis event, and 20 of the 50 people joined our waitlist. The first night we opened paid deposits, we called five people from that list at 7:30pm. Three picked up, and we managed to get seven sign ups, they were so excited they referred and paid for their families that night. Five of the 20 referred someone else, and our traction has only grown since.

# Team

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108277&key=user_uploads/991771/13686614-1a12-4b14-a657-d33d042b3ee6)

The GutGutGoose founders winning the YC product pitch

Leon started university at 14 and spent four years at a $3bn YC unicorn. After we started GutGutGoose, he built a pharmacy, now doing $4M a year, to fund the science behind our engine. Anis joined in September; he co-built the model, runs operations, and is the youngest ever to win Queensland’s Math Olympiad. He’s on a Chancellor’s Excellence Scholarship in AI and Data Science, and (fun fact) was once the world’s number one Catan player.

# The ask

We’d love introductions to gut-health clinics, patient communities, or microbiome researchers who could help us recruit and shape the 80-person study. Email us at [admin@gutgutgoose.com](mailto:admin@gutgutgoose.com). More at [gutgutgoose.com](http://gutgutgoose.com).

Hey everyone! We're [Jordan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jordan-zietz/) and [Daniela](https://www.linkedin.com/in/danielamunoz12/), founders of LemonLime.

**TL;DR**

Most companies don't have the time or technical expertise to build custom AI automations. LemonLime connects to your existing tools, studies your business, and builds specialized automations for you — actual outcomes, fast.

<https://youtu.be/aFcB1fJhPmY>

**The problem**

Every small business knows they should be "using AI," but almost none of them can. We learned this firsthand doing custom AI consulting for businesses. After building workflows for a handful of customers, two things immediately became obvious:

1. The context AI needs to succeed is scattered — files, documents, chat threads, you name it. Searching for and organizing this information was 95% of the work, every single time.
2. Companies don't want to spend weeks learning another complicated new tool. That's a huge ask for busy teams.

Small businesses need impact out-of-the-box, they don’t have the time or capital to spend on fancy AI initiatives that aren’t creating value from day one.

**Our solution**

Since company information is all over the place, we started by building the layer underneath that powers AI search and retrieval. If you’ve heard the term “company brain”, that’s what this first layer is.

After your company’s unique knowledge architecture is built, users can use plain-language to deploy agents and automations that support their business without writing a single line of code.  You tell it what you want automated, LemonLime automates it.  It’s that easy.

Don’t know where to start?  No worries, LemonLime handles that, too. After running deep research on your business, LemonLime automatically surfaces suggested automations that you can implement with a single click.

This is me running 20 agents in parallel. This is my real everyday workflow, not a demo.

**What we do** Jcode is an open-source coding agent that's 20x more memory-efficient than Claude Code, which means you can run 20x more agents in parallel on the same machine. It hits state-of-the-art results on coding benchmarks. Try it: <https://jcode.sh/>

**The problem** Most coding agents are heavy. Each instance eats gigabytes of RAM, and because memory is the bottleneck, you can only run a handful at once. That caps how much work you can hand off at a time. The real power of agents is dispatching lots of different tasks in parallel and having them all worked on at once, and that's exactly what today's tools make too expensive to do.

**Our solution** Jcode is engineered from the ground up to be lightweight, roughly 20x more memory-efficient than Claude Code. Since RAM is what caps how many agents you can run, cutting memory 20x lets you fire off 20x more tasks in parallel on the same hardware. It's fully open source, so you can run it yourself and inspect exactly what it does.

**Who I am** I'm Jeremy, 21, building Jcode. I think running many agents in parallel is the single biggest lever in developer productivity. Previously I hacked GitHub Copilot for unlimited tokens, and I'm top 500 in the world on Monkeytype. GitHub: <https://github.com/1jehuang>

**Developers:** Try Jcode today: <https://jcode.sh/>

launches.tagline: We built a computation layer for health insurance that predicts the lowest true-cost coverage for anyone. We will be the national standard for how America chooses coverage, with the only engine that knows both what plans cost and what they actually do.
launches.body:
Hey everyone — we're **Chang and Bryan**, the founders of **Insurf**.

American health insurance is f\*\*\*ed: chosen by guesswork, enforced by denial. We built the engine that fixes both halves.

**TL;DR**

**Surely** computes the lowest-cost plan for anyone. **Inveto** fights denials for real clinics across Texas, Georgia, and California, and each contract-authorized, de-identified outcome becomes coverage data nobody else has. Everything Inveto learns, Surely knows.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1x5B44OPfZxd-32UBeGT-0a5WVdMf3Jnl](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1x5B44OPfZxd-32UBeGT-0a5WVdMf3Jnl/view?usp=sharing)

**The problem: America picks health plans from one number**

More than 20 million Marketplace enrollees choose coverage off the sticker premium. That guess is expensive.

• In our data, the lowest-premium plan was the lowest-cost option in **0 of 2,000 simulated years**.

• In one example, the cheaper sticker would have cost **$8,052 more** in a single bad year.

• That's one person. Multiply the risk across a family. Across a company.

• This year alone, **four million Americans** found out what their plans actually cost — and walked away from coverage.

We compute.

**Surely — the cost engine**

Surely ranks all plans by what they'll actually cost: premiums, deductibles, drug tiers, networks, out-of-pocket caps. Every number sourced from government filings.

**Inveto — the denial workbench**

Clinics upload a denial and the clinical record; Inveto produces source-cited, physician-signed appeals and supported prior authorizations. Live with real clinics across Texas, Georgia, and California today.

**The moat is the join**

Every contract-authorized Inveto outcome becomes rights-cleared data about what plans actually do, including approvals, denials, appeals; Surely reads all of it. **What plans cost + what plans do. Nobody else has both.**

**Why now**

In 2028, health plans stop renewing automatically: 20 million+ people will re-choose coverage every single year — the largest forced re-shop in the history of American health insurance. $150 billion a year in premiums, re-decided annually.

And employers are next. The federal government projects **800,000 companies and 11 million+ people** will switch to ICHRA, where employees choose their own plans. That's a **trillion-dollar shift**. With Insurf, employers can expect to save **\~$5,000 per employee, per year**.

**Who we are**

Two friends who met during orientation at Brown. Chang got into medical school at 17, then worked a pharmacy counter watching thousands of people pay out of pocket for what they were promised. Bryan placed internationally in CS and physics competitions and has published IEEE research since high school.

**Our ask**

• Tired of overpaying for health insurance?

• Weighing ICHRA, or trying to cut your company's benefits spend?

• Running a specialty clinic buried in denials and prior auths?

See how much your company can save here: [insurf.io/audit](https://www.insurf.io/audit) or email [founders@insurf.io](mailto:founders@insurf.io) — we'll show you exactly what you'd save.

**Everyone sells plans. Nobody prices them. We compute.**

launches.title: Data center development is broken. We fix that.
launches.tagline: Helping American local governments steward American industrial innovation
launches.body:
Local governments are the backbone of industrial development - through zoning codes, they determine where, when, and how anything gets built.

Today, data centers are landing in cities whose zoning codes never imagined them, and local governments are scrambling to respond. They need months of work before a single line of new code gets drafted - that means comparing their code with other cities, checking for consistency with state law, and more.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=113860&key=user_uploads/1527348/6d052667-b707-4790-a425-c4173d7010dd)

We built Verdant Code to compress months into days. We automate the sourcing and the analysis so cities spend their time on judgment instead of data retrieval. Long-range planning work that used to take a six-figure consultant engagement now happens in-house as cities intended.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=113860&key=user_uploads/1527348/cd930e43-f7cd-4c12-ade6-8d6d330d081f)

Data center development is a symptom of a larger problem with America's industrial base. Local governments run the code and permitting decisions that gate industrial development, but they run them on decades-old workflows. Local governments spend $11B a year on this work, yet development stalls anyway.

American zoning codes have not caught up with American innovation. It's time for that to change.

launches.title: Verdant: helping cities process permits faster
launches.tagline: Modern permitting and planning software for local governments
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** 

Verdant is building the modern tech infrastructure for local government, and we’re starting with end-to-end permitting software that dramatically cuts local government permit review time. 

We help applicants file complete, compliant applications upfront, then help staff review them - our AI reads documents, plans, and diagrams, then flags issues and drafts the final report. 

**Launch Video**
[ ](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e5VeQc-NIrlNqIHZP-ASPhuE9DwUzouM/view?usp=sharing)
**Our story**

While studying international politics at Georgetown, I spent three years in and around government (Capitol Hill, then DOJ and Deloitte) and kept hitting the same wall: policy sets direction, but execution is throttled by legacy software. My co-founder Jason has worked in govtech for the past four years researching public benefits automation at Georgetown and building govtech products at Holly and Aidy (YC W24) for local governments.

Jason and I connected over our passion for improving local government processes. The people who keep cities running are stretched thin across understaffed offices, and we want to give them the capacity to do more of what they signed up for. After interviewing 200+ local government staff, we learned that permitting is one of their most painful processes and their software has not done enough to help.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104860&key=user_uploads/3242750/71ea38cf-11ee-427f-8a30-f9381d983c70)

**What we’ve heard**

Permit and entitlement review takes too long, and local government staff are overwhelmed. Applicants often apply with incorrect information, triggering rounds of back-and-forth with the government. And once complete materials are finally in, understaffed departments can’t review everything quickly enough. 

Pandemic-era incumbent contracts are churning because staff are frustrated with expensive legacy systems that only intake and track permits – no automation involved. Our end-to-end solution picks up where those systems stop, automating the review itself to fix permitting where it's most broken.

**What we’re building**

Say a homeowner wants to renovate their house. Before anything else, they have to figure out which permits and entitlements they need. Verdant starts here: applications chat with an AI agent trained on the city ordinances to determine what to apply for. From there, we route applications to a Turbo Tax-style permitting intake portal that guides them through the application, answers their questions, and flags gaps before submission, so what lands on the staff's desk is correct and compliant.

After submission, our AI helps building officials and planners run completeness checks on applications, flagging errors in site plans and drawings. When the application is approved, Verdant uses the context already gathered to draft the next deliverable, whether that's a staff report for the planning commission or a memo for city council.

Beyond the permit lifecycle, Verdant also supports long-range planning: our ordinance research tools let local governments compare how other jurisdictions have written their codes so they have reference points when updating their own.

**Our asks**

* Reach out! If you work in local government (planners, building officials, community developers, city managers, etc.) we’d love to chat.
* Spread the word! If you know anyone in the permitting or planning space, we’d love to connect with them.

 

**Contact us at [founders@verdantapp.com](mailto:founders@verdantapp.com)**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kh9h-H6lO_M>

The last decade of social platforms optimized for content you consume by yourself. But the most durable thing online has always been doing things together, and games are the most natural way people connect. We think the next great social platform is one where friends play, not scroll.

**What we built**

Describe a game, make it, and play it.

* Solo and multiplayer
* 2D and 3D, playable on the web and on Android (iOS coming soon)
* Everything is social, with room codes, leaderboards, likes, comments, and creator profiles

Every game is a link, so it spreads through group chats and Discord instead of dying after one play.

20,000+ creators and 100,000+ monthly active users, growing organically, much of it through discovery via AI tools like ChatGPT. The loop is working: users make things, share them, and their friends come back to play and make their own.

**Where this goes**

Gaming is already bigger than film and music combined, and Roblox showed that handing creation tools to players can build a $40B company. AI takes that further: when making a game costs one sentence, games stop being products and become a language, made in minutes, shared like memes, personalized to the exact people playing them.

name: Rise Reforming
long_description:
Geopolitical conflicts and natural disasters frequently expose the vulnerability of the American chemical industry. The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Localized production using an undervalued resource: biogas. The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether.

Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals. Our beachhead market is dimethyl ether (DME), used as an aerosol propellant and a low-carbon fuel additive in propane. Our target market is methanol: an established billion $ chemical and the future of low-carbon shipping.

We're doing our pilot project at a Chicagoland wastewater plant. This will be the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demo in the Americas.

We're hiring for a senior chemical process engineer. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rise-reforming/jobs/wJ9Q9nv-senior-chemical-process-engineer

Floracene lets any healthcare operator describe the internal tool they need and deploy it in one click - connected to production data, with read and write access scoped by the user. Think Lovable or Retool, except purpose-built for the needs of healthcare business that has no engineering team.

The bottleneck in healthcare isn't building anymore. Anyone can vibecode an 80% solution in an afternoon, custom to their own workflow, with people already on staff. The tool then dies locally on the builder’s computer, because IT (correctly) won't let anyone deploy a tool touching PHI without first-class authentication and permissioning. Our first customer had multiple employees who had each built useful tools and dashboards locally, but couldn’t actually share these with coworkers or connect to their core practice data. Within weeks of implementing Floracene, they were able to consolidate their BI tooling into Floracene and shipped 4 net-new to production.

A staggering ~$200B is spent on administrative software in healthcare every year in the US. Tens of thousands of those companies still run core operations on spreadsheets, and we're at the top of the first inning of AI adoption.

Asaph and Jonah met on the hospitals team at Palantir two years ago, and have each spent the last four years in the plumbing of US healthcare: claims, eligibility, and payor contracting. Asaph was an early PM at Garner. Jonah was a founding engineer at Metriport (YC S22) after starting his own fax-automation startup for fertility clinics.
