* Andrew Tran studied CS at Yale. At Yale, he trained LLMs to reason over multi-modal biological data. At Ramp and Hudson River Trading, he worked closely with data teams to build out ergonomic tooling for data engineers and researchers.
* Rick Gao studied CS at Yale. He was previously at Verition Fund Management, where he worked with internal data teams and counterparties to develop ingestion pipelines and internal financial models.
* Tony Li studied CS and Math at Yale. During his time at Carthage Capital and ByteDance, he worked with data engineering teams to build data pipelines, data analysis, and agentic tooling.

Check out <https://alkera.ai> and reach out at [contact@alkera.ai](mailto:contact@alkera.ai). We’d love to showcase a demo, learn more about your data teams’ pain points, and share more about how Alkera can help supercharge them.

name: Definite
long_description:
Definite is where finance teams build everyday back-office agents on one live model of their books. We plug into your ERP, ledger, payroll, and payments read-only and compile everything into one clean model that stays current as money moves. Your back-office team then builds agents on top in plain English. We never write back and we never move money. The agents are yours, the plumbing is ours.

We met in first year computer science at Waterloo and interned at Meta, Optiver, and BitGo. At Optiver they ran an n8n hackathon and the interns automated basically nothing. It couldn't talk to the systems that mattered. When we pitched banks and fintechs on agents, they kept telling us the same thing. The agent isn't the hard part, getting clean data out of their systems is.

Right now, automating anything in a back office means engineers hand-stitching data from a dozen sources in different formats on different schedules. Tools like n8n and Workato assume your data is already clean and joined. In finance it never is. So the teams with the most repetitive work and smallest budgets get nothing.

The hard part is the compiler. Every source gets cleaned, matched, and joined into one live model of transactions, invoices, vendors, and payments, and it has to stay right as money lands every day. 

Everyone throws engineers at this. We're doing it once so nobody has to again. Every back office is getting agents eventually. Whoever owns the data they read from owns the thing all of them depend on, and eventually the books themselves. That's what we're building.

launches.tagline: The most accurate AI agents for financial reporting
launches.body:
_AI agents that run the entire regulatory reporting pipeline for banks, from raw ledger data to the filed report._

**_TL;DR_**_: Definite automates regulatory reporting for banks end to end, from raw ledger data to filed report, turning weeks of manual work into hours._ [usedefinite.com](http://usedefinite.com)

Hey! We're Gurshabd, Mazin and Farhan from Definite.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ji1ae8y_V4E>

**The Problem**

Proving to regulators that their books follow the rules is a constant, non-negotiable obligation for banks. Each report is thousands of numbers, personally signed off by an executive. Getting it wrong can mean a **fine up to a million dollars** over a single undetected error. Producing that proof is slow, and doesn't even guarantee it's correct. 

Here's where the current system breaks down:

1. **Wasted Hours:** A controller pulls data from the core system into Excel and maps it line by line by hand. By regulators' own estimate, one quarterly filing takes weeks of employee time, time pulled from higher-value finance work every quarter.
2. **False Confidence:** The software banks use to file checks formatting, not truth. A loan mapped to the wrong schedule line sails through every check. Nothing catches it until an examiner does, and by then it's not a mistake, it's a violation.

**The Solution**

**Report agents:** We connect to your books and our agents build the reports you owe.

**Verification engine:** Every number is recomputed from source records and checked against a versioned rulebook, so each line carries its rule and source data.

**Self-correcting agents:** When a check fails, the agent gets the reason and fixes it in seconds. Real exceptions come to your team with a drafted explanation, not a blank error. This loop is why our agents are the most accurate in finance.

**Receipts:** Every check produces a tamper-evident receipt you can hand an examiner or auditor.

Your team reviews and signs instead of building.

**How we got here**

Gurshabd worked at BitGo, a regulated crypto custodian, where attestations proving customer assets matched the ledger were built by hand every period. Farhan worked at Meta where he delved extensively into machine learning and building AI agents. Mazin saw Optiver recheck daily regulatory numbers by hand, then built LLM agents at [Boosted.ai](http://Boosted.ai) and learned finance people won't act on AI output unless every number comes with its source.

The lesson from all three: in finance, producing a number is cheap, proving it is the job. On two public reporting benchmarks, DeepSeek V3 with our verification engine outperformed GPT-5 on reconciliation accuracy (FinBalance) at roughly 50× lower cost, and beat the entire published field on XBRL calculation validation (FinAuditing).

launches.body:
EdotEnv (YC S26) is a Quant Neolab building toward RSI. They turn markets into self-improving research environments for AI agents.

The path to RSI is a continuous loop: agents conduct experiments, learn from the results, and autonomously become better at conducting the next round of research. For that loop to continue, each round must present a harder problem than the last.

Markets create this dynamic naturally. Every discovered inefficiency attracts competition, and every successful strategy makes future opportunities harder to find. Markets therefore provide an advancing frontier for self-improving agents.

EdotEnv captures this process in multi-step environments where agents form hypotheses, design experiments, verify results and iterate. They use these environments to evaluate and post-train agents on increasingly difficult research tasks.

They work with frontier AI labs and academic groups building research harnesses, evaluation benchmarks, and post-training environments.

EdotEnv's team previously worked in quantitative research at G-Research, high frequency options trading at TransMarket Group, and LLM inference research at Etched.

launches.title: Standard Machines. Teaching AI to Design Advanced Chips.
launches.tagline: Standard Machines builds environments to train and evaluate models on advanced chip design tasks. We work with frontier labs to push their model capabilities.
launches.body:
**The Idea**

Advancement in AI relies on chips. Transformers won because they mapped well to GPUs. Frontier Labs are now co-designing their own silicon to maximize intelligence/joule.

It takes years and 100s of experts to bring a chip from architecture through tape-out.

Our goal as a company is to push the frontier of AI on chip design tasks - enabling advanced chips to be taped-out by small teams in months.

We also believe this is the path forward to achieving true recursive self-improvement (RSI). Where AI designs better chips and better chips train more intelligent AI.

To achieve this, we're building **RL Environments For Long-Horizon Chip Design.**

Our environments enable 1000s of parallel rollouts for training on chip design tasks. We also curate a private held-out test set for performing evals in the environment to compare model capabilities.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111880&key=user_uploads/1978488/da8f5344-b2f0-4613-b8ef-5ee18a23300c)

---

**What Exists**

Chip design should be a perfect domain for this type of RL. Instead:

\- The academic benchmarks are one-shot puzzles of \~100 lines, and they're in every training set.

\- The field's de facto standard (NVIDIA's CVDP) has saturated - going from 34% to 97% once agents could iterate against the grader.

\- The published tasks are short-horizon and graded by running testbenches. In one study, designs that passed their bundled testbenches 95-97% of the time were only \~20% correct under formal checking.

And none of it resembles the real loop: months of work, tools in the loop, and hard trade-offs between latency, throughput, area, and power.

---

**What We Build**

Our RL Environment is designed for long-horizon chip design tasks.

\- **Long-horizon.** One episode is the real loop: choose a microarchitecture, write the RTL, simulate, synthesize, check timing and power, revise.

\- **Reliable grading.** Every task is an executable contract with exact checking. No LLM judge anywhere in the reward path. Correctness is a hard gate: a fast, small, wrong chip earns zero.

\- **Physics as the yardstick.** Every task ships with a computed speed-of-light bound: the best the physics of the task allows. Scores are reported as a fraction of that bound, so they're comparable across tasks.

\- **The full trade-off.** Real chips are trade-offs. We record area, power, latency, and throughput as an unreduced vector - labs can scalarize this into a terminal reward for training however they want.

\- **Deterministic.** Every graded result replays bit-identically on another machine.

---

**Why Now**

Chip Design is increasingly something the frontier labs care about. They are all designing their own custom inference chips. Anthropic is already hiring chip-design RL engineers at $500-850k to build these types of environments in-house - and there’s currently no yardstick that hasn’t been saturated.

---

**Who We Are**

I was the first intern & youngest hire into GPU Architecture at Apple, working with industry-leading architects.

I've seen how leading-edge chips get designed end-to-end: what the loop looks like, and how the power/perf/area trade-offs actually get graded.

Our environments run that same loop & formalize that grading.

**Asks**

If you’re working on RL, post-training, or data at a lab or neolab, or interested in post-training models for chip-design capabilities. Please reach out, [founders@standardmachines.com](https://www.standardmachines.com/launch).

---

Read our full launch post, [here](https://standardmachines.com/launch).

launches.tagline: Field Robots Faster with ATC Deploy
launches.body:
Today we're sharing Agency Tool Company and our first product, ATC Deploy: a faster, more reliable way to ship software to robots wherever they are. It moves updates up to 20 times faster than docker pull or scp and works with any software stack already in use.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jx0rLRVa06s>

## The updates that took until 2 a.m.

Davis and I spent eight years building Scythe Robotics and putting hundreds of autonomous mowers to work across the country. For years, we deployed software with a tool I'd cobbled together for our first few robots. As the fleet grew, deployment became an ordeal: engineers stayed up until 2 a.m., we coordinated with customers to move robots out of sheds and into LTE coverage at set times, and failed transfers restarted from zero. Shipping a fix could take more coordination than building it. We had models to train and customers to serve, so the tooling limped along with incremental bandaids.

We've since heard the same story from robotics teams across industries. That deployment becomes a hidden bottleneck: teams become release-averse, feedback loops slow and improvements stall. Stitched-together web and IoT tools barely work if you know which scripts to run and who to call, so they survive, even if it means every update is distracting from improving the product.

## What we built

ATC Deploy ships whatever you already run: OS images, Docker images, or any file tree. Run “atc ota push user@robot”, and it sends only the changed bytes, then restarts your software through hooks you define—way faster than a docker push.

Install takes one “curl | sh” command and a config file so you can get back to work fast. Interrupted transfers resume where they stopped, and an offline robot can receive updates by USB if you need. There's no new runtime, packaging format, or operating system to adopt.

## Shipping to robots today

ATC Deploy already ships software to robots at Burro, which has deployed more than 750 machines worldwide, Tempo, polishing concrete across several US states and Canada, and Gather, who is scaling their 99.9% accurate inventory drones nationwide. Their teams spend less time managing delivery and more time improving the robot.

**Operate a robot fleet? Join the ATC Deploy waitlist at [agencytool.com](https://agencytool.com/).** Know a team that should be using it? Send them this post, or to [mailbox@agencytool.com](mailto:mailbox@agencytool.com).

launches.tagline: AI that finds the money your company is losing
launches.body:
TL;DR: We made an AI system that reads through a company's information (communications, documents, databases - whatever they want to analyze) and finds concrete, actionable steps they can take to improve their business and make it more efficient.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SxuAHO3-0WEjPPqZUkK-39jWfitRvlQj](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SxuAHO3-0WEjPPqZUkK-39jWfitRvlQj/view?usp=sharing)

**The Product** 

Large companies are extremely complex systems. As soon as a company scales past fifty or so employees, it becomes totally impossible for an executive to know every single thing that happens at a company. This means that, since everyone at a company only understands a small slice of what's going on, it's essentially inevitable that inefficiencies arise on a global level that aren't visible at smaller scales. Before Cerenovus, this was a very difficult problem to tackle, because there was just too much information for any one person to have the whole picture. Cerenovus changes this.

**Here's how Cerenovus works:**

First, Cerenovus ingests the company's information. This looks differently for every company based on their priorities and existing systems, but typically this means hooking into documents, communications and databases that the company wants to analyze, and bringing all the information together in one place.

Next, Cerenovus runs an AI-powered synthesis pipeline to organize the information and map out all existing systems and workflows. Once the system has mapped out how things work at a company, it scans for a wide variety of common failure modes, and does open-ended analysis to find places where processes can be streamlined. Finally, its findings are compiled into polished, cited briefs, reviewed and validated by humans, and then shipped back to our clients.

We're looking to sell to any business interested in optimizing their business, making sense of information, and leveraging AI to the greatest extent possible. However, the people that can use our product the most are the ones that do this kind of optimization repeatedly: private equity value creation teams, exit planners, and operational consulting firms.

**The Lore**

We're three ex-Harvard nerds who were brainstorming in a library one night, and found that we were all (in different ways) interested in the problem of knowledge organization. Jonathan was obsessed with building out a personal "second brain" for himself in Obsidian; Ollie had worked on building agent harnesses that could self-improve by updating their internal knowledge base; and Lucas had seen how, whenever a company got acquired by the private equity firm he worked at, people within the company didn't have the full picture of how work got done. We decided to leave school and build our idea together, and the months since have been a blur of coding, conferences, and customer calls.

We'd love to be connected to:

\- Private Equity Value Creation Teams

\- Exit Planners

\- Operational Consultants

\- Innovative middle-market businesses looking to improve their operations

launches.title: Molagri: Resistance-free pesticides 🪲
launches.tagline: Species-specific biopesticides built from engineered insect viruses, updatable the moment pests develop resistance.
launches.body:
**TLDR:** We build next-generation pesticides from engineered insect virus-like particles. They target a single pest species, stay safe for humans, pollinators, and the environment, and can be reprogrammed over time as pests evolve resistance.

Pesticides underpin modern agriculture and food security, accounting for $80B in annual spend. Without effective pesticides, we can't grow enough food.

<https://youtu.be/6rxXDJeC14Y>

**The Problem 🌱**

Pests are developing resistance faster than new pesticides can be invented to replace the failing ones. At the same time, regulators are banning core active ingredients over environmental and human toxicity. Farmers are losing tools from both ends at once.

**Our Solution 🪲**

We build pesticides out of insect virus-like particles. We start with a virus that only infects insects and is harmless to humans. We strip out its genome so it can't infect or replicate, and we keep the empty protein shell as a delivery vehicle.

We engineer that shell with two parts:

* A **targeting element** that recognizes a single pest species (or a set of species). This is what keeps the product species-specific and invisible to humans, pollinators, and beneficial insects.
* A **payload** that kills the pest.

Both parts are swappable. Changing the targeting element will modify which pest it kills. Changing the payload will result in a new kill mechanism for the same pest, which is how we update the product when resistance appears.

Designing for true pollinator safety is hard, so we did the underlying science ourselves. We solved a cryo-EM structure of a key receptor in honey bees, which lets us deliberately engineer our targeting elements so they do not bind pollinators.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108796&key=user_uploads/2273508/62f4362a-1938-4843-ab26-c9a62c742a84)

**Why Us? 🧑🏽‍🔬**

We are Zaky and Min, viral structural biology PhD candidates and lab mates at the University of Toronto, where we have worked together for the past 6 years studying how viruses interact with their hosts. We have published in Nature Microbiology and Nature Communications, and Min holds the world record for the highest-resolution structure of a coronavirus spike protein.

**Traction 📈**

We have signed our first grower LOI, have more in the pipeline, and produced our first set of viruses for testing. During the batch we also solved a cryo-EM structure of a honey-bee receptor that directly informs our pollinator-safe design.

**Connect with us!**

* **Growers and producers**: if you are fighting resistant pests or losing tools to bans, we would love to talk about your crops and target pests. Reach us at [molagri.com](http://molagri.com) 
* **Everyone else:** intros to ag and crop-science operators, or anyone who has built regulated biological products, are always welcome.

launches.title: Peer: AI-Native Freight Brokerage
launches.tagline: Peer brokers every load autonomously, from quote to delivery.
launches.body:
Freight brokerages in 2026 look like stock trading floors in 1989. Rooms of people on phones, quoting prices from memory, faxing paperwork across the country. Then electronic trading showed up and those floors emptied out. Peer (YC S26) is that moment for trucking.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IsbGimgbdogUQdADAzDloIuPn9zQgEJi](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IsbGimgbdogUQdADAzDloIuPn9zQgEJi/view?usp=sharing)

Trucking is a $900 billion industry, and 91.5% of American trucking companies run ten trucks or fewer. Nobody shipping freight can manage hundreds of those relationships, so they hand the load to a broker, who finds the right truck, in the right place, at the right price.

Peer is an AI-native freight brokerage. A shipper sends Peer a load and agents do everything after that: price it, find and vet the trucking company, handle the paperwork, track the delivery, and fix what goes wrong on the road. Even the most tech-forward incumbents need thousands of people to run a brokerage. Peer runs on agents, doing far more loads with far fewer people.

Shippers want a fair price fast, a truck that is insured, and a trucking company that shows up. An agent quotes market rates in minutes instead of days of emails, because it reads the request the moment it lands. It catches a lapsed insurance policy before the freight moves, because it rechecks continuously, not once at signup. And it drops a trucking company that keeps failing, because it has no relationship to protect.

Aaron and Felix are both technical and both dropped out of Harvey Mudd to build Peer. Aaron built voice AI for trucking fleets at Waylens and researched AI agents at the MIT Media Lab. Felix worked in machine learning at Magnefy and shipped AI tools to the LA Department of Water and Power. Together they won the Google DeepMind Hackathon at UCLA.

launches.body:
**TL;DR: Stratum builds AI agents that automate the slow, manual processes governments run on. We're starting with application review - clearing backlogs in a fraction of the time and saving agencies tens of billions a year.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108362&key=user_uploads/1648613/f70bb601-955f-4c6c-946f-8d8c90d04fa6)

**The problem**

Governments run on manual work. Millions of complex processes - reviews, approvals, filings, claims -are still handled by hand, one file at a time, on software built long before AI existed.

Take application review. Every permit, license, patent, drug approval, and benefits claim in America is reviewed by hand, one file at a time. Millions sit in queues while people wait months and years: veterans on disability ratings, families on pensions, builders on permits.

The tools reviewers open every morning were built long before AI. So the work stays manual, and the queue only grows.

This isn't one broken workflow. It's how the entire government runs.

**What Stratum does**

Stratum builds AI agents that automate the slow, complex, manual processes governments run on.

We're starting with application review.

A reviewer uploads an application and selects the rubric to check it against. From there, an agent takes over: it plans the review, works through the file end to end, and checks every requirement, routing each step to the right model.

A human approves every outcome, and every step is fully auditable.

The difference is scale. Instead of one reviewer on one file, hundreds of agents run in parallel — clearing an entire backlog in the time it once took to review a single application.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108362&key=user_uploads/1648613/e23f9409-271f-4879-95aa-374eb37ae64f)

**Who we are**

We're Vihaan (VJ) and Raj - brothers.

Vihaan (CTO): founding engineer #3 at Cadastral (acquired by Legora), waterloo dropout.

Raj (CEO): led GTM at Deel, dropped out of CS grad school at the University of Bath.

**Where this goes**

Application review is the first workflow. The mission is to integrate AI across every vertical inside the government.

Governments are among the largest, most complex organizations on earth — and almost none of it has been touched by modern AI. We're changing that, saving agencies tens, eventually hundreds, of billions a year and making the government one of the most efficient institutions in the world.

Looking to bring AI into your agency? Reach out to the team or book a demo [stratumindustries.co](https://stratumindustries.co/)

Contact: [founders@stratumindustries.co](mailto:founders@stratumindustries.co)

launches.title: Stratum Industries - clearing the entire U.S. Government backlog
launches.tagline: AI agents that review government applications end-to-end, so backlogs that took years clear in minutes.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Stratum builds AI agents that clear the U.S. government's backlog. A reviewer drops in an application, picks the rubric to check it against, and an agent plans, executes, and reviews the file end to end. Hundreds run in parallel with a human approving every decision, so a backlog that used to take months clears in the time it took to review one file.

**The Problem**

Every permit, license, patent, drug approval, grants and benefits claim in America has to be reviewed by a government adjudicator, on software built decades before AI. The result is millions of applications stuck in queues, and real people waiting months or years: veterans on disability ratings, families on pensions, builders on permits. The approval isn't the problem. The software it runs on is.

**How Stratum Works**

1. A reviewer drops in an application and selects the rubric it needs to be checked against.
2. An agent reads every page and checks the file against that rubric.
3. Every step routes to the model that reviews it most accurately for the least cost.
4. Anything missing goes back to the applicant as one specific request.
5. The officer gets the whole file summarized, with every citation behind it, and approves or denies it.

Hundreds of these run in parallel in the cloud, with full auditability at every step, and a person always makes the final call.

launches.body:
Hey everyone! We’re David and Michael, co-founders of FlowManual.

**What FlowManual is**: AI preconstruction for General and MEP contractors, executing projects while cutting risk. 

**TL;DR:** Construction contractors waste hundreds of hours monthly on manual tasks, sifting through 500-page PDFs only to miss fine print that can cost tens of thousands. FlowManual automates the back-office work before and during construction, so teams can reliably secure and complete projects faster than ever before.

<https://youtu.be/aO5fBj_3kpU>\
\
**The Problem:**

Meet Jeremy. He’s a project manager at a mid-sized contractor, and his job is to secure projects and then make sure the company doesn’t lose money on already thin margins.

A bid invite lands in his inbox. To put together one number his firm can send in, Jeremy has to read thousands of pages. A 400-page project manual, drawings, insurance, spec sections, and so much more. Buried somewhere inside all this print is a line that can ultimately decide whether this job makes or loses money. From a liquidated-damages clause to a scope item sneakily handed to the mechanical contractor, if Jeremy misses it, it’s a $5K-$10K mistake.

Jeremy’s got one week, three other bids on his desk, and no way to read all of it as carefully as he’d like. So he reads what he can and sends in a number.

Say he wins. A change in the signed contract by the General Contractor or a sneaky difference in vendor pricing costs the company thousands after the fact. Every step of the way requires hundreds of pages of reading and referencing done under a deadline. And Jeremy does this for every job.

**The Solution:**\
FlowManual automates these historical workflows that contractors run on, allowing teams to submit bids and complete projects faster than ever before. Here’s a couple major features:

* AI Takeoffs from drawings
* Drawing comparisons / overlay
* Bid leveling
* Contract Review

Our software doesn’t do the job for you, but it works alongside you to reduce time spent and mistakes made.

**About Us:**\
Michael and David were college roommates and engineers at Harvard. When renovations for a heater in our dorm took 6 weeks, we poked at the problem, realizing it stems from a larger issue. Through hundreds of conversations with professionals, we found an industry that ran on file cabinets, Excel, and page-by-page manual review.\
\
**Our Ask:**

* **Know anyone in construction?** Connections to anyone in the industry, including on the legal and tech side, is greatly appreciated. Anyone in Project Management, Business Development, Marketing, IT are ideal! Reach us at [founders@flowmanual.com](mailto:founders@flowmanual.com) 
* **Feedback, intros, or just want to chat?** Book a call with us, or email [founders@flowmanual.com](mailto:founders@flowmanual.com)!

launches.body:
Hey YC, we’re Sahil, Maki, and Tony. We’re building Pluto ([talentpluto.com](https://talentpluto.com/))

Resumes made careers readable. LinkedIn made them searchable. Pluto makes them understood.

<https://youtu.be/gMuOogxpSo4>

**TL;DR** - A professional talks to Pluto for 10 minutes about what they’ve done, what they’re great at, and what they want next. Pluto makes that context discoverable to the right people and AI agents, helping them understand the person more fully. When there’s a real fit, Pluto can also make a warm introduction to a startup.

18K+ professionals have already shared their career context with Pluto. 100+ companies use Pluto to meet people with their full story, including Mercor, David AI, Rho, Warp, and Runlayer.

**Ask:** Talk to Pluto and let it get to know your work. If you’re hiring, send us the role and we’ll introduce you to people with context and confirmed interest.

### **The problem**

A resume and online profile are not enough for the AI era.

They show where someone worked and what title they had. They do not capture what the person actually did, what they are unusually good at, and what they want next.

That context usually lives in conversations. So professionals get reduced to keywords, logos, and titles, while the people and AI agents trying to understand them are left with an incomplete picture. 

Hiring makes this problem obvious. Companies miss great people because the real signal never makes it online. But as AI agents increasingly help people find, evaluate, and connect with one another, every professional will need a richer, more accurate way to be understood.

### **The solution**

Pluto is an AI voice agent that understands a professional’s career and puts that understanding to work.

Professionals talk to Pluto for 10 minutes about their experience, strengths, goals, preferences, and what they want to keep private. Pluto asks follow-up questions, remembers the context missing from their resume, and makes them discoverable to the right people and AI agents.

Companies tell Pluto who they want to meet. Pluto searches its network and the broader market, understands fit on both sides, privately confirms interest, and makes a warm introduction when both sides want to connect. No mass applications. Professionals stay private and in control. Companies meet people who are already understood.

**How It Works**

1. Talk to Pluto for 10 minutes
2. Review what it learned and choose what to share
3. Get found and understood by the right people and AI agents
4. Get introduced to startups when there’s a fit

### **Why We Started This**

The best hiring has always happened through trusted, high-context introductions. We think AI can make that possible for everyone.

Warm introductions are one way Pluto puts that understanding to work today. Long term, Pluto becomes the career context layer for the AI era - the version of a professional’s story that agents can understand, trust, and act on, while the professional stays in control.

### **Our Ask**

If you’re a professional, talk to Pluto and let it get to know your work. 

If you’re a founder, hiring leader, or talent engineer, send us the role you’re hiring for.

[talentpluto.com](http://talentpluto.com)

\- Sahil, Maki, Tony

launches.body:
TLDR: machine0 is a CLI for agent compute: “machine0 new mybox” gives your agent a full cloud VM, billed by the minute, from $0.013/hr up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB and 8×H100s. Agents drive it themselves via CLI or MCP.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gyllkZ0M04E>

## The Pain

Agent workloads are moving from ephemeral to always-on. A coding agent working on a hard feature runs 6-8 hours. Auto-research agents run for days. OpenClaw & Hermes run 24/7. As you run more in parallel:

* **Resources**: a few agents on a big codebase saturate your RAM and CPU. Auto-research needs GPUs you don't have.
* **Security**: “—yolo” on your personal machine is one prompt injection away from exfiltrated credentials.
* **Availability**: close your laptop and the agent dies mid-task.
* **Isolation**: there's no clean line between everything on your laptop and the minimum this agent actually needs.

## The Solution

machine0 gives every agent its own computer. It's a CLI that both humans and agents can use without reading docs:

* “machine0 new mybox” creates an SSH-ready VM with a static IP and HTTPS endpoint. Always on (99.99% uptime) until you switch it off.
* **Billed by the minute.** 1 vCPU / 1 GB at $0.013/hr up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB, plus GPUs from RTX 4000 Ada to 8×H100s.
* **Profiles.** Bundles of MCP connections, credentials, prompts, and env vars, injected at VM creation. Each agent gets exactly the capabilities (or personality) you choose, and nothing else.
* **Agents self-serve.** Hand the CLI or MCP server to Claude, Codex, or OpenCode and it manages its own fleet: spin up a box for a build, snapshot it, tear it down.
* **Suspend & resume.** Pause an idle machine, stop paying for compute, resume exactly where it left off.
* **Snapshot & clone.** Configure one machine perfectly, then stamp out ten identical agents from it.
* **NixOS is first-class.** Declarative, reproducible machines.

## How people use it

* **Compute for your agent**: give it the CLI and it spins up its own VMs for builds, tests, and long jobs instead of grinding your laptop.
* **Hosting the agent itself**: run Claude, Codex or Hermes 24/7. Snapshot once, then clone as many as you want.
* **Swarms of agents**: an orchestrator agent spawns worker machines, farms out subtasks, and tears them down when the work is done.
* **Auto-Research on GPUs**: drop an agent on an H100 with a goal and let it run for days.

## About me

I'm a solo, second-time YC founder. I was CTO of Upflow (YC W20), where I scaled EPD post series A and personally owned DevOps, infra, and security for years because they were too high-stakes to delegate. Upflow handles sensitive accounting data for companies like Postman, ProductBoard, and Lattice, and is doing many millions in ARR.

Before that I built consumer payments at Hike Messenger (100M+ users) in India. Working with sensitive data and infra for years is what got me deep into the problems machine0 solves, security especially.

## Asks 🙏

* Try it: <https://machine0.io>
* Let's talk about your agent fleets, software factory or auto-research: [hello@machine0.io](mailto:hello@machine0.io)

launches.tagline: We use AI to help kids learn faster
launches.body:
**Hi everyone - I'm Alex, founder of Bloomy.**

**TL;DR: We help kids learn faster by using AI. In early pilots, students grew \~2x faster than the national average.**

[Bloomy](https://bloomylearning.com) is an AI-powered mastery learning platform for K-12 students. We diagnose students’ skill gaps, place students on a personalized learning path, and give them standards-aligned lessons and a Socratic AI tutor that helps without just giving away the answer.

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/8E5PhhWjtD4>

**Why I'm building this**

I started as a teacher. I taught 7th grade English and Writing with Teach For America, and every day I struggled to deliver differentiated instruction to 30 students with 30 different sets of needs.

Some students needed remediation, some needed acceleration, and many needed a tutor sitting next to them helping them reason through the next step. Benjamin Bloom's 2-sigma result always felt obviously true to me; the hard part was making that kind of tutoring affordable and available to every child.

Then AI changed the cost curve. 

When I saw innovative school concepts such as Alpha School, the model clicked: mastery-based learning, personalization, and high-agency students. But I kept thinking about the families and schools that already exist: homeschool families, microschools, hybrid schools, and regular classrooms where most kids are today.

**What Bloomy does**

Bloomy starts with a diagnostic (we integrate with third-party diagnostics and provide our own in-house one) and places each student onto a personalized learning path. Students work one skill at a time, get a short, standards-aligned lesson, practice, ask BloomyBot for Socratic help when they're stuck, and only move forward after showing 90%+ mastery. The skill path updates live based on the student’s performance and our own knowledge graph.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104376&key=user_uploads/3410278/aff91335-737d-4b76-bcc2-40414d3f3c08)

_Our knowledge graph informs skill progression to make learning more efficient._

Parents and teachers can see what the student has mastered, what's in progress, and where they need support.

**Where we are**

We're being adopted in many different contexts: districts with traditional schools, charter schools, hybrid schools, microschools, homeschools, and even families who just want some extra academic support for their kids.

Families can subscribe to Bloomy monthly or annually, and families using ESA/EFA funds may also qualify for direct pay or reimbursement depending on their state’s rules.

Before Bloomy, I taught with TFA, earned my Master’s in Education, designed GMAT and GRE curriculum for Manhattan Prep, led Lyft’s driver growth team for New England, earned an MBA from Stanford, and managed AI transformation engagements at McKinsey. Bloomy is the thing that combines all the aspects of my career: learning design, go-to-market, and AI.

If you want to reach out, you can email me at [alex@bloomylearning.com](mailto:alex@bloomylearning.com) or follow our updates on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/bloomy-yc-s26/).

launches.title: 6thSense — Giving Robots Touch
launches.tagline: Giving Robots Touch
launches.body:
6thSense builds wearable tactile sensing rigs that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and pose — across touch, vision, depth, force, and 3D hand pose, all in real environments. We sell that multimodal data to the companies training the next generation of dexterous robots.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gXx53tcIv5U>

Robots are getting good at seeing. They're still terrible at touching. That's because there's almost no data capturing what a hand actually feels while doing real tasks in real homes. Lab data doesn't cut it. We go anywhere and capture the missing layer that manipulation models need to learn fine motor control.

What makes our data different is the hardware we built to collect it. Our tactile sensing devices are designed and manufactured in-house, purpose-built to capture the richest touch signal in the industry — with scale in mind from the very beginning, enabling us to actually solve the tactile data problem. Every sensor maps directly to how robotic skin needs to work: a 1-to-1 analog for the tactile arrays going into the next generation of robot hands. That means the data we collect today doesn't just train better policies. It transfers directly to the hardware it's meant to run on. The team comes from Tesla, Mecka, Samsung, DoorDash, and Amazon, with expertise across hardware, sensors, ML, robotics, and software at scale. If you're training a manipulation policy or need custom tactile data, reach out.

name: Nori
long_description:
We manufacture Nori: A sub-$2000 bimanual mobile manipulator that can clean rooms, restock shelves, and fold clothes. Nori can handle basic tasks out of the box, and its software lets anyone teach Nori to automate work specific to their home or business. 

Nori aims to solve the robotics data bottleneck. By deploying affordable robots to customers around the world, we can gather the diverse data required to train the next generation of generalist robotic policies. Every user of Nori makes Nori smarter.

Since launching 6 weeks ago we have already deployed our first robot and have over $440k+ in sales.

We can bring general-purpose robotics to homes and businesses that could never afford it before. There are 132.7 million households and 8.4 million employer business locations in the U.S. At $1,688 per robot, selling just one Nori to 0.5% of them represents a $1.2B market opportunity in the U.S. alone.
one_liner: The most capable American-made humanoid robot for $1,688

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Robots are finally capable enough to be useful, but they're priced like cars, not appliances. A capable humanoid costs $20,000+, so general-purpose robots stay in labs and pilots instead of homes. 

It's a big problem because household labor is one of the largest unpriced markets in the world. Today's answer is a stack of single-task machines, a dishwasher, a washer, a vacuum, each $600 to $1,000 and doing exactly one thing. Whoever ships a general-purpose robot at appliance prices doesn't win a niche, they open consumer robotics the way the PC opened computing.

We're robotics researchers from Columbia (RoboPIL, CGUI). After years watching \[$100K research robots struggle with tasks cheap hardware could handle\], we realized the gap between lab robots and home robots isn't intelligence, it's cost discipline. Nobody was going to fix that from inside a lab, so we left to build it: a $1,688 robot anyone can teach.

**TL;DR** Ooak Data turns internal company data into a training ground where AI agents can be tested on real work.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EgbFzN-g4cVY-dk7ZPH6gR37F28D56xo](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EgbFzN-g4cVY-dk7ZPH6gR37F28D56xo/view?usp=sharing)

**The problem**

AI agents still fail on real work: the messy, multi-tool, permission-heavy workflows inside actual companies. You can't synthesize it either, real org charts, permissions, and cross-tool dependencies don't come out of a generator. You have to source it from real companies and make it safe. That's the hard part, and it's what we do.

**Our Solution**

We connect to a company's tools (Gmail, Slack, Notion, Jira, Drive, SharePoint) and anonymize everything into a digital twin: structurally identical, but privacy-safe. Labs use our product to train and evaluate AI agents on real work.

We're working with multiple frontier labs and are now well above 7 figures in revenue. We've cut ingestion-to-delivery time 3x since launch, across data from 20 companies.

name: Graphify Labs
long_description:
Graphify is a Knowledge Graph control plane for enterprise software. The open-source tool has 116K+ GitHub stars and 6.5M+ downloads, and is used in production by engineers at Shopify, Datadog, JP Morgan, American Express, Harvey, Automation Anywhere, and Vanguard.

On top of that graph, our enterprise layer reviews every pull request and formally verifies each code change: it proves the new behavior matches the old, or hands back the exact input that breaks it. That makes it built for the changes teams fear most, like refactors, framework upgrades, and large-scale migrations, where you need proof that nothing broke, not a guess.

The graph updates itself as the code changes and keeps context instead of forgetting it, so your whole team and their coding agents work from one shared, always-current view of the codebase instead of a thousand private threads.

It runs entirely inside your perimeter, fully air-gapped on-premise or self-hosted in your own cloud, so no code or data ever leaves your environment.

launches.title: Graphify Labs: Knowledge Graph Engine for Enterprises 🧠
launches.tagline: Shared memory of your codebase, for humans and agents.
launches.body:
Hey everyone, I'm [Safi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/safi-shamsi/), founder and CEO of [Graphify Labs](https://www.linkedin.com/company/graphify-labs/).

For fifty years, the hard part of software was writing it. AI flipped that overnight. It writes more code than any team can read, and a lot of it is slop. That leaves two **hard problems**: no one can hold the whole codebase in their head, and no one can be sure an AI's change didn't quietly break something. **Graphify solves both.**

**By the numbers**

\- **108K+ GitHub stars**: one of the top five open-source projects ever from a YC company, and the first to cross 100K⭐ mid-batch

\- **5M+ downloads** of the open-source engine

\- **6,000+ signups** on the platform in its first weeks

\- Enterprises already running it in production

**The memory.** One shared, always-current knowledge graph of your whole codebase, across every language and every repo, plus its docs and tickets, so a change in one service shows its impact across all the others. Instead of grepping through files one at a time, your engineers and their AI agents trace how everything connects, who calls what and what a change touches, and answer questions across the entire system, at a **fraction of the tokens**. Agents connect over a single **MCP endpoint**, so the graph works inside Claude Code, Cursor, and every major coding tool. It groups the code into communities, the real subsystems, so teams can plan, onboard, and understand the architecture across the whole **SDLC**.

**The proof.** Graphify reviews every pull request, including changes that span **multiple repositories**, and verifies each one. It writes and runs a test that reproduces the bug, proves the new code behaves exactly like the old, or hands back the exact input that breaks it. Most AI reviewers just have one model comment on another model's code, which is still a guess. **Graphify proves its findings**, because it runs on a real **code graph and formal verification**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111176&key=user_uploads/3674994/e7f719ea-bca0-4c12-a922-12c728426dd4)

**It learns.** Graphify remembers what your team ships and what it rejects, and feeds that back in, so its reviews get sharper over time and stop flagging what your team has already decided is fine.

> Migrating a large codebase with AI is like changing a train's engine while it is moving. Graphify lets you do it without stopping the train, and proves the new version does exactly what the old one did.

**Here's the launch film**:

<https://youtu.be/nvJ1M_GRj8Q>\
\
It also proposes a fix and keeps it only if it re-verifies through the fix loop. Graphify connects to **Jira, Linear, and Sentry** so it knows the ticket a change should satisfy and the production bug it should resolve.

The enterprise layer runs on-prem, so your code never leaves your environment.

**The founder.** [Safi Shamsi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/safi-shamsi/) is a published knowledge graph researcher and the author of The Memory Layer. His research on knowledge-graph retrieval improved retrieval 50% and cut hallucinations 67%. Now he's applying that work to one of the hardest problems in software: giving every engineer and AI agent a shared memory of the codebase, and a way to prove their changes still work.

Soon every line of software will be written or reviewed by an agent. That software will need a memory of itself and proof that it works. **We're building both.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111176&key=user_uploads/3674994/439244a1-338f-46cc-8594-b7c2a74bffcb)

**The ask:** Before September 10 we're taking 10 design partners: a free 14-day build where we deploy the enterprise graph on-prem, with your team \

name: Aerogen Systems
long_description:
We are building the future of chip manufacturing.

Chips are more advanced than ever, and the features inside them keep getting smaller. But the cleanroom infrastructure supporting their manufacture has not scaled at the same pace. Intel, TSMC, Samsung, and others spend billions building and operating massive cleanrooms, only to isolate their most advanced wafers from the surrounding facility as much as possible.

We think that architecture is backwards. Instead of making the entire building cleaner, why not make the machinery itself as clean as possible?

Talos is our proprietary tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor equipment and continuously destroys airborne molecular contaminants before they reach the wafer. Instead of fighting contamination by constantly flooding tools with ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos keeps the environment inside the machine 10–100x cleaner, without the massive purge-gas bill.

Talos is powerful on its own, but it is also the foundation for a much bigger vision: the Cleanpipe.

The Aerogen Systems Cleanpipe is an ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Rather than relying on a billion-dollar cleanroom to protect every cubic foot of factory space, Cleanpipe creates a controlled environment only where cleanliness actually matters: around the wafer.

Talos cleans the tools. Cleanpipe connects them. Eventually, we delete the cleanroom and build more advanced chips, at greater scale, with radically less infrastructure. With cleanpipes connecting tools, chip fabs can exist anywhere.
one_liner: Modernizing Chip Manufacturing Infrastructure

launches.title: Aerogen Systems: Building Chip Fabs Without Cleanrooms
launches.tagline: Redefining the architecture behind chip manufacturing
launches.body:
Hi YC!

We’re [Noah](https://www.linkedin.com/in/noahvogel/) and [Colin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/colin-lavery-67b7512a3/), the founders of [Aerogen Systems](https://www.aerogensystems.com/). We’re building the next generation of clean infrastructure for chip manufacturing.

**TL;DR:** Aerogen Systems makes semiconductor tools clean themselves. Talos, our tool-integrated purification system, continuously destroys airborne contaminants around the wafer, creating 10–100x cleaner tool environments while reducing dependence on ultra-high-purity nitrogen. Over time, Talos becomes the foundation for the Cleanpipe, an ultra-clean interconnect network that lets wafers move between tools without depending on the surrounding cleanroom.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5yBzBCzwFV8>

# **The Problem**

**Chip features keep getting smaller, but cleanrooms do not scale with them.**

Semiconductor manufacturers spend billions building enormous cleanroom facilities, then spend even more trying to isolate their most advanced wafers from the environment they just built.

As features approach the atomic scale, trace airborne contaminants that were once tolerable can create defects, reduce yield, and disrupt some of the most sensitive manufacturing processes on Earth. Yet the industry's answer has largely been more of the same: cleaner facilities, more filtration, and more ultra-high-purity nitrogen flooding sensitive equipment.

**The proof is in the yield numbers.** 2026 reporting puts Intel’s 18A program between roughly 50% and 65% yield as it pushed the node toward high-volume production. With global semiconductor sales projected to reach **$1.5 trillion** in 2026, every percentage point matters. Improvements in yield and manufacturing efficiency can represent tens of billions of dollars in value.

# **The Solution**

At Aerogen Systems, we think the industry is approaching this problem backwards.

**The whole factory does not need to be a massive cleanroom.** Only the environment immediately surrounding the wafer does.

Talos is our proprietary, tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor manufacturing equipment and continuously recirculates and purifies the environment around the wafer. Instead of constantly replacing contaminated gas with more ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos destroys contaminants at the point of use, offering 10–100x cleaner tool environments while dramatically reducing dependence on purge gas and consumable filtration.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/a095a4e2-31a2-4307-b8f1-bca417cb27d7)

_1. Rendering of standalone Talos unit._

But Talos is only part of the vision.

With tool-integrated purification units as a foundation, we build **the Cleanpipe: ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure** that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Talos cleans the tools. The Cleanpipe connects tools to each other. Together, they delete the cleanroom and all the expenses that come with it.

# **What We’ve Built**

Talos has progressed through multiple generations of hardware development and is protected by patent-pending IP. We’ve validated the core purification architecture and are now working toward tool integrations, pilots, and commercial deployments with semiconductor manufacturers and equipment companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/a8596c2c-c29b-4271-8d92-85672dce0dc1)

_2. Test results showing Talos bringing industry-standard 6N purification levels down to 8N — a 100x improvement in cleanliness._

The next step is connecting these purified environments together through the Cleanpipe, creating an ultra-clean path around the wafer from tool to tool and ultimately removing the need to maintain the entire fab as one enormous cleanroom.

# **The Team**

Aerogen Systems started as a NASA-backed research group at the University of Michigan, where our team developed the underlying purification technology. 

We have spent the last several years designing, testing, patenting, and rebuilding this technology for extreme manufacturing environments.

* Noah, CEO, worked in manufacturing engineering at SpaceX, where he focused on production rate and yield improvement for the Starship program.


* Colin, CTO, previously built advanced particle detectors at H3D and led the team through the earliest design cycles of Talos.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/4db2a255-30a8-44ee-928b-b07425918094)

# **Our Ask**

We want to meet semiconductor fabs, equipment OEMs, and manufacturing teams interested in pilots, tool integrations, and commercial deployments. If this sounds like you, please reach out to [hi@aerogensystems.com](mailto:hi@aerogensystems.com)!

We are building toward a world where fabs no longer need billion-dollar cleanrooms to manufacture the world’s most advanced chips.

launches.title: TareBio: Vaccines for any cancer or infection in weeks
launches.tagline: We make personalized or population-level vaccines reverse-engineered from the immune system. We have already cured cancer in mice and are vaccinating our first patient within the year.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Our platform develops **personalized** or **population-level** vaccines for **_any_ disease** in weeks by **changing _only one input_**: the immune imprint. Instead of trying to predict which antigens might work, we read out immune cells already fighting the disease in the body and reverse-engineer antigens that activate them. We've already run our platform end-to-end and created a vaccine that cured cancer in mice. We will be vaccinating our first patient within the year.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108804&key=user_uploads/431020/46cdbd4d-72d9-4231-a781-01a886dd82a4)

View our launch video here: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ty7jA8ecY2o>

**The vaccine bottleneck**

For 200+ years, vaccines have been designed using the same workflow: study a pathogen or tumor, _predict_ which antigens might trigger protection, vaccinate, and hopefully generate a good immune response. This works for simpler infections. It has struggled for decades on complex diseases like HIV, TB, Hep C, and nearly _every cancer_. Currently, vaccine design is treated as a prediction problem.

**What we do differently**

Instead, we treat it as a readout problem. The **immune system has _already solved_** antigen selection in the body, it knows what it's responding to and the best immune cells for the job. So, we flip the whole process around:

1. Capture the immune cells already responding to a cancer or infection, the "**immune imprint**"
2. Use this imprint to directly identify, or “**reverse engineer**”, activating antigens
3. Build a **vaccine** from those antigens

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108804&key=user_uploads/431020/31744f0e-4a44-4aa9-aa2e-29d174a8d30a)

The same platform works for **_any_ disease** by changing one input: the immune imprint. Function over prediction, no constrained search space, and the output is a vaccine that can generate durable immunity in the body, not a transient antibody conjugate or cellular therapy.

**Proof**

We built the full platform in mice and ran it end-to-end: identified antigens from the immune imprint of the cancer, designed a vaccine from them, and **cured lymphoma in mice.** Nothing about the technology is specific to lymphoma, it generalizes to any cancer or infection. We are using our technology to create both personalized (n=1) and population-level vaccines.

**Why us**

I'm Eta Atolia, founder and CEO. I built this platform over the last 8 years as part of my MD-PhD at UCLA-Caltech with funding from The Gates Foundation. Before this, I did my undergrad at MIT with most of my time dedicated to cancer immunotherapy and infectious disease research at the Koch and HMS. Our scientific advisory board includes Darrell Irvine, PhD (Vice Chair of Immunology at Scripps, Former MIT Professor of 22 years, world-renowned vaccine engineer) and Manish Butte, MD, PhD (Chief of Immunology at UCLA and expert rare disease clinician).

**Our ask**

We are actively working with organizations and individuals to create both population-level vaccines and personalized treatments.

Helpful things as we build:

* If you have **patient tumor** **or** **blood samples**, please reach out.
* Intros to **biotech + pharma** and **vaccine teams** for partnerships.
* **Immunologists, oncologists, infectious disease specialists,** and **ML engineers** who want to build this with us.

If any of this resonates, reach out at [contact@tarebio.com](mailto:contact@tarebio.com).

launches.body:
There's a new kind of agent.

It exists on its own computer, connected to your tools, with a living brain of everything you and your company know.

Introducing Almanac, the agent with a company brain.

<https://youtu.be/UZVOJTQhW1I?is=Bb0d2--YkZYf7xdp>

Almanac works with its own browser and terminal, signed into the accounts you connect. Everything in your tools compiles into a wiki that it reads before every task. Your teammates' Almanacs share that wiki. You text it work. It texts you when it's done.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106258&key=user_uploads/2550783/615174e2-3d24-480d-a8f5-7c849c5a24b9)

**What we hand ours**

* Divit has it gather feedback from our customer Slack channels and file GitHub issues, with screenshots and reproduction steps.
* Kushagra connected his Chase account. It inspects recurring charges and cancels subscriptions he doesn't use.
* Before meetings, it sends us a brief built from our past emails and calendar. After, it drafts the follow-up. The draft is usually good enough to send.
* It watches our production environment. When something trivial breaks, it fixes it and raises a PR.
* It buys our dinner. At this point it suggests the order.

**It knows when to stop.** At a login, a payment, or a decision it shouldn't make alone, it pings you or hands you the live browser.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106258&key=user_uploads/2550783/9b85821d-c37b-4da7-87a9-6218d731ad53)

**Automations are just sentences.** "Whenever a customer reports a bug, check whether anyone else has reported it, reproduce it, and update the GitHub issue." Say it once. There's no workflow builder.

**The brain is shared.** Your teammates' Almanacs read and write the same wiki. So can your other agents: Claude Code and Codex can start caught up on your company. \
\
**Our bet.** We're Rohan, Kushagra, and Divit. We grew up together in India and met 11 years ago preparing for the JEE. Since then: machine-learning research and engineering across Vector Institute, CMU, MIT, Harvard, and Arcesium. From the start we've had one bet: AI will need a context layer, and it takes the shape of a wiki. For the last year and a half we've built agent wikis for Harvard, for NASA, and once, an attempt at the whole internet. We are, perhaps predictably, obsessed with wikis. Almanac is that bet, pointed at your company.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106258&key=user_uploads/2550783/7bab1366-3e4c-4140-829d-e1bc9666d9ab)

Text it your first task tonight. See what's done by morning.\
\
Try it out today: <https://usealmanac.com>

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We’re [Alex](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alexyctung/) and [Leon](https://www.linkedin.com/in/linghong-yao/) - cofounders of [Whitespace](https://whitespacehq.ai/).\
\
Whitespace is the AI operating system for wholesale distributors. It connects to their systems to build a living model of their business, then deploys self-improving AI agents to do work like inventory planning, customer service, and order processing.

**Problem**

Wholesale distribution is a $60 trillion global industry that touches one in every five dollars of global output. Yet it still runs largely manually. At a typical wholesale distributor, 30-50% of staff are dedicated to back-office tasks.

They spend their days on email, spreadsheets, and legacy systems, relying on tribal knowledge in their heads. Businesses cannot scale without hiring, and training a new hire takes >6 months.

A quote from one of our customers really brings this to life: “I have 6 reps typing 600 lines of orders from email into the ERP every day. Everyone is inside our ERP and spreadsheets, copying data from one place to another.”

**Solution**

Whitespace is the AI operating system for wholesale distributors. It connects to their systems to build a living model of their business, then deploys self-improving AI agents. 

We’re already working with wholesale distributors in sectors including industrial supplies and building materials to set up agents for processes like:

* **Inventory Planning.** Forecasts product demand, recommends reorder quantities against stock levels, and learns over time from actual demand.
* **Customer Service.** Monitors inboxes for support queries, digs through systems to find answers, and responds with human oversight.
* **Order Processing.** Monitors inboxes, enters orders into the ERP, flags exceptions to humans, and learns from their corrections.

<https://youtu.be/4UxlKKXrgfI?si=EwGhX1LCTGyauuw6>

**Team**

Both our families ran wholesale distribution businesses, so we grew up seeing the inefficiencies and the opportunities firsthand.

[Alex](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alexyctung/) advised F500 manufacturers and distributors on tech/AI at BCG, took a startup from launch to 7-figure ARR in a year as its first non-engineering hire, and graduated top of his college at Cambridge.

[Leon](https://www.linkedin.com/in/linghong-yao/) built AI products for F500 logistics distribution companies at InstaDeep, published first-author RL papers at tier-1 conferences, and previously founded an EdTech startup that served thousands of users worldwide.

We’ve been best friends for 12 years since high school. We’ve lived and worked together, and are now tackling a challenge close to our hearts.

Most often, I’m stepping outside to do external-facing tasks, like researching my leads on LinkedIn or comparing flight options. I want my agents to do these tasks as well.

Currently, those can’t be completed because their gateway to the world (in-built web search) has limited access. Often the agent also asks to use the browser with a logged-in session, which I’m uncomfortable with.

So, I built the connector layer that I wish existed.

**Solution:**

Click’s MCP is a single installation that provides your agent with an ever-growing bundle of the best data connectors. The current set of connectors enable new use cases inside the chat, like:

* Lead research & enrichment
* Researching ad campaigns from competitors
* Analyzing sentiment around a topic across social media
* Planning travel with live fares & availability

**Team:**

I’m Aditya, the founder of Click. Previously, I helped build Ethereum, with a vision to create a platform that enables new kinds of applications. 

Now, I’m focusing on the next application platform - the AI chat surface. Click builds useful services that meet users right inside the conversation. I’m building one trusted service at a time, and research is the first one.

launches.tagline: GitNexus gives coding agents a map of your codebase, so they stop burning tokens looking for it.
launches.body:
##### We're building the most token-efficient coding agent in the world. The reason it works is GitNexus, our open-source knowledge graph for your codebase.

<https://youtu.be/-ErU4cCRSlQ>

##### The problem

Coding agents don't understand your repo. They grep, they guess, they re-read the same files, and they stuff half your codebase into a context window hoping the answer is in there somewhere. You pay for every one of those tokens, and the agent still misses the cross-file relationship that mattered.

The bottleneck isn't the model. It's context.

##### What we built:

GitNexus indexes your repository into a knowledge graph (symbols, call paths, imports, ownership, history) and serves the agent exactly the context a task needs, instead of everything it might need.

It's one connected stack:

* The knowledge graph. Run npx gitnexus analyze and you have it
* A coding agent that runs on top of it
* Automated PR review grounded in the same graph

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110659&key=user_uploads/1607382/1d3e51af-d3b5-4ee6-b0c3-b80bc4337c3e)

##### The proof:

On the DeepSWE benchmark, we ran the same agent with our graph and without it:

* 37% to 68.4% pass rate. Nearly twice the bugs solved
* Half the cost per fix, with fewer tokens
* On the hardest tasks, the gap more than triples

Full methodology and results: <https://www.akonlabs.com/benchmarks>

##### Where we are:

* 45,000+ GitHub stars
* 65,000 weekly npm downloads
* 10+ enterprises onboarded

##### About the team:

Subham Kundu and Abhigyan Patwari have spent nearly half a decade working on knowledge graphs. Between them, they've been founding engineers, CTOs, and principal AI engineers, taking products from 0 to 100 at multiple startups. Subham is a seasoned engineer who has scaled products to millions of users, won multiple hackathons, and doing a PhD in reinforcement learning. Abhigyan is a seasoned technologist and serial open source contributor, with involvement across multiple open source projects.

##### Run it in your way:

Managed, or fully sovereign. Self-hosted, air-gapped, nothing leaves your network.

##### Looking to cut your coding agent bill?

If you want to lower your coding agent spend without giving up frontier performance, sign up at <https://www.akonlabs.com>. We'll get you set up on your own repo and show you the before-and-after on your actual token costs.

##### Our other asks

* Try the open-source version. Run npx gitnexus analyze. Takes a minute
* Intros. Engineering leaders where agent cost or code-context quality is a real line item, especially in regulated or air-gapped environments

launches.title: Vendo: Let Your Users Build Their Own Features on Top of Your Product

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Nour and Yousef, co-founders of Vendo.

**TL;DR:** Vendo is the customization layer that lets your users build their own features and micro-apps right inside your product, on your existing API and within your brand and guardrails.. Plug it into the agent you already have, or drop in a production-ready one, with a single command. It's open source.

**Try it now:** [vendo.run](http://vendo.run) \
**Star us on Github**: <https://github.com/runvendo/vendo>

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JjtDhA7DZw8>

## **The Problem**

Every product team is drowning in the same thing: a feature backlog that never ends. Different customers want different things, and you can't build a thousand versions of your product. So most requests sit in a board for months, and the customer who asked churns quietly because your product doesn't do the one thing they needed.

The AI wave made this worse, not better. Everyone knows their product should be agent-native, but building a real agent (one that can take actions, generate UI, remember context, and stay inside your security guardrails) takes serious engineering hours and ongoing maintenance. So most teams ship a chatbot bolted to the corner of the screen and call it AI. Users don't want another chatbot. They want your product to do the exact thing they need.

## **How Vendo Works**

Vendo installs into your product with one command. It reads your theme, your components, and your API surface. From then on, your users can describe what they want in plain English and Vendo builds it for them, live, inside your app:

* **Personalize the product** to exactly how each user works, in your own design system.
* **Build automations** that run on a schedule and take real actions in your product.
* **Pull in hundreds of external tools**, so the workflow doesn't stop at your app's edge.

Everything runs in secure sandboxes and inside your existing security guardrails. The agent only ever has the same access the user has, so it can't do anything they couldn't already do themselves, and your source code never gets touched.

You can plug Vendo into the agent you already have, or get a production-ready one out of the box with actions, UI generation, and a knowledge base included. It's completely open source, and it takes one command to install and push live to your users.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106667&key=user_uploads/2705364/5b5c05c6-3415-4d23-bf67-a779d56456c7)

## **Who We Are**

We're a Stanford and Berkeley team who’ve known each other since kindergarten and previously built in-store AI shopping assistants for retailers.

* **Nour (CEO)** studied Mechanical Engineering at Berkeley and interned as a mechanical design engineer. Before startups, he played professional academy soccer for the San Jose Earthquakes for 7 years.
* **Yousef (CTO)** graduated high school at 15 and completed a Bachelor’s in EECS from Berkeley and a Master’s from Stanford. He previously built FPGA infrastructure at Apple and worked on chip design at AMD.

### **Our Ask**

* **If you run a product team** and your backlog is full of "can it also do X" requests, we want to talk. We'll integrate Vendo for you.
* **If you're a developer** who wants the best open-source way to put a real agent into your product, come try it and tell us what breaks.
* **Intros welcome** to any company feeling the request pain who wants an agentic interface on top of their product.

Reach us at [vendo.run](http://vendo.run) or [nour@vendo.run](mailto:nour@vendo.run)

launches.body:
Hey YC! We're Alfredo and Ranad, the founders of Omanta.

**TL;DR: Omanta creates a personalized research lab around a single patient. We integrate a patient’s complete medical record, personal genomics, and use AI to take on the most complex cancer cases. Our researchers tackled GitLab co-founder Sid Sijbrandij’s case, helping bring him into complete remission.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkZaq_fENqI>

\
**Why this matters**\
If you're a cancer patient, you'd think the hardest cases have entire teams dedicated to solving them. The reality: most doctors have about 20 minutes per patient, while the science never stops moving. New discoveries emerge every day, yet reaching standard clinical care can take over a decade (\~17 years on average). Physicians make high-stakes decisions with limited time, and even the most difficult cases rarely have anyone whose full-time job is to interrogate every layer of that one patient's disease and push the newest science toward their treatment.

That's the gap we built Omanta to close.\
\
**What we do**\
We meet patients wherever they are in their journey. We integrate their complete medical record and personal genomics with AI and clinical evidence to understand the molecular drivers of their disease. Then we map every existing therapy against their biology, and if the right therapy doesn't exist, we build it, from cancer vaccines and immunotherapies to highly targeted radioligand therapies.\
\
We've worked on some of the most complex cancer cases in the world. Most notably, **Alfredo was the genomics lead for the personalized therapeutic campaign behind GitLab founder Sid Sijbrandij's complete remission**, partnering with leading institutions to pursue personalized mRNA/DNA vaccines, CAR-T programs, drug repurposing, expanded-access therapies, and continuous molecular monitoring. We've seen what becomes possible when the full force of modern science is organized around a single person, and Omanta brings that depth of investigation to every case.\
\
**Why us**\
We met eight years ago working on early CRISPR cancer research and have been building toward this ever since.

* **Alfredo Gonzalez, PhD (CEO)** — translational genomics. Led the year-long investigation of 25TB of sequencing and molecular data for Sid Sijbrandij, key missing information in existing genomic reports, and uncovered actionable findings that reshaped his therapeutic strategy, including personalized mRNA/DNA vaccines, CAR-T, expanded access, drug repurposing, and continuous monitoring. PhD at UCLA, where he built one of the world's largest centralized multi-omic datasets for rare tumors. Previously at the Broad Institute (Cancer Dependency Map, validating targets from large-scale CRISPR screens) and Harvard's Wagers Lab.
* **Ranad Humeidi, PhD (CSO)** — chemical biologist. Earned her PhD in Chemical Biology from Harvard in three years, where she identified a druggable mechanism in ulcerative colitis that became the basis of a multimillion-dollar GSK collaboration. Built and directed a multimillion-dollar scientific program centered on a single rare-cancer patient, then went on to direct scientific strategy for 12+ medically complex patients after standard options were exhausted. At the Broad, she co-created and co-led a fellowship turning scientific discoveries into companies.

\

* Intros. If you or someone you love is facing a difficult cancer diagnosis, we want to hear from you.

* Reach us here on Bookface or at [alfredo@omanta.com](mailto:alfredo@omanta.com) & [ranad@omanta.com](mailto:ranad@omanta.com).

name: Fabraix
long_description:
Fabraix builds state-of-the-art AI red-teaming agents that continuously detect security vulnerabilities in customer-facing AI. Our product, Nyx, has already found vulnerabilities in agents at dozens of Fortune 500 companies. On AgentHarm, the leading benchmark for offensive AI security, Nyx achieved a 78% attack success rate, compared with 67% for GPT-5.6 Sol.

AI agents can change more often than teams can test them. A new model, prompt, tool, permission, or data source can change what an agent does, even when the application code stays the same. And AI is also increasing how much software companies produce and how often it changes. We built Nyx to automate the work required to red-team AI agents. It is multi modal by design and interacts with the target indirectly through controlled replicas of SaaS products and websites that we maintain, placing malicious payloads in webpages, documents, files, messages, and tool outputs to test how an agent behaves under different conditions.

Nyx often finds its first vulnerability within minutes or hours rather than days or weeks. Because the work is fully automated, companies can repeat the test with every change and at a much lower cost than what a 7-figure red-teaming (and point-in-time) engagement would require.

We're also the team behind ACE (Adversarial Cost to Exploit), a benchmark that measures AI security in terms of how much it costs attackers to break an AI system; providing a game-theoretic framework to understand how motivated a rational attacker would be in exploiting the system.
