launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋 - we're Aman and Sarthak, founders of Decawork.\
\
**TL;DR:** AI agents shouldn’t have permanent access to company systems. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into fixed rules or manually approve every step. Decawork trains small, company-specific AI models that approve every agent action in real time, based on company policies and interests, the agent’s task, and its past actions. Access is granted for the task at hand and revoked when it’s done.\
\
Launch video: [Watch it here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SanpHIyFcV4)\
\
🚧 **The Problem & Why now?**\
Companies are putting long-running, more autonomous agents to work on broader tasks and goals. These agents need access to critical company systems, but their actions can be unpredictable and may not serve the company’s interests.

OpenAI’s agents have already hacked Hugging Face during testing with reduced safeguards. Replit’s agent deleted data from a live application’s database.

An agent’s access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Permanent access lets an agent keep using permissions even when they are no longer appropriate for its task.

As agents take on more work independently, access decisions need to happen in real time. But companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rule or have people manually approve every step.\
\
✅ **How we solve this?**\
Decawork gives AI agents access for the task at hand and revokes it when the task is done.

* Connect your agents. Route API requests and MCP tool calls through Decawork to see activity and manage access in one place.
* Set company policies. Write policies in plain English, specify when human approval is required, and connect your existing identity and IT service management systems.
* Deploy a company-specific policy model. We deploy small models that approve actions in real time using your company’s policies and priorities, task context, and past actions. Your agents do the work. Decawork evaluates each proposed action and enforces the access decision before it runs.

🚀 **Team**\
Sarthak built AI systems at NVIDIA that were deployed at OpenAI and Meta, and worked on enterprise AI agents at Ema.

Aman built the AI compliance platform at Barclays used by internal teams globally, then led product at a consumer AI startup serving 100K+ monthly users, hand-wiring credentials for the agents he shipped.

Every one of those deployments came down to the same questions: what can it access, who approved it, and what did it do? We kept solving agent access by hand - so we quit to build the system we wished we’d had.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109883&key=user_uploads/1632535/0ef2784e-ab45-422f-91b9-960473f11dd5)

🙏 **Our Ask**

* If you’re on an IT team or know someone who’s worried about AI agents accessing or misusing company systems, talk to us: <https://decawork.ai/cal> or [founders@decawork.ai](mailto:founders@decawork.ai)

**TL;DR:** Pennant is building AI-native proxy voting solutions for institutional investors, public companies, and their advisors. We’re live with paying enterprise customers, including one of the largest US public pension plans, a Top AmLaw 100 firm, and leading governance advisors. Before Pennant, our team built trillion-dollar tech at BlackRock, cast proxy votes at State Street, and advised Fortune 100 boards at PJT.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_WDs1VB213EcPS5caE5XK7L6UkZLz07l](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_WDs1VB213EcPS5caE5XK7L6UkZLz07l/preview)

**The problem:** Proxy voting at publicly traded companies drives trillions in market value every year. Shareholder votes decide $100B mergers, trillion-dollar pay packages, and the boardroom battles that define companies.

Yet the work is brutally manual: reviewing thousands of pages of SEC filings, research, and engagement notes that live in a patchwork of PDFs, spreadsheets, and post-it notes. And for professional advice, the market has relied on two firms, ISS and Glass Lewis, for 40+ years, a duopoly that controls 97% of the market.

**Why Now:** Technological change and market sentiment are ripping this market wide open.

CEOs have been sounding the proxy-advisor alarm for years:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/45604eff-9d48-4271-90ed-b3bf6000b461)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/a5232d8f-91b7-44bd-8116-f0d251b764d0)

And now big investors and the White House are taking action.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/12da7f65-6e5c-4e57-b2d5-76c18fac1fcf)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/00e9661e-2b7e-414d-8c2c-f4d4f47b8b55)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110156&key=user_uploads/3388610/47c99681-6ca9-484b-ab33-102a4021cd92)

JPMorgan is even building its own solution. But 99% of the investors, companies, and advisors we talk to don't want to own this themselves, or don't have the resources to. That's where Pennant comes in, and it's why we're winning business out of the gate.\
\
**Why Pennant is better:** Pennant isn't a better proxy advisor. We're building something bigger: the AI-native operating system for corporate governance, built by former proxy voters and technologists, a team that cast these votes and shipped the software at institutional scale.

Pennant gives institutional investors, and the advisors and companies they engage with, voting and governance intelligence to act on their own principles at scale. Legacy tools follow rigid rules; Pennant reasons through each ballot item, inbound email, and engagement question the way your team would, handling the clear calls and flagging the nuanced ones, keeping people in the driver's seat.

As one of our customers put it last week, “\[incumbent xyz\] can handle our routine stuff for another year, but we’re thrilled to use Pennant for the custom heavy-lifting that we’ve been wanting to do for a long time, and use you for everything from there.”

Pennant also serves the other side of the vote: public companies, law firms, and bankers who need to read their shareholder base and predict risk before the annual meeting. Same data, bigger market. The market at the intersection of investing and corporate governance is estimated at well over $200 billion, and it remains largely unserved by today's tools.

**Traction:** Pennant is live with paying enterprise customers, including one of the largest US public pension plans, a Top AmLaw 100 firm, and leading governance advisors. We're partnered with a top global asset manager as a design partner and are actively engaged with S&P 500 companies. Before YC S26, Pennant was selected for Palantir's Startup Fellowship (Cohort 002).

**Why us:** We've known each other for 15 years, since our undergrad days at Cornell, and started our careers on the same analyst desk at BlackRock building tech products for these exact customers. We have a rare pairing: direct industry experience as the customer, plus the engineering chops to ship fast and earn trust.

After BlackRock, Ryan (CEO) was the customer for 6+ years, voting proxies at 3,000+ company meetings and advising Fortune 100 companies on how to win critical votes at PJT Partners. He used Glass Lewis and ISS every day.

Tommy (CTO) took the technical path, shipping products at BlackRock before earning his Harvard MBA and founding Mindware, where he built workflow-ready infrastructure for AI agents. He was building agentic AI before "agents" were hot, and Pennant is where his engineering background meets Ryan's proxy-voting expertise.

**Our ask:** If you own or touch proxy voting as an investor, advisor, or public company, we want to talk: <https://calendly.com/ryan-getpennant/30min>

Learn more at [getpennant.ai](http://getpennant.ai)

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We’re building Touchy 🙌, a voice and image-first AI assistant for the iPhone that personalizes itself to you. You can activate Touchy from your lock screen to instantly get things done across your apps or get answers about the world around you. Touchy is free to try, get it here: <https://apps.apple.com/us/app/touchy-ai-at-your-fingertips/id6798889392>

<https://youtube.com/shorts/IJNucvAZ_-k>

## **The Problem**

You probably know the feeling:

You ask the assistant on your phone, across the room, to send a colleague a message.

It cheerfully replies that it found 10 search results for “text Bob on Slack”.

So you trudge to your phone, find the app, open the DM, and begrudgingly type out your message instead.

We wanted a better personal assistant, one that had the intelligence and integrations we’ve come to expect from our AI agents, with the convenience of one that was native to your devices. We also believe that for AI to truly be personal, it needs to be deeply integrated into your life and the world around you. Right now, AI systems are constrained largely to using digital tools, yet the physical world is rich with audio and visual information that your phone is capable of receiving.

## What We Built

So we built Touchy. One button press and you're instantly talking to an assistant that can see what you see, remember what you've said, and take action across all the tools you use. 

What sets Touchy apart:

* **Reimagined UX.** Touchy is a fast, fully iOS-native app with a unique interface that is delightful to use and brings it closer to the world around you.
* **Sees and hears the world around you**. Speak to Touchy and it can speak back. Easily snap a photo with the app’s camera to give Touchy access to what you’re seeing.
* **Gets things done across your apps**. Touchy comes with built-in integrations with 1,000+ popular apps, as well as iOS-native capabilities such as you contacts and location.
* **Make it yours over time**. You chat with Touchy in a single, continuous conversation. It automatically collects memories and preferences, and tailors itself to be more useful to you as you use it.

It's built to give you your attention back. Ask it something, let it act, and get back to your day — no app fighting for your attention.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111407&key=user_uploads/3697324/23ce7916-fce5-44c4-9ebf-f04049fee639)

## The team

We’re Rohit, Andrew, and Kev. Before this, Rohit was doing a PhD on AI alignment at Google DeepMind Princeton and graduated #1 in Berkeley EECS. Andrew built educational software that scaled to half a million students worldwide. Kev was a startup founding engineer, developing data and GPU infrastructure that power many of the leading AI neolabs today. 

We met during undergrad at UC Berkeley, and we’re coming back together to research, productionize, and scale the future of personal technology.

## Our ask

If you have an iPhone, download Touchy and try it out: <https://apps.apple.com/us/app/touchy-ai-at-your-fingertips/id6798889392>

We would love to learn what people find themselves using Touchy for, and what they wish they could use it for. You can also report bugs by shaking your phone or just telling Touchy. You can also reach us at [founders@touchyapp.com](mailto:founders@touchyapp.com)

launches.title: Lamb Labs: Custom Chips for AI Inference
launches.tagline: Co-designed models and silicon: we hardcode the model architecture into chips targeting 20,000+ tokens per second and 63x higher intelligence per watt.
launches.body:
**Hi Everyone!** 

**We’re Niki and Thomas - cofounders of Lamb Labs.**  

**TL;DR: We build custom AI inference chips that run inference at 20,000+ tok/s and 63x higher intelligence per watt than a traditional GPU. Fully local and private by construction, no subscriptions, no API costs.** 

**Our mission: the world’s fastest LLM at the lowest power.** 

<https://youtu.be/MhhY1Dy9ltE?feature=shared>

**Our hot take: AI models are finally getting good enough to hardcode them directly into silicon.** Once you stop treating the chip as a general-purpose GPU and burn a specific model into hardware, inference gets radically faster and cheaper per watt. Most of the industry is still building flexible, general chips. We think that flexibility is exactly what's wasting your energy. So we’re on a mission to reduce the energy footprint of AI. 

**The Problem**

AI is taking power on two fronts: concentrating control of data and intelligence, and consuming ever more electricity to grow. That future scares us, so we're building against it.

Here's the technical root of the waste: **GPUs burn most of their energy during inference moving data, not computing.** LLM/VLM inference is memory-bound, fetching a weight from memory costs \~100–1000x the energy of the arithmetic you do with it. So you underutilize the GPU you paid for: some GPUs only hit 20–40% compute utilization during LLM inference while the rest idles waiting on memory.

Cloud hosting adds its own tax: expensive per-token bills, latency you can't control, network dependencies, and your data leaving your control.

**Our Solution**

We build the model and the chip together. 

The Hardware Layer

* **Custom architecture, RL-tuned.** We built an RL environment that co-designs the chip architecture for a given model, optimizing directly for speed and energy per token.
* **Aggressive quantization.** Removes complex math, which shrinks the size and cost of the chip.
* **Weights on-chip.** The model weights live where the compute is overcoming the memory-bandwidth bottleneck

 

Because everything is hardcoded, it's fully local and secure by construction. No connectivity dependency, nothing leaves the device.

The Software Layer 

Designing the chip led us to solving a fundamental flaw in LLMs so we are now open-sourcing a new model next week, converted from another open source model, to run 2x faster on any hardware. Come back next week for part 2 of our launch to find out more….

**Our Ask**

If you answer "yes" to any of these, we'd love your help:

* **Are you paying for inference in watts, not just dollars?** Neocloud or private DC operators who are power- or hardware-cost-bound rather than demand-bound, talk to us.
* **Do you need inference where the cloud isn't an option?** Private AI deployments, regulated, air-gapped, sovereign, or bandwidth-starved deployments.
* **Do you want to deploy the fastest AI models in your stack?** High frequency trading, agentic workflows 
* **Are you stuck on a thermal or battery budget?** Robotics, wearables, consumer AI hardware where a Jetson-class part is over-provisioned and runs too hot.
* **Can you introduce us to anyone above?** Warm intros are the single most useful thing.

Contact us at [contact@lamb-labs.com](mailto:contact@lamb-labs.com)

launches.title: Palisade - AI that detects and fixes OS vulnerabilities across every endpoint in minutes
launches.tagline: AI that finds and fixes OS-level vulnerabilities across device fleets
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** For companies running large fleets of OS-level endpoints (running GPU clusters, having a network of cloud devices, or deploying on-device), Palisade detects and fixes operating-system vulnerabilities (privilege escalation, remote code execution, memory corruption) that are extremely hard to detect and mitigate without applying AI to kernel-level data (syscalls, eBPF traces, process/memory events, network packets). A fix that used to take weeks to roll out, Palisade now applies in minutes across every endpoint.

Hey YC! I'm Prince, an ML researcher and engineer who dropped out from Caltech at 18 to build Palisade.

**What’s the problem:** Modern attacks increasingly target the operating system, but most security products only observe the network, cloud, or application layers. That leaves OS vulnerabilities among the hardest problems to detect and the slowest to remediate across a fleet.

**Why I’m building this:** Since I was 16, I have done plenty of professional red-team and blue-team security work. One pattern kept showing up: OS-level vulnerabilities were consistently the hardest to handle. Detection required low-level visibility, and even after identifying a vulnerability, rolling out a mitigation across hundreds or thousands of machines often took weeks. My background in both machine learning and operating systems convinced me this didn't have to be a manual process, so I built Palisade to automatically detect and remediate these vulnerabilities at the kernel level across an entire fleet.

**What Palisade does:** Palisade watches your systems at the kernel level—syscalls, eBPF traces, process and memory events, and network packets—and uses AI to find OS vulnerabilities other tools miss, then implement the fix automatically across every endpoint.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106995&key=user_uploads/2688178/fa8c6d6a-b058-4f44-87d0-5511d038718b)

_The Palisade control plane, live against a real kernel (LSM-BPF). The live feed at the bottom: every row is a real syscall decision._

The vulnerabilities it catches are the ones you can't see from the app or network layer alone:

* Privilege escalation
* Remote code execution
* Memory corruption

Most are caught before an exploit ever happens, and the fix is applied immediately, fleet-wide. The same patch that used to take weeks now lands in minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106995&key=user_uploads/2688178/2f4e756d-1348-44a2-bdce-bb3491925da5)

_The host audit: real findings ranked by severity. The bottom one is the cloud-metadata exposure: the same path behind the Capital One breach. One click on **Apply fix** and it's installed as a kernel rule._

Palisade can already detect and fix real problems:

* CVE-2024-1086: use-after-free in the Linux kernel's netfilter (nf_tables); local privilege escalation to root
* CVE-2025-6019: libblockdev/udisks privilege escalation to full root
* CVE-2025-32463: sudo --chroot local privilege escalation to root

**Who it's for:** Companies running a lot of OS-level endpoints, where a single kernel vulnerability multiplies across the whole fleet. Whether it’s network servers or GPUs, we have you covered.

<https://youtu.be/CTVhq7jfTPY>

**Our asks:**

* Intros: if you run a large fleet of OS-level endpoints, or know a security/infra lead who does, I'd love an intro.
* See the demo and tell me if you’d use it. Brutal feedback welcome.

— [prince@palisade-ai.com](mailto:prince@palisade-ai.com), <https://calendly.com/prince-palisade-ai/30min>, DMs welcome

launches.tagline: Your user verifies their identity once, and we return their medical records through one API.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Hubble gives your product a patient's medical records through a single API. Your user verifies their identity once, and we assemble their records from across the providers they've seen and return them for your AI agent to use. Where APIs are not sufficient, we keep going with AI (browser and voice agents). Every request runs on the patient's individual right of access.

**The problem**\
If you're building something that needs a patient's records, there's no clean way to get them. A patient's history is scattered across every provider they've ever seen, and each system is its own island. Most APIs returns the patient-portal subset rather than the full record, and coverage is inconsistent because every health system sets up its integration differently. So most teams either build per-provider integrations for months, fall back to faxes and manual portal logins, or push the problem back onto the patient by asking them to track down their own records or remember a login they set up years ago and have long since lost.

**What Hubble does**\
Your user verifies their identity once, and we go get their records so you don't have to.

* **One verification, no work on your end.** The patient verifies their identity in a couple clicks. After that, assembling the records is our job, not yours and not theirs.
* **We don't stop at the portal subset.** We connect into EHRs and HIEs where they work, and when an API comes back empty we keep going.
* **Browser and voice agents for everything else.** Agents submit the patient's request through provider portals and call records departments on the patient's behalf, working the phone trees so nobody on your team has to.
* **Built on the patient's right of access.** Every request runs on the patient's individual right of access. They review every source we request from and can revoke at any time. Every retrieval is logged.

**About the team**\
We're the team behind the AI agents at Grow Therapy and Amazon's One Medical, used by millions of patients. Prabha was Grow's first PM building and scaling their AI agents. Aaron built the AI infrastructure at One Medical serving 1M+ clients. (Fun fact: we've known each other for over a decade.)

launches.title: Skymerse: Autopilot for Flight Operations
launches.tagline: From planning and monitoring in the operations center to real-time support in the cockpit.
launches.body:
I’m Damian, founder of Skymerse (S26). I’m a licensed flight dispatcher and have spent 10 years working across flight operations, aviation data, and software.

We’re building one AI system to automate flight operations - from planning and monitoring in the operations center to real-time support in the cockpit.

Our goal is full automation of the work behind every flight.

<https://youtu.be/czP5N1FJ1ds>

## The problem

Airlines have spent decades digitizing flight operations. The information moved from paper to screens. The work of understanding it did not. A flight exists across many systems. Each system may be good at its own job, but the complete operational picture exists between them.

Pilots and operations teams still have to build that picture themselves. They search, compare, and interpret information to plan, monitor, and adapt every flight from schedule to landing.

When something changes, they do it again. When responsibility moves from the operations center to the crew, much of the context has to be passed on or rebuilt.

Today, people are the integration layer.

## What Skymerse does

Skymerse builds a live operational model of every flight. When an airline’s schedule flows in, it assembles the operational context for each flight and keeps it current as conditions change.

That model is the foundation for automation. Skymerse does not stop at displaying information or sending an alert. It understands what a change means for the flight, updates the operation, and carries the required work forward automatically.

Skymerse plans, monitors, and adapts flights from the operations center to the cockpit. Instead of rebuilding context across tools and handoffs, Skymerse manages each flight as one continuous process, from schedule to landing.

## Why I started Skymerse

Skymerse started with [Notamify.com](http://Notamify.com). I built Notamify because I was amazed by how much information pilots and ops teams have to process before every flight - and how much of that work was still done by hand.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111421&key=user_uploads/1472269/7e9fe835-e22f-4cb1-92dc-ac0f99a0cce2)

Notamify interprets every single NOTAM into operational impact. It reduces the briefing time from 2 hours to 2 minutes per flight. It now serves airline customers and thousands of pilots and aviation professionals.

As we built it, the larger problem became clear. Making one source easier interpreted is valuable, but people still have to connect it with the rest of the operation. They still have to work out what it means for their flight and what to do next.

Skymerse is that next step: from helping people understand one part of a flight to automating flight operations e2e.

## Automate your flight operations

We are onboarding airlines that want to automate their flight operations. If you lead flight operations, dispatch, or an OCC, we want to show you Skymerse on your flights.

[Book a demo](http://skymerse.com/demo) or email [hello@skymerse.com](mailto:hello@skymerse.com).

Hi everyone - Stan and Jonas here, founders of **Grip**. We build intelligent robots that sort _any_ waste, not just the clean, predictable objects existing systems are limited to. We're starting with plastic contamination in organic waste.\
\
<https://youtu.be/qIJ4a49WxpI>

**The problem**

We didn't start with a thesis, we found it on sorting lines, after visiting waste facilities across several countries:

* **Contamination is existential.** Plastic that organic-waste facilities can't remove gets shredded, processed, and spread onto agricultural soil. Operators spend up to 30% of operating costs fighting it and still fall short. Even Germany's 0.1% limit for plastic in finished compost is a tacit admission that full removal isn't possible with today's tools.
* **The labor force is aging and shrinking.** The picking work is unpleasant and turnover is brutal. Operators increasingly aren't choosing between people and robots. They're choosing between robots and nobody.
* **Dangerous items cause fires.** Batteries, propane tanks, and vapes slip through and ignite during handling and shredding: 448 reported fires at US and Canadian waste facilities in 2025, \~$2.5B in damage, and insurers are walking away. At the same time trash sorting is sitting in the top 5 of US deadliest occupations.

**What we built**

The hard part isn't the gripper. It's that waste never looks the way you planned. Objects arrive crushed, folded, tangled, half-buried, and moving. Put today's sorting robots in front of this and they break.

We're building one manipulation system that picks whatever shows up, at the front of the line where the material is most chaotic and existing automation stops. That means chaotic scene understanding, robust grasp planning, and hardware built for real waste streams: our custom three-way gripper is designed to maximize throughput, taking out as much contamination per cycle as possible.

Our rugged hardware matters, but intelligence is the product. Every pick generates data no other system ever encounters: what the robot saw, what it tried, how the material responded, whether it worked.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111317&key=user_uploads/3678142/bc867fdc-9225-4b85-83f9-f83433465d5b)

**Why now**

Waste policy has moved from vague ambition to enforceable deadlines:

* Separate bio-waste collection is now mandatory across the EU. More material, and more contamination, every year.
* New EU fertiliser rules just cut permitted impurities in compost and digestate, with national limits like Germany's stricter still.
* The US is real: California mandated a 75% cut in landfilled organics, missed it, and enforcement is ramping. At the same time, landfills near major cities are filling up, and that pressure is pushing more and more US municipalities to collect organic waste separately. More material, more contamination, more facilities that need to sort it.

More than 6,500 biowaste plants and thousands of recycling facilities across Europe and North America face this with no robot that can touch it. That's Grip.

**Why us**

We've built autonomous race cars, quadrupeds, drones, and excavators, robots that operate in dirt, weather, and chaos rather than controlled labs. Grip is that experience applied to an industry where physical intelligence removes a real bottleneck.

**Our ask**

We'd love intros to:

* Owners and operators of composting, anaerobic-digestion, and organic-waste facilities
* Owners and operators of MRFs and recycling facilities
* Regulators and experts shaping contamination limits and recycling standards

If someone runs a facility and will show us their hardest sorting problem, we'll get on a plane.

launches.title: Hyperprobe: On-call Agent for engineering teams
launches.tagline: The fastest way for coding agents to debug incidents live in production.
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR:** AI writes most of our code now. Debugging it when it breaks in production is still slow, because the value that explains the failure was never logged. HyperProbe is an on-call agent for engineering teams. It takes an open incident to a confirmed root cause by dropping read-only probes into your running service and capturing the exact variable state logs don't have. No redeploys, no restarting the app. \
\
📹 **Launch Video: [https://youtu.be/QtaZrQ8_Uk8](https://youtu.be/QtaZrQ8_Uk8)**

**🚧 The Problem**

Team ships faster than ever with agents that write most of our code. This is already shrinking the useful context engineers need to debug AI written code. Not helped by the limited telemetry added in the same code by AI. So when something breaks in prod, the first instinct for engineers is to open logs or throw them to agents. But if the line you are looking for is not there, agents will start guessing the root cause on limited data, forcing engineers to collect more logs by redeploys.

The result: our best engineers become our on-call team, incidents stay open longer, and patches come from data that never capture production context, so issues recur.

You can see where that leads. In September last year, a public fintech in India paid out $5 million after failed transactions were incorrectly marked successful. NYSE the same year miscalculated price bands for 40 symbols, printing trades so wrong they had to be reversed. Same pattern: the code ran clean, wrote the wrong state, and neither logs nor traces could show it.

 ✅ **What Hyperprobe does**

HyperProbe gives engineering teams an on-call agent that works the incident and takes it to a confirmed root cause, live in production.

* **Plan:** the agent picks up the alert from PagerDuty, Datadog, or Slack, then reads your logs and traces to locate the file and line. The easy incidents resolve right here.
* **Probe:** logs not enough? places read-only virtual breakpoints on the suspect lines and captures the exact variable state live, across services. No redeploys, no restarts. 
* **Confirm:** the diagnosis is verified against real captured evidence, not a guess. Your engineer gets a confirmed RCA and commits the fix.

There are two pieces. An SDK that runs inside your service, and an MCP server your coding agent talks to. The SDK is what makes setting probes (virtual breakpoints, log or metric) possible without a redeploy. 

### **🔍 A few examples**

* **An intermittent 500 that won't reproduce locally:** catch it live with full variable state 
* **A third-party API misbehaving:** see the exact payload and response
* **A function returns a wrong value with no error:** see what it computed and why
* **Anything that only happens in prod:** stop redeploying with console.logs

🚀 **The team**

We've both lived this problem. Shailendra ran production at scale. Karan was a senior architect at a SaaS company. Before this, both spent three years building production SDKs for a testing product, learning the hard parts of pulling real runtime state out of a running service without breaking it.

Every incident we watched came down to the same question: what was the actual value at the moment it broke. Nobody built it for the way engineers debug with coding agents now. So we did.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110401&key=user_uploads/3173209/ddf3d8d0-2bd4-4a8c-9547-fa5ea2496469)

### **🎁 Why now**

For thirty years the expensive part of software was writing it, and every tool got built for that. Generation is now nearly free, but the cost didn't disappear. It moved downstream, to figuring out why the generated code broke in production.

And that system is now mostly code no human wrote or holds in their head. When it breaks, the engineer has less context than ever, and their first move is already to hand it to the coding agent. That agent only has your logs and traces, so it guesses. We give it the evidence instead, captured live from the running code at the point of failure.

### **🙏 Our ask**

* If you're an engineer tired of the redeploy loop, debugging code you didn't write at 2 AM, try it on your own service.**,** first investigation in 10 min:[ https://docs.hyperprobe.co/quickstart](https://docs.hyperprobe.co/quickstart)
* If your best engineers have become your on-call team and you want that fixed, let us work one real incident from your stack, free: <https://calendly.com/shailendra-hyperprobe/30min>

TovenAI’s agents analyze activity across existing communications and trading systems using each firm’s policies, procedures, and applicable regulations as context, assembling the relevant evidence for compliance teams.

Our trade-reconstruction agent rebuilds the full sequence of a trade, links every event to its source evidence, and reduces the process from around four hours to minutes. Our electronic-communications surveillance agent reduces the false-positive burden by 3× and, in a head-to-head evaluation, delivered roughly 7× more value per alert reviewed than the market-leading incumbent.

Our platform supports several other compliance workflows, giving teams broader coverage with less manual work.

With prebuilt integrations to more than 30 systems – including Bloomberg, Cloud9, CME and NICE Actimize – firms can evaluate TovenAI on their own data in under a week without replacing their existing stack.

## **Why us**

We met eight years ago at Stanford. Batu later worked as a quantitative research engineer at Citadel Global Quantitative Strategies, building AI systems for quantitative research. Sam was a machine learning engineer at Meta, working on its ads recommendation systems.

We work closely with our customers and sit besides compliance officers every day. This gives us a rapid feedback loop, lets us see their workflows firsthand, and allows us to redesign compliance operations with AI at their core.

Sam’s mother spent her 15-year career in risk and compliance and was our first sounding board as we began exploring the space.

launches.title: Verdict Machine: AI cybersecurity for financial institutions’ digital assets
launches.tagline: AI that understands each institution's complete on-chain environment, assesses its cyber risk, and generates tailored controls to prevent hacks
launches.body:
Hey all! We are Dan, Liran, and Isaac. Before Verdict Machine, we launched blockchain security at Check Point (NASDAQ: CHKP).

**TL;DR:** Blockchain is becoming critical infra for all finance. More than $3.4B in digital assets was stolen in 2025. Verdict Machine is AI cybersecurity for financial institutions' digital assets. We use AI to understand each institution's environment, assess cyber risk and generate tailored controls that prevent hacks.

**Building for:** banks, asset managers, DeFi protocols and infra, companies that use stablecoins or RWAs. If that’s you, email us at [founders@verdictmachine.com](mailto:founders@verdictmachine.com).

<https://youtu.be/dYmEjST7Nc8>

### Signed is not safe

Sophisticated hackers don’t need to compromise a wallet to steal funds. They only need to trick an authorized operator into approving one malicious transaction.

On-chain, settlement is final. There is no chargeback and no reversal. The security decision has to happen before the transaction executes.

Attackers are sophisticated and see the entire institution, while existing security tools see fragments:

* Hidden dependencies. Vendors, protocols, bridges and infrastructure are assessed separately or not at all.
* Limited context. Controls check a transaction, not the institution behind it.
* Stale controls. Rules are written once and reviews run once, while the institution and its risk keep changing.

 

### How Verdict Machine works

Verdict Machine uses AI to secure each client end to end.

**Inventory.** It builds the complete inventory of a client’s on-chain environment: assets, wallets, smart contracts, users, vendors, counterparties, and transaction patterns.

**Posture.** It quantifies cyber risk and recommends tailored controls to minimize exposure.

**Enforce controls.** Before execution, it evaluates each proposed transaction to prevent attacks in real time.

The same live model powers every workflow:

**Real time prevention.** Security and compliance teams secure their most critical transactions.

**Continuous cyber diligence.** Asset managers and risk teams underwrite the cyber risk of protocols, vendors, and counterparties before and after capital is deployed.

**Wallet screening.** Payments and stablecoin teams screen for fraud, unauthorized transactions, and risky wallets.

### Why now

Institutions are racing to launch stablecoin and tokenized-asset products. MiCA and DORA are in force, so the people who own this risk now have to show their work. Attackers punish under-protected organizations.

Fireblocks and Chainalysis reached $8B valuations for digital asset custody and compliance. Cybersecurity for on-chain finance is a bigger opportunity. Every financial institution is going to use digital assets and therefore will require digital-asset cybersecurity.

### Traction

We left Check Point the day before Y Combinator started. We already have POCs with asset managers and digital-asset infrastructure providers moving billions of dollars weekly for financial institutions, and we are in active evaluations with a digital-asset team at one of the world's largest banks.

### Why us

We previously launched and led blockchain security at Check Point (NASDAQ: CHKP). Our CTO Isaac is a cyber veteran from Matzov, Israel’s cryptography unit. We are crypto natives with many years building infra for crypto and fintech. We built Verdict Machine to bring AI-native, institution-specific security to on-chain finance.

Managing or deploying crypto, stablecoins, or tokenized assets? Talk to us.

[verdictmachine.com](http://verdictmachine.com) · [founders@verdictmachine.com](mailto:founders@verdictmachine.com)

launches.tagline: Get 3x more done in a fraction of the time with a team of Dock agents.
launches.body:
After a decade building and scaling companies — including Branch, which[ Govind](https://www.linkedin.com/in/govindkavaturi/) and I grew from zero to $100M+ ARR — we kept hitting the same wall: doing more always meant hiring more. Now, for the first time, it doesn't have to. That's why we built[ **Dock**](https://trydock.ai/).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JO0dwm_NU_s>

AI agents have changed what's possible, which is why we're building again. Dock gives you a team of proactive AI agents  that work alongside you — they talk to each other, hand off work, and take initiative instead of waiting to be prompted. So you steer instead of babysitting a dozen chat windows.

## **The Problem**

AI agents can finally do real work. But today they work alone — isolated chats that sit there waiting for you to prompt them. The moment you run more than one, _you_ become the middleman: copy-pasting context between a dozen windows and unblocking every agent by hand. The more agents you add, the more work you create for yourself. It doesn't scale.

## **The Solution**

Dock turns those isolated agents into a real team. Here's how it works:

### **1. Spin up a team of specialized AI agents in minutes.**

Each agent has a real role, its own objectives, and persistent memory — so it gets better at its job over time instead of resetting every session.

### **2. They work together, proactively.**

Your agents  pursue goals on their own, message each other, and hand off work when one needs something from another — no copy-pasting, no you relaying context. They only come back to you when there's a real decision to make.

### **3. You and your team work right alongside them.**

Everyone — humans and AI agents  — works in the same shared workspace, toward the same goals. The earlier you plug Dock in, the more your agents  learn about how your company actually works.

## **Why this works**

Multi-agent coordination is an infrastructure problem, and we built that infrastructure. Dock runs its own agent harness and runtime, executes in the cloud or on your machine, and gives every agent memory, schedules, and a shared workspace as primitives. Agents working as a team is not a feature we added. It’s what the system is.

## **Why we're building this**

We've spent our careers inside growing companies — hiring, scaling, managing — and felt the coordination drag of every new person you add. When AI made it possible to grow output without growing the team, this problem was already ours. In a real way, Dock found us more than we found it. Today we run our entire company on Dock, and we think soon every company will run on humans and AI agents  working together.

Get early access:[ **trydock.ai**](http://trydock.ai)

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** OpenRelay is building an Inference Delivery Network (IDN) on top of its CDN for GPUs. We provide one entrypoint for inference across every chip. 

Send us a workload and we’ll cut your costs up to 20% by running it through our network, balancing the best available accelerator (NVIDIA, TPU, Trainium, AMD) across clouds and handing back a single endpoint. You never pick the hardware, chase quotas, or rebuild your stack per provider. And if you run GPUs or other AI accelerators (an NVIDIA cluster, TPUs, a reserved fleet), you can plug your capacity into our rails and we'll bring the inference demand. Get started [here](https://openrelay.inc/).

P.S. sign up for our Luma page to be notified of our Launch Party!

<https://luma.com/s6x8cx5x>

\
<https://youtu.be/7uNhqcjBXJg>

## The Team

Hey guys! We're **Jaden and Prashant**, the founders of OpenRelay. We came at the same problem from opposite sides.

* Jaden built a half-megawatt data center at 20 from a warehouse shell, then joined Voltage Park early, where he ran virtualization and helped stand up HPC.
* Prashant built accelerator infra at AWS, where he ran custom model deployments and wrote custom kernels to squeeze out Trainium performance.

 

We kept seeing the same thing: there's more AI compute than ever, and you still can't reach it. We left our jobs to fix that.

## The Problem

Compute is everywhere; liquidity is nowhere. Accelerators are scattered across dozens of clouds, chip vendors, and operators, each behind its own quotas, drivers, contracts, and console. Teams that want to run inference can't reach the capacity, and the capacity can't reach them.

Running inference naively is easy; running it at scale is hard. Any operator can spin up a model on a box. Turning idle GPUs into a production endpoint (load balancing, isolation, autoscaling, failover, metering, billing) is a software platform most individual operators won't build. So capacity sits stranded behind their own front door, and developers either overpay for scarce reserved GPUs or hand-stitch a fragile multi-provider stack.

## Solution

We built one set of rails across all of it.

Send a workload (any container or model) and we schedule it onto the best-fit accelerator, attach a production endpoint, and scale it. We route to the cheapest accelerator that meets your latency and throughput targets, and we benchmark continuously. If the market can't beat renting yourself, we backstop with our own inference demand, so you’re never on the hook. 

You never pick the chip, cloud, or region; we handle routing, isolation, failover, metering, and billing across 4+ clouds and every major chip family. We're language- and framework-agnostic (no SDK lock-in), and you can drive everything from our CLI and REST API.

It's two-sided: if you run GPUs or other accelerators (a neocloud, a data center, a pay for an underutilized reserved fleet), you can connect that capacity to our rails and we'll bring the inference demand, turning hardware into a revenue-generating endpoint without building a platform yourself.

## Traction

We're **live in production**, generating 100 billion tokens a week across 22 physical locations across Europe, APAC, North America, and the Middle East running on 8 different accelerator SKUs.  

## Asks

We'd love to hear from you!

* **Run GPUs, or know someone who does?** This is who we most want to talk to: companies running their own nodes for inference, data centers, reserved fleets, even a crypto or mining cluster looking to move into AI. Plug your capacity into our rails and we'll bring the demand. Reach us at [founders@openrelay.inc](https://mailto:founders@openrelay.inc).
* **Shipping inference and tired of picking chips?** Bring a workload and we'll get you on the best available hardware today.
* **Feedback, intros, or just want to chat?** Book a call with us, or email [founders@openrelay.inc](mailto:founders@openrelay.inc) for anything else.

\
❌ **Problem**

While Jacob was serving in the U.S. Marine Corps, Typhoon Haiyan had just swept through the Philippines. Jacob and his unit were given a clear order: deliver life-saving supplies of medicine and food as soon as possible. Despite working around the clock, the effort was regularly blocked due to aircraft breaking down, flight-critical parts being out of inventory, and pilot fatigue.

Similarly, when building his previous startup, Matija’s team were given 24 hours’ notice to deliver a satellite propulsion system to the mission integrator. FedEx and UPS could not guarantee on-time delivery, forcing Matija to make a 23-hour trip to hand-deliver the flight hardware. He spent the flight back thinking that there has to be a better way.

It turned out that it wasn’t just us. Everyone from startups to the U.S. military, needs faster delivery. We saw an opportunity to create the fastest form of transportation in the world.

🚀 **Rockets are the answer**

We are building Rook, an autonomous rocket that delivers 250 kg of cargo up to 750 km away. That’s Okinawa to Taiwan in 15 minutes.

Rook launches from a standard 40-ft shipping container, flies through space, re-enters at hypersonic speeds and lands on unprepared surfaces, allowing it to launch and land anywhere on the planet. This opens up completely new commercial markets and military capabilities.

Rook can deliver swarms of autonomous unmanned systems to the battlefield, delivering a fully-autonomous 21st century D-Day effect for the U.S. and allies. The same Rook can deliver time-critical goods for manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, offshore oil and pharma, preventing downtime costs of up to $2M/hour.

🏆 **Traction**

* **Won a $1.25M DoW contract** from the US Air Force.
* **Completed our first tethered test** at the Oklahoma spaceport on a small-scale prototype
* **Successfully hot-fired our engine and igniter** built using hopOS, our AI-augmented secret sauce.
* **Successfully demonstrated drone deployment** from our rocket cargo vehicle.

🥷 **Team**

**Matija (CEO):** Previously founded porkchop (electric propulsion for small satellites) - launched on SpaceX Transporter-3, built a $400M+ sales pipeline, sold the IP. Led a 20+ person supersonic UAV team at Destinus and scaled Ukrainian loitering-munition production from 10 to 100+ units/month.

**Jacob (CTO):** US Marine Corps (MV-22 avionics) → SpaceX (Falcon 9/Heavy; built the OG booster refurb program) → Virgin Orbit (LauncherOne) → Masten (led systems integration & test on NASA's CLPS lunar lander) → SpinLaunch. A decade of making rockets fly on schedule.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112220&key=user_uploads/480112/8946bdbe-09b5-447f-8022-6233e2401800)

🙏 **Asks**

* **Intros to DoW customers and end-users.** Anyone with warm paths into the Navy, PACOM, or program offices working contested logistics - we want to talk.
* **Intros to commercial end-users.** Businesses with high downtime costs such as manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, offshore oil, pharma - all are right down our alley.
* **Payload partners.** We want to deploy your drones, interceptors, electronic warfare jammers and more! Reach out if you want to give your product the ability to teleport to the battlefield!

launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TLDR;**

* **Hebbian Robotics builds APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale**
* Our APIs enable data providers to get **on-demand signals and metrics** on the quality of their data, without managing infrastructure
* We help our customers evaluate data quality without training a robotics model

<https://youtu.be/ffvFNs3bjbs>

**Our Ask**

* Buyers want data they can trust. If you're selling egocentric or robot data, **Let’s Chat ([https://calendly.com/brandon-hebbianrobotics/30min](https://calendly.com/brandon-hebbianrobotics/30min)**) and we'll show you how quality signals and metrics help you sell more at higher prices
* **Check out Pareto ([https://pareto.hebbianrobotics.com/](https://pareto.hebbianrobotics.com/)),** an example of how our APIs can be used

### **Who We Are**

* We’re Brandon and Kingston, we've trained AI models for industrial cleaning robots and built production systems for camera fleets across the globe
* [**Brandon Ong**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/388120)'s previous AI startup was backed by Sequoia. He did research on AI for low resource languages that topped Stanford’s LLM benchmark, SEA-HELM, and dropped out of his joint PhD in Robotics at Columbia and NTU
* [**Kingston Kuan**](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/968709) spent years at Jane Street building systems that scaled to millions of messages per second. At Verkada, he worked on their core video surveillance platform that processed large scale multimodal data

### **The Problem**

* **High quality data is the bottleneck for unlocking the next frontier of intelligence in robotics**
* Buyers want **data they can trust** 
* Data providers don’t have the bandwidth to provide signals and metrics about the quality of their data when they are **focused on** **operational excellence**  
* This means that **model developers are forgoing model improvements due to a lack of high quality data**, impeding progress in robotics

### **Our Solution**

* APIs for searching and analyzing Physical AI data at scale that enables providers to get **on-demand signals and metrics on data quality**
* Buyers demanding per-collector hour limits? **Prove compliance while we stay ahead of the workarounds**
* Changed standard operating procedures for collection? **Monitor for quality drift and regression**
* Suspect duplicate samples? **Verify quickly with a single API call**
* Our APIs enable **evaluation of data quality without training a robotics model, fast iteration cycles for** high quality data collection, and unlock **model improvements** 

### **How to reach us**

* We want to support data providers who believe in collecting high quality data in an ethical way
* To get started, email [**brandon.ong@hebbianrobotics.com**](mailto:brandon.ong@hebbianrobotics.com)

launches.title: Earendil | Autonomous Air Defence
launches.tagline: Autonomous, combat-proven interceptors for defending against drone swarms.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We build autonomous interceptors that kill drones for less than the cost of the threat. Aeglos is in active operational use and has scored operational intercepts. The team has hundreds of confirmed combat intercepts. Looking for introductions to NATO-aligned air defence and C-UAS leads.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kZmj9NTDALo>

**The problem**:

Air defence economics are broken. A Patriot interceptor costs $3-7 million and is routinely used against $50,000 drones. Production rates of a few hundred units a year make these systems too scarce and too expensive for the volume of low-cost threats now in the air. They should be reserved for high-value targets.

Exactly like the Sherman tank versus the Tiger: it does not matter how good the system is if there are more threats than ammunition.

**What we do**:

Aeglos is a high-speed autonomous interceptor designed end-to-end for the mass drone problem: airframe, autonomy software, and operator model. The operator clicks launch, then selects the intercept in software. No stage of flight requires a pilot and no flying experience is needed. One operator can control up to 64 interceptors. Engagement cost stays below the price of the drone being destroyed.

Most C-UAS offerings are a single interceptor airframe. Operators still need skilled pilots, long training pipelines, and constant attention during the engagement. We built the complete system so any operator can achieve consistent intercepts without those requirements. The result is a system that can be fielded at the small-unit and critical-infrastructure level without the specialist crews or multi-million-dollar missiles that current layered air defence relies on.

Aeglos is operationally deployed, radar-agnostic, manufactured in Europe, and NDAA-compliant with no Chinese components.

**Why us:**

The entire team is ex-military with frontline Ukrainian experience, primarily in elite units and air defence. Collectively, we have hundreds of confirmed drone intercepts across multiple systems. We designed Aeglos from that experience - in the same contested Ukrainian airspace where most Western systems have not yet been stress-tested at scale.

[\@James Walton](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3723601): British Army and UAS expert with frontline Ukrainian experience who has previously run companies.

[\@Dan Komorny](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3723983):  A decade of experience in Drones and Security directly in Ukraine. Serial entrepreneur with multiple startups under his belt.

The Team: Commandos, Airborne, Special Forces and Air Defense veterans.

**Ask**

Introductions to air defence and C-UAS leads in NATO-aligned militaries, national acquisition teams, and operators responsible for protecting forward positions and critical infrastructure.

We are also open to partnerships with complementary companies.

launches.title: Florin: A full-stack insurance company with 0 underwriters
launches.tagline: Autonomously places hard-to-price risks in seconds
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Florin is a full-stack insurance company with 0 underwriters. Software takes a submission from a raw intake form to a bindable quote in seconds. Instead of matching a business to a class code, it verifies what the business actually does using satellite imagery, permits, public records and social media, then prices it by simulating tens of thousands of ways its next few years could go.

<https://youtu.be/BaXtkdP6_nc>

**What we do and why**

Insurance prices risk with class codes. An underwriter receives an application PDF, matches the business to a row in a rate table, and quotes off that row. This breaks in two ways. Applications are incomplete or wrong, so the price is built on bad inputs. And when a business does not fit any row, either because it is genuinely new (robotics, AI, autonomy) or because the table says the whole class or state is unprofitable, the answer is a declination. That is why carriers are exiting entire states and why a three-year-old industry can barely buy coverage at any price.

Florin replaces the table with evidence. It ingests the submission directly, no intake team. It builds its own picture of the business from the outside: aerial imagery of the actual premises, permits and public records, even the insured's social media, where it has caught operations that were never disclosed on the application. From that verified picture it runs simulations of the business's possible futures and produces a quote you can bind in seconds. No human touches the file.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109455&key=user_uploads/3776296/18477520-2b5a-4473-a727-92daf673768d)

**Team**

\- Shaurya Aggarwal built silicon on Google's next-generation TPU team

\- Amol Pant was on Tesla's supercomputer team, designed rovers for NASA, and was early at a Thiel backed robotics startup

\- Aydin Sorensen was early at Terrafirma, a construction robotics company that recently raised $115M

Shaurya and I have been best friends since middle school, and Aydin and I were roommates in college. We all lived together in Seattle for 2 years.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109455&key=user_uploads/3776296/4f7bfc6e-40f1-4d8d-9111-97c034db9729)

**Our asks**

1\. If your business has a risk that regular carriers and brokers keep declining or pricing absurdly, we want to hear from you. Email [shaurya@florin.inc](mailto:shaurya@florin.inc) or grab time at <https://calendly.com/shaurya-florin/30min>

2\. If you are a world-class quant, engineer, or underwriter and would rather build the pricing model than read files, we are hiring. Same email.

launches.body:
[ ](https://youtu.be/AbNIwYUdFBc)
Today we're introducing Locke, an applied AI company changing the way companies and governments work together. Our first focus: building an AI-native government affairs firm that helps companies monitor regulations, lobby policymakers, and win government contracts.

American governments spend over $10 trillion a year - and it's all up for grabs, reallocated annually through budgets, appropriations, and contracts. But while every other major market has been made accessible, government hasn't. Its front door is guarded by legacy government affairs firms that charge incumbent prices, and their customers get a fragmented product: one firm for the Hill, another for agencies, another for proposals and procurement, with no one accountable for the outcome.

Locke is building the front door government never had. We combine our AI agents with in-house lobbyists who own the entire path - from research to first meeting to funded contract. On the backend, our agents make the path faster than ever - analyzing legislation, tracking stakeholder engagement, and drafting complex contract proposals.

Since quietly launching six weeks ago, we've blown past a $500K annual revenue run-rate serving clients across defense, healthcare, GovTech, and more.

Locke was founded by Parth Badhwar, who came to this problem from both sides of the table: policy roles at the White House and Deloitte, then leading GTM at a startup that sold to dozens of government offices. The team is small, talent-dense, and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch.

Locke’s mission is bigger than replacing lobbying firms. It's a future where winning government support depends on what you make, not who you know.

It's day one in that mission.

Learn more at [locke.inc](http://locke.inc) or email [founders@locke.inc](mailto:founders@locke.inc).

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** SpaceFlow is an AI-native procurement services company for businesses that make, move and serve physical goods. We help procurement teams bring more spend under management, execute source-to-contract work and turn identified savings into realized savings without adding headcount or replacing existing systems.

<https://youtu.be/lS9pBj_LeV8>

### The problem

Procurement must absorb changing demand, supplier issues, and growing volume without increasing cost or risking continuity. Every existing option fails on the same axis:

* **Internal teams:** expertise and judgment, fixed capacity. It takes years to build and when someone leaves, the tacit knowledge that keeps operations running is lost.
* **SaaS:** automation and visibility without execution. The customer still staffs the operation, supervises it, handles exceptions, and owns the result.
* **Outsourcing:** capacity, expertise, and accountability, permanently labor-linked. More volume, suppliers, and locations require more service-delivery headcount.

The unmet need is operating capacity that **takes responsibility for completing the work** while becoming faster, more consistent, and more profitable as volume grows.

## The insight

* **Software can recommend actions; it cannot assume commercial authority.** The customer keeps execution, exceptions, and supplier outcomes. Whoever owns the exceptions owns the expertise, and expertise is the entire product in procurement.
* **Incumbents cannot follow.** Consulting and outsourcing firms store process knowledge in employees and grow revenue through staff hours. Automation directly cannibalizes that model.
* **The economics are breakable.** Traditional services sit below software economics: Accenture at Rule-of-22.6, Genpact at 24.1. An AI-native operator can reach **Rule-of-60**.

## What we built

**The proprietary platform SpaceFlow uses to operate procurement for customers.**

* A **process-mapping engine** converts interviews, SOPs, approval rules, and existing system configurations into executable workflows. A supply-chain consultancy estimates it cuts customer launch from **26 months to 4**, a 6.5x jump in deployment capacity.
* It **executes procurement end to end**, from demand and production planning through sourcing, contracting, purchase orders, exception resolution, and reconciliation, across the customer's own systems.
* Operating across companies in the same vertical turns cross-company experience into **proprietary process and supplier intelligence**, while pooled demand creates **group-purchasing power**: better execution, prices, resilience, and terms for every customer.
* The same platform **monitors service levels, resolves exceptions, and remains accountable** for completing the operation. Per-action autonomy limits, approval queues, and an immutable audit log make every task provable.

## Proof so far

* **Live:** $400M a year of supplier spend under management, zero systems migrated. Multiple six figure contracts signed.
* **Demand for delegation:** our first customer cancelled 3 planned procurement hires, the CSCO invested his own money, and two chains are signing to progressively outsource purchasing, one planning a procurement team 90% smaller by 2027.
* **Results:** 3x faster RFQ cycles, off-contract spend down 42% at one customer, $120K a year saved at another.

## Where this goes

SpaceFlow will replace legacy service providers across the physical economy. Traditional service firms grow by hiring; SpaceFlow grows output faster than headcount, targeting **$1B in revenue with headcount capped at 100**. 

## What's in it for you?

1. **You run a physical-goods company with $100M+ supplier spend:** send us 12 months of PO history and we'll map one lane and size the savings, free. [spaceflow.tech](http://spaceflow.tech) · [emre@spaceflow.tech](mailto:emre@spaceflow.tech)
2. **You know an operator like that:** intros are gold.

**Emre Isik (CEO)**  studied computer engineering at the University of Cambridge and dropped the master's to build SpaceFlow full time. Before that he researched embedded AI for motor control at UCLA's Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics, published a machine-learning paper on reasoning with small data, and trained with Turkey's international informatics olympiad reserve team at 15. 

**Ali Eren Aytekin (co-founder)** left engineering at Istanbul Technical University to build SpaceFlow.  He was Microsoft Imagine Cup EMEA runner-up for a genetic-signal classifier that hit 98.3% accuracy, and co-authored the published paper on low-data reasoning. That deal became the learning SpaceFlow grew from.

**Hakan Enes Aksu (co-founder)** left information engineering at Boğaziçi University to build SpaceFlow. He has been shipping commercial software since 16, when his Reddit ad-automation service earned $40K in revenue, and he later built a tender-matching engine that reads public tenders against a company's product catalog and sold it to a corporate customer for five figures. launches.title: SubVysion: Preventing $150B is wasted construction spending
launches.tagline: Autonomous rovers building the 'Google Maps' of subsurface infrastructure
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/5IY3vHEJ7J4>

Construction has a mapping problem. Of the $2.2T in annual US construction spending, $150B is wasted due to a lack of subsurface knowledge. All construction starts from the ground up, and more often than not, unexpected assets underneath the surface will hold a construction project back. Whether it's an unknown utility line, unexpected rock layer, or old foundation that wasn’t on any design map, the costs of delays from underground conflicts quickly add up. 

Take utility strikes, when an excavator hits an active utility line. For every dollar spent on the explicit repair cost of that utility line itself, the contractor loses an additional $30 per repair-dollar in project delays, insurance claims, idle work crews, and increased insurance premiums. For a hyperscale project such as data center construction, a single day of delay can cost the cloud-provider up to $14 million dollars for that single day.

In metropolitan areas, maps are incomplete at best and none create a unified picture of critical infrastructure, making excavation especially dangerous when natural gas or electric lines are broken.

Enter SubVysion. We’ve built a fleet of autonomous rovers carrying ground-penetrating radar and other sensors that create a centimeter-accurate map of subsurface infrastructure. Our hardware is the first and the best to map the entirety of US infrastructure. Using our rovers, we comprehensively map construction sites, city streets, and even larger indoor buildings, at 100x better granularity and 10x the speed (with a single rover) compared to our competitors. We process vast amounts of data using machine learning and agents, and output that data into an easy-to-understand 3D scene. 

Who are we? Maxwell Stone was an early ML engineer at Roboflow (YC S20), and Wenson Tang built the world’s smallest and cheapest LiDAR-capable drone for adverse environments. We both studied computer science at the University of Pennsylvania. Together, we’re building SubVysion to map the entirety of America’s subsurface infrastructure.

We’re currently on job sites in Philadelphia and Texas, helping our first market of utility contractors save hundreds of thousands of dollars every year. We’re soon to expand our mapping services to municipalities and energy providers as we scale up our rover fleet and capacity!

If you’re in the energy, infrastructure, or hyperscale construction world, we’d love to hear from you at [founders@subvysion.com](mailto:founders@subvysion.com)!

launches.title: Avoca Systems: AI-powered radiology scheduling and communications
launches.tagline: Automating radiology scheduling and patient communications
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We’re Max Shand and Campbell Mercer, co-founders of Avoca Systems.

TL;DR: Avoca automates patient scheduling and communications for radiology groups. Our radiology-specific AI handles calls, online scheduling, faxes and e-referrals, guiding patients from referral and booking through to results and follow-up. We’re already live across more than 250 clinics, including networks operating 150+ locations.

<https://youtu.be/ZU3Ebvs5Mk0>

**What it does**

Radiology scheduling is unusually complex. A valid appointment can depend on the modality, body region, contrast requirements, patient history, preparation instructions, equipment availability, staff qualifications and referring-provider details.

These rules are fragmented across legacy systems, spreadsheets and the tacit knowledge of experienced receptionists. Generic voice and scheduling tools struggle to bring them together.

Avoca integrates with a radiology network’s existing systems and turns its workflows and operational knowledge into one automation layer:

* **AI calls:** Answers inbound calls and runs outbound campaigns for bookings, rescheduling, cancellations, preparation questions and general enquiries.
* **Online scheduling:** Lets patients upload their referral, complete the necessary clinical and safety questions, and find an appropriate appointment in real time.
* **Fax and e-referral automation:** Ingests and interprets referrals, identifies missing information and contacts patients to complete their booking.
* **Operational intelligence:** Encodes each network’s booking rules, rosters, staff capabilities, preferences and tacit knowledge so Avoca can safely fill available scanner capacity.
* **Patient communications:** Guides patients through preparation, intake, reminders, results and follow-up using voice, text and email.

**Why this matters**

Up to 30% of calls into radiology centres go unanswered as patients wait on hold. Referrals arrive through phones, websites, faxes and electronic systems, leaving staff to manually interpret documents, contact patients and coordinate appointments across multiple systems.

At the same time, radiology providers face staff shortages, rising operating costs and reimbursement pressure. Missed calls and unprocessed referrals mean patients wait longer while valuable scanner capacity goes unfilled.

Avoca helps networks capture more patient demand, reduce administrative work and complete more scans using their existing clinics, equipment and clinical systems.

**Traction**

* Partnered with 250+ clinics, including several of Australia’s largest radiology networks
* Reduced call abandonment from approximately 30% to 2%
* Patient satisfaction averaging 4.6/5
* More than 80% booking conversion for eligible patient calls in major deployments
* Integrated with leading radiology and healthcare systems, including Visage, Karisma, Comrad, Epic, Oracle Health and eClinicalWorks
* Now expanding into the United States

**Why we’re building this**

I (Max) was the first employee at Afterpay and later founded and sold Serenade. Cam was previously a principal engineer at Honey Insurance and Macquarie. Across those experiences, we saw how much better an industry can operate when complex workflows are turned into simple, intuitive products.

Healthcare is a chaotic mess of work that falls between systems: calls that go unanswered, referrals that sit in fax queues and operational knowledge that exists only in the heads of experienced staff.

We started with radiology because the scheduling complexity is exceptionally high and the consolidation of radiology clinics into large groups allowed us to focus our GTM efforts on just a few influential stakeholders who acutely feel the pain we’re solving for.

**Our big** **ask**

* Any introduction to a radiology network or health system chief executive (CEO, CIO, COO, CDO, CRO - even the new brand of CAIO - Chief AI Officer) would be hugely appreciated. We’re new to the US and eager to meet leaders tackling the patient access and scheduling challenges we’re solving.

Finally, if you operate a radiology network - or know someone who does - we’d love to hear from you. Please reply here or reach us at [hello@avocasystems.com](mailto:hello@avocasystems.com).

launches.title: Tracer: Fable-level AI at 1/3 the cost using open-weight models
launches.tagline: Adaptive AI systems that combine open-weight models for better answers at lower cost.
launches.body:
Hi! I’m Adam, founder of Tracer.

We built **Echo**, an adaptive AI system built entirely from open-weight models. Instead of making you choose between models, Echo decides how much compute each request needs, which models should work on it, and how their answers should be combined.

**Across our current eval mix, Echo reaches Fable-level performance at roughly 1/3 the inference cost.**

Today, Echo is strongest on math, science, and the coding benchmarks we currently cover. Multilingual and broader knowledge performance still has room to improve, while longer-horizon coding and agentic evaluations are underway.

Echo is continuously updated as we expand the model pool and improve ensembling and cross-model coordination.

<https://youtu.be/hM0NypILdgw>

## **Why we built Echo**

There are now dozens of strong models, each with different strengths, weaknesses, and prices.

We started with a simple experiment: what if you had a perfect oracle that always knew which model would perform best for each request?

The oracle was substantially stronger than any individual model in the pool.

Echo is our attempt to recover that advantage without knowing the answer beforehand.

Instead of picking one model for everything, Echo goes beyond routing and dynamically allocates compute across a pool of open-weight models behind a single interface.

## **The result**

We evaluate Echo against frontier models across reasoning, math, coding, multilingual and other benchmarks.

We measure both **quality and the actual model inference cost used to produce the answers.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108361&key=user_uploads/1217984/867cc6aa-16b8-4330-b497-c33d78e62b24)

On MATH-500, Echo reached **98.6% at $4.58**, compared with Claude Fable at **99.8% at $12.64**.

On LiveCodeBench, Echo reached **92.8% at $5.35**, compared with Claude Fable at **92.0% at $8.71**.

These results show where Echo is already strongest. LiveCodeBench is encouraging, but it does not capture the full difficulty of repository-level and agentic coding. We are currently running longer-horizon evaluations where Echo must plan, use tools, modify code, and recover from errors across multiple steps.

Those results are visible in the Eval Observatory and are active areas of improvement.

We publish the underlying evaluations, including individual answers, costs, wins, and losses:

**→[ Explore the Echo Eval Observatory](https://echo.tracerml.ai/eval?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**

## **From open source to Echo**

We first explored this idea through Tracer's open-source work: learning from real AI workloads where expensive model calls are actually necessary and where cheaper paths are enough.

The project has now crossed **1,000 GitHub stars**, with developers using and experimenting with the approach in their own AI pipelines.

Echo is the next step. Instead of optimizing individual calls with a routing layer, we're building one adaptive system that decides how intelligence should be allocated end to end.

**→ [GitHub](http://github.com/adrida/tracer)**

## **Every company’s AI traffic has a shape**

Our public evaluations test Echo across a broad mix of general tasks. Production workloads are different.

Every company has its own traffic distribution and quality requirements. Some requests genuinely need expensive frontier-level intelligence. Many don’t.

For teams that work with us, Echo can be configured to learn the structure of their workload and identify where expensive intelligence is useful and where cheaper paths are enough.

**Public Echo does not train on users’ private traces. Workload-specific learning is enabled only for teams that explicitly work with Tracer to configure it.**

We set up this optimization with each team around its workload, quality bar, and data requirements.

The goal is simple: **an AI system that continuously learns how to spend the minimum amount of inference required to maintain the quality you need.**

That means **\~3x cheaper is not necessarily the ceiling for a real production workload.**

## **Try Echo now**

Echo is publicly available through a chat UI and an **OpenAI-compatible API**.

You can try it directly, connect an existing application by changing the base URL, or plug Echo into OpenCode and other agent harnesses.

Echo is continuously updated as we improve model selection and ensembling.

**→[ Try Echo now](https://echo.tracerml.ai)**

## **We’re looking for teams with large inference workloads**

If your company is running meaningful LLM inference in production, we’d like to test Echo against your workload.

We’ll map the quality-cost frontier on your traffic and determine how much of your inference actually requires expensive intelligence.

Teams can then work with us to activate private, workload-specific optimization.

→ [**Optimize Echo for your workload**](https://cal.com/adam-rida-tracer/tracer-first-call)

## **About Tracer**

I’m **Adam Rida**, founder of Tracer. I was previously a PhD candidate at **Sorbonne University/CNRS**, where I conducted and published research in ML interpretability. Before founding Tracer, I built applied ML systems across finance, insurance, and supply chain, then grew [DeepRecall](http://deeprecall.io/) to \~**€100k ARR as a solo founder in less than 3 months**.

I’ve spent most of my career studying how models make decisions and turning that research into production systems.

launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋, we're Jonathan and Guy, founders of OneCLI.**\
\
🏆 TL;DR**

OneCLI is an open source agent harness for teams. Each employee gets their own sandboxed pro assistant agent, connected to their GitHub, Gmail, Notion, Dropbox, or CRM right from the chat/Slack, while the whole workspace runs under one policy your admins control. \
\
Agents never hold real secrets: the credential is injected at the network layer, per request, after the call is authorized. You can't steal what isn't there.

**Launch Video**\
<https://youtu.be/LUAMdqbl_Rw>

🚧 **The Problem**

Lately, autonomous agents have arrived and shown up everywhere. Tools like OpenClaw and Hermes have become extremely popular and been adopted by open source communities, mostly by individuals. Companies, however, have been left behind: they need integration with their identity providers to enable easy provisioning of agents on behalf of an employee's identity, with least-privilege access.

Those tools have fundamental flaws. Security fundamentals, like secret handling and organization-level control, are missing by default. So companies must choose between weak agents or making them powerful but risky.

✅ **What OneCLI Does**

OneCLI gives teams the whole harness, open source and self-hosted, so agents can be powerful and safe at once:

* **Sandboxed agent per employee:** each agent runs isolated with its own memory, skills, and permissions.
* **Secrets injected at the network layer:** the agent gets a placeholder, the gateway swaps in the real credential per request, after the call is authorized. Credentials never enter the agent's context, memory, or logs.
* **Policy enforced outside the model:** admins define org-wide policy. Block endpoints and scope access per agent.
* **Human-in-the-loop where it counts:** sensitive actions (send the email, delete the Linear ticket, empty the S3 bucket) wait for deterministic approval in the chat.
* **Full identity trail:** every agent is bound to an employee, every call logged with who it acted for and which policy allowed it.

🚀 **Team**

We've spent our careers in security. Jonathan built zero trust network access at Axis Security (acquired by HPE). The core ZTNA idea is that you never trust the client and enforce access outside it, at the network layer. Guy was the first employee at Argon (AppSec company acquired by Aqua Security), protecting client codebases. Agents need exactly the treatment ZTNA gives humans, so we built it.
